                ast_transform.py # Python AST → Tack IR
                lowering/        # KernelTransformer's parts: loops, arrays, vectors, inlining, ...
                template_rewrite.py  # AST pre-pass for template parameters
                ir.py            # IR node definitions (30+ node types)
                ir_traversal.py  # walk_ir, transform_ir, clone_ir
                ir_names.py      # Binding names, fresh_name
                ir_verify.py     # verify_ir: invariants at each pass boundary
                ir_bounds.py     # Debug mode's bounds checks: sites, access guards
                ir_resolve.py    # Replace IRDimSize with constants
                ir_optimize.py   # conservative copy propagation
                ir_type_annotate.py  # Annotate expressions with dtype
                ir_pack_scalars.py   # Group scalar params into array buffers
                type_inference.py    # Annotate IR params from actual args
                atomic_support.py    # Atomic target and dtype checks
                workgroup_support.py, workgroup_participation.py  # Workgroup checks
                inspect_kernel.py    # tack.inspect()
                types.py         # ScalarType: f32, i32, i64, etc.
                array.py         # Array, Texture3D
                dlpack.py        # DLPack import/export
            codegen/             # IR → target code
                identifiers.py   # Collision-free target identifiers
                llvm_gen.py      # → LLVM IR (for CPU backend)
                msl_gen.py       # → Metal Shading Language
                cuda_gen.py      # → CUDA C
                hip_gen.py       # → HIP C (extends cuda_gen)
                opencl_gen.py    # → OpenCL C (extends cuda_gen)
                bounds.py        # Debug mode's bounds-check helper (C family)
            runtime/             # Dispatch and device management
                backend.py       # Backend base class: declared capabilities
                kernel_utils.py  # resolve_variant(), the fast path, variant keys, kernel caches
                disk_cache.py    # Lowered IR and compiled variants on disk (tack.cache)
                debug_bounds.py  # Debug mode's hidden arguments and IndexError
                dispatch.py      # devices, the default device, launch placement, tack.sync()
                cpu.py           # CPU backend (llvmlite JIT, threading policy)
                cpu_pool.py      # CPU thread pool, JIT-compiled from LLVM IR
                metal.py         # Metal backend (pyobjc)
                cuda_backend.py  # CUDA backend (cuda-python)
                hip_backend.py   # HIP backend (hip-python)
                level_zero_backend.py # Level Zero backend (ctypes)
            cache.py             # tack.cache: settings, MPI bundles, python -m tack.cache
            algorithms/          # General-purpose parallel primitives
                scan.py          # Parallel prefix sum (exclusive/inclusive)
                copy.py          # copy, fill_value
                stats.py         # Statistics and histograms

    tack-vis/                     # Scientific visualization algorithms
        src/tack/
            dataset/             # Datasets, spaces, views and their algorithms
                algorithms/      # contour, clip, threshold, gradients, ... (one per file)
            interop/             # External framework interop
                vtk.py           # VTK ↔ Tack zero-copy exchange

Both packages share the tack namespace via pkgutil.extend_path; tack-vis depends on tack-core. The path tracer that was tack-rendering is archived under archive/tack-rendering until the dataset API settles.

docs.title: Code Size
docs.text:
tack-core is about 25,100 lines of Python, including docstrings and comments (wc -l over packages/tack-core/src, October 2026); tack-vis adds about 12,400:

Directory Lines Role lang/ ~8,800 Frontend: validation, AST transform, IR, passes, verification codegen/ ~4,500 5 code generators and shared helpers runtime/ ~10,200 5 backend runtimes, variant resolution, disk cache, CPU threading and pool

No C/C++ code. No build step. Everything is pure Python with JIT compilation at runtime.

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text:
The decisions below are the structural ones. The principles behind them, and the correctness rules the compiler follows, are in Design Principles.

Pure Python throughout. Unlike Taichi (which has a C++ core with pybind11 bindings), Tack implements the entire pipeline in Python. This makes the codebase easy to read, modify, and debug. Kernels run as native code generated by LLVM or the vendor compiler, not through Python; the Python cost is in compilation, paid once per compiled variant, and in per-call dispatch overhead.

Separate IR from codegen. The IR is a simple tree of Python objects (not strings, not LLVM objects). Each codegen backend walks the same IR and emits its own output format. This makes adding a new backend straightforward.

AST-level function inlining. @tack.func calls are inlined by copy-and-rename at the AST level: during IR transformation, each call site lowers a renamed copy of the callee's validated AST. This avoids needing function call support in the IR or any backend.

Template expansion at AST level. @tack.device_class objects are resolved by rewriting the kernel AST before IR transformation. Class-level scalar attributes become constants, instance scalar attributes and array attributes become parameters, and method calls become inlined function bodies. The IR and codegens never see templates.

Non-owning pointer interop. tack.array_from_ptr() wraps external device memory without allocation or copy. Each backend implements wrap_ptr() so that the wrapped memory is never freed by Tack (the CUDA, HIP and Level Zero buffers carry an _owned = False flag). Such arrays are read-only by default, with an explicit writable opt-in. The flag is checked by host-side Array methods and, for kernels, at dispatch: a read-only array bound to a parameter the kernel may store to is refused before the launch. This enables interop with in-situ frameworks (Catalyst), GPU libraries (pycuda, cupy), and cross-library buffer sharing. See Interoperability.

docs.title: AST Transform
docs.text:
The AST transformer (ast_transform.py) converts a Python function's AST into Tack IR. It is the heart of the frontend.

KernelTransformer is one class assembled from mixins, one module each in lang/lowering/, grouped by job. Each sets up the state it owns in its own _init_... method and reaches the others through self:

Module Mixin What it lowers ast_transform.py KernelTransformer the visit_* walk (assignment, calls, subscripts, names, operators) and the expression machinery the others use (_visit_expression, _visit_ordered, _capture_value, _source_error) lowering/loops.py Loops the parallel loop, ndindex, sequential loops, while lowering/arrays.py ArrayAccess indexing and linearization, vector and structure-of-arrays elements lowering/vectors.py VectorValues vector and matrix values, components, methods, scalarized assignment lowering/inlining.py Inlining @tack.func calls, return restructuring, renaming lowering/local_arrays.py LocalArrays tack.shared, tack.local_array lowering/checks.py LoweringChecks checks on emitted IR: effects outside the parallel loop, values left in scalar positions, unbound names lowering/bounds.py BoundsChecks debug mode's IRBoundsCheck (_checked) lowering/values.py — VectorValue and TupleValue

docs.title: Entry Point
docs.text:
# In kernel.py, when get_ir() is called:
from tack.lang.ast_transform import transform_kernel
ir_module = transform_kernel(ast_tree, vector_arrays=..., texture_arrays=...,
                             python_func=kernel.func, template_funcs=...)

transform_kernel creates a KernelTransformer (an ast.NodeVisitor) and visits the module. The result is an IRModule containing one IRFunction.

call_bindings.py supplies static device-call resolution from the defining Python callable and transformation-local template method map. AST-only callers can supply an explicit bindings dictionary. Bare kernel intrinsics remain available without a Python import; device functions require a bound Func object. No global function-name registry is consulted.

Original kernel source is validated by source_validation.py before transformation. Original @tack.func bodies are also validated before return restructuring or variable renaming, so unreachable unsupported syntax cannot disappear. Unsupported constructs raise UnsupportedSyntaxError, a NotImplementedError subclass, with the function name, construct, and line/column in captured, dedented source. The transformer's default visitor also rejects unknown nodes. Docstrings and pass are explicit no-ops; decorators and annotations are host metadata.

docs.title: KernelTransformer State
docs.text:
The transformer tracks several pieces of state:

  • _loop_depth — 0 at the top level. The for i in range(...) at depth 0 becomes IRParallelFor; nested loops become IRSequentialFor.
  • _in_parallel_loop, _parallel_loop_seen and _kernel_body — enforce the one-loop rule and the outside-the-loop rule. _visit_parallel_for accepts one for statement directly in the kernel body; a second one, or one inside a top-level if or while, raises UnsupportedSyntaxError, as does a kernel with none. While _in_parallel_loop is false, _visit_body passes each lowered statement to _check_outside_parallel_loop, which rejects an array store, atomic, barrier, block reduction or print (_effect_name) at the statement's source position. It runs on the lowered IR so effects from inlined device functions and template methods are seen; nested bodies are visited first, so the reported position is the innermost one.
  • _inline_counter — monotonic counter for generating unique variable names during @tack.func inlining.
  • _vector_vars — tracks which local variables are vectors or matrices (name → component count). _matrix_vars holds (rows, columns) for the ones that are matrices. _bind_vector sets both and _variable_value reads them, so use those rather than the dicts.
  • _vector_arrays — tracks which parameters are vector arrays (for scalarization), with _matrix_arrays beside it. The runtime passes a matrix array's entry as a (rows, columns) tuple; the constructor splits it. _array_shape(name) gives an element's shape either way.
  • _texture_arrays — tracks which parameters are textures (for tex.sample()).
  • _texture_origin — maps renamed texture names back to original parameter names (needed when textures pass through @tack.func inlining).
  • _shared_vars — names of tack.shared() and tack.local_array() variables (affects indexing — these are arrays, not scalars).
  • _pre_stmts — statements generated by expression-level inlining that must execute at the expression's original position. Reentrant body traversal preserves the surrounding expression's pending statements.

docs.title: Expression Evaluation
docs.text:
_visit_expression isolates an expression's value and prerequisite statements. _visit_ordered visits operands left to right and materializes earlier loads before a later operand's inlined effects. Boolean and conditional expressions put those prerequisite statements inside IRIf guards, rather than moving them before the guard. Inlined while conditions are lowered into an always-entered loop with condition statements and a guarded break, so continue reevaluates the condition.

Augmented stores reuse a single evaluated address and retain the old load before right-hand-side effects. Sequential range bounds and steps are captured before the loop. CPU codegen also short-circuits pure IRBoolOp and IRIfExp expressions with branches and phi joins. Comparisons and logical expressions yield normalized i32 values 0/1.

See the kernel language contract for the supported subset and numerical decisions still open.

docs.title: Parallel For
docs.text:
At loop depth 0, for i in range(n) becomes:

IRParallelFor(var="i", start=IRConstant(0), end=IRName("n"), body=[...])

With range(start, end, step), Tack transforms the step into a contiguous-index parallel loop with a decomposition assignment:

# for i in range(0, 100, 3) becomes:
# for __step_idx__ in range(0, ceil(100/3)):
#     i = 0 + __step_idx__ * 3

docs.title: Sequential For
docs.text: At loop depth > 0, for loops become IRSequentialFor. The step attribute is preserved (used by codegens for the C for-loop increment). Bounds and steps are captured once before entry. Loops inside while are also sequential. Literal zero and negative steps are rejected; dynamic steps must be positive. A break from the outer parallel loop is rejected, while nested sequential break and both forms of continue are supported.

docs.title: ndindex
docs.text:
A top-level for i, j in tack.ndindex(w, h) (or three dimensions) becomes one IRParallelFor that keeps its dimensions: dims names one index variable per dimension, slowest first, and extents holds their sizes as host-evaluated expressions, like the loop's end (their product). The body starts with i = __nd_0__ and j = __nd_1__ (plus a range's start, for a (start, end) pair), and nothing divides: each backend binds the dimension variables from a launch of the same shape (see lang/parallel_dims.py).

A kernel that uses workgroup primitives, a loop of four or more dimensions, and an ndindex nested inside the parallel loop keep the flat form, a loop over the product whose body recovers the indices:

j = __idx__ % h
i = __idx__ // h

docs.title: Function Call Dispatch
docs.text:
visit_Call is the most complex method. It handles:

  1. Math builtins (sqrt, sin, etc.) → IRCall
  2. tack.atomic_add/min/max → IRAtomicOp
  3. tack.shared(dtype, size) → IRSharedAlloc
  4. tack.local_array(dtype, size) → IRLocalAlloc
  5. tack.barrier() → IRBarrier
  6. tack.thread_id() → IRThreadId
  7. print(...) → IRPrint
  8. int(), float() → IRCast
  9. tex.sample(u, v, w) → IRTextureSample
  10. Vector and matrix methods (.normalized(), .dot(), .cross(), .sum(), .transpose(), .inverse(), ...) → scalarized ops, in _emit_vector_method and _emit_matrix_method
  11. tack.vec2/vec3/vec4(...) → a VectorValue (_visit_vector_construct); tack.mat2/mat3/mat4(...), tack.mat(row, ...), tack.identity(n) → a VectorValue with a two-dimensional shape (_visit_matrix_construct, _visit_matrix_identity)
  12. @tack.func calls → inlined via _inline_func_call

A name that the function does not bind is resolved through CallBindings before anything else in visit_Name and visit_Attribute: one bound to a tack.constant lowers to an IRConstant (under an IRCast when the constant is typed), and math.pi/e/tau likewise.

docs.title: Assignment Handling
docs.text:
visit_Assign checks for several special forms before falling through to a plain IRAssign:

  1. Shared/local allocation: smem = tack.shared(...), arr = tack.local_array(...)
  2. Vector construction: v = tack.vec3(a, b, c) (_try_parse_vector_construct)
  3. Multi-dimensional array store: array[i, j] = val → linearized index
  4. Tuple unpacking: a, b = func() → multiple IRAssign nodes. A target that is a subscript or a component gets its value through a temporary and is stored at its own position among the targets (_store_unpacked), after the whole right side has been evaluated.
  5. Components: v[c] = x, v.x = x, vf[i][c] = x, m[i, j] = x (_component_target turns the named forms into subscripts; _component_selector and _matrix_selector resolve the index)

docs.title: Vector Scalarization
docs.text:
Vector operations are expanded at the AST level. A vector variable v with 3 components becomes 3 scalar variables v__0, v__1, v__2. Binary ops on vectors produce component-wise IR nodes:

# v = a + b  (where a, b are 3-vectors) becomes:
v__0 = a__0 + b__0
v__1 = a__1 + b__1
v__2 = a__2 + b__2

Array loads/stores are similarly scalarized: v = array[i] loads array[i*3], array[i*3+1], array[i*3+2].

During lowering a vector or matrix is a VectorValue: a list of component expressions with a shape, (n,) or (rows, columns). A source tuple (the indices of f[i, j], several results of a device function) is a TupleValue. Both are lists so that code mapping over components stays plain; the classes exist to tell them apart from each other and from a list of statements. Three rules follow from the representation:

  • Map, do not pass through. An operation given a VectorValue has to return one. _elementwise does that for anything componentwise, checks that the operands' shapes agree, and keeps the shape; use _like when building a result by hand.
  • Neither class may reach the IR. _check_single_values scans each lowered statement once and raises UnsupportedSyntaxError at the statement's position for one left in a scalar position. Without it the verifier reports "expected expr node" with a tree path.
  • Assignment is per component, but the right side is one value. _settle_components evaluates into a temporary any component that could observe an earlier component's write: a read of an earlier target component for a variable, any array load for an array element, since arrays may share storage.

Operations that use each component several times (@, determinant, inverse, outer_product) capture their operands into temporaries first, or the expression tree grows with every product in a chain.

docs.title: IR Design
docs.text: The Tack IR (ir.py) is a tree of Python objects with plain attributes. ir_traversal.py declares structural children explicitly and provides shared walks and rewrites. ir_verify.py checks invariants at compilation boundaries. Control-flow-sensitive passes retain their own ordered walks.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
IRModule
  └── functions: list[IRFunction]
        ├── name: str
        ├── params: list[IRParam]   (name, type_annotation, _is_array, etc.)
        └── body: list[IRNode]      (statements)

docs.title: Loops and Control Flow
docs.text: Node Description IRParallelFor Outermost loop → GPU thread dispatch. Has var, start, end, body. IRSequentialFor Inner loop → C for-loop. Has var, start, end, step, body. IRWhile While loop. Has condition, body. IRIf Conditional. Has condition, then_body, else_body. IRBreak Break out of loop. IRContinue Continue to next iteration. IRReturn Legacy return node; rejected in kernel IR. Device returns are eliminated during inlining.

docs.title: Expressions
docs.text: Node Description IRBinOp Binary operation: left op right (op is +, -, *, /, //, %, **). IRUnaryOp Unary: -x, not x. IRCompare Comparison: left op right (op is <, <=, >, >=, ==, !=). IRBoolOp Boolean: a and b, a or b. IRIfExp Ternary: a if cond else b. IRCall Math builtin call: sqrt(x), sin(x), etc. IRCast Type cast: int(x), float(x), tack.f64(x), etc. dtype is a ScalarType. IRConstant Literal: 42, 3.14. dtype is a ScalarType, set by type annotation pass. IRName Variable reference. IRAttribute Attribute access: obj.attr (used for array.shape).

docs.title: Array Operations
docs.text: Node Description IRArrayLoad Read: array[index]. array is an IRName, index is any expression. IRArrayStore Write: array[index] = value. IRAtomicOp Atomic: atomic_add(array, index, value). IRDimSize Dimension query: array.shape[dim] (resolved to constant before codegen). IRTextureSample Texture read: tex.sample(u, v, w). Stores array_name, coords, shape.

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Lowering emits these only for a kernel lowered with debug=True (tack.set_debug(True) or TACK_DEBUG=1); see lang/ir_bounds.py.

Node Description IRBoundsCheck An access's index: flat as i64 when each of indices lies in [0, extent) of the extent beside it, otherwise -1, after recording the first violation (site, an index into the function's bounds_sites) in the hidden errors array. IRArrayExtent An array parameter's extent at run time: LEADING (dimension 0), ELEMENTS (a flat index's bound) or STORAGE (scalar components). Never compiled in: ir_resolve turns it into a load from the hidden extents array, so checking does not specialize on lengths.

docs.title: GPU Primitives
docs.text: Node Description IRSharedAlloc Allocate threadgroup memory: tack.shared(dtype, size) or tack.shared_like(array, size). Has optional array_name for shared_like (resolved in ir_resolve). IRLocalAlloc Allocate per-thread memory: tack.local_array(dtype, size) or tack.local_array_like(array, size). Has optional array_name for local_array_like (resolved in ir_resolve). IRBarrier Threadgroup sync: tack.barrier(). IRThreadId Local thread index: tack.thread_id().

docs.title: Other
docs.text: Node Description IRAssign Assignment: target = value. After type annotation, has _resolved_type. IRPrint Debug print (emits printf on CPU/CUDA/HIP, no-op on Metal).

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
IR nodes are annotated by various passes:

  • IRParam.type_annotation — ScalarType (f32, i32, etc.), set by type inference.
  • IRParam._is_array — True for array/texture params, False for scalars.
  • IRParam._is_texture — True for Texture3D params.
  • IRParam._texture_shape — (W, H, D) tuple for texture params.
  • IRAssign._resolved_type — ScalarType or None, set by type annotation pass.
  • Expression dtype — ScalarType on all expression nodes (IRBinOp, IRArrayLoad, IRCall, IRCast, etc.), set by the type annotation pass. Codegens read this instead of reimplementing type inference.
  • IRTextureSample.shape — (W, H, D), set by IR resolve.
  • IRFunction.bounds_sites — debug mode only: one ir_bounds.BoundsSite per checked access (kernel or device function, file, line, source text), set by lowering and read by debug_bounds to word the IndexError. The function also gains two hidden array parameters, __tack_errors__ and __tack_extents__, after the kernel's own.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
• The IR has exactly one IRParallelFor at the top level (the thread dispatch loop).
  • Sequential loops appear only inside the parallel loop's body.
  • IRDimSize nodes are resolved to IRConstant before codegen, except in the host-evaluated parallel loop end, which remains dynamic. IRArrayExtent nodes are resolved to loads of the hidden extents array.
  • After type inference, every IRParam has type_annotation and _is_array.
  • After scalar packing, no scalar params remain (GPU backends only).

verify_ir(function, stage) enforces structural, loop-target, binding, resolution, parameter, and annotation checks. A failed check raises IRVerificationError with the kernel, stage, node kind, and tree path. See IR Passes for the stages and their limits.

docs.title: Shared Traversal
docs.text:
CHILD_FIELDS records each node's child attributes and their roles: expressions, optional expressions, statement lists, parameter lists, and function lists. walk_ir(root) yields nodes in preorder; transform_ir(root, rewrite) rewrites children before applying rewrite(node). Rewrites mutate the tree in place and preserve metadata on unchanged nodes. A replacement's children are not visited again. Repeated references to a node are visited at each occurrence; cycles and unregistered node kinds raise errors. copy_nodes=True copies each occurrence before rewriting it, preserving metadata while allowing statement-specific substitutions. Copy propagation uses this mode so a later rewrite cannot alter an earlier shared expression.

Only structural children are followed. Types, texture extents, cached shape dependencies, and debug/source metadata do not become accidental subtrees. Resolution, scalar packing, copy substitution, and shape-dependency queries use this schema. Analyses that depend on statement order or control-flow context must still implement that logic explicitly.

docs.title: IR Passes
docs.text: Tack runs several IR passes between AST transformation and codegen. Each pass inspects the IR tree; transformation passes mutate a private copy.

docs.title: Pass Order
docs.text:
1. ir_resolve       — Replace compiled-in dimensions, set texture shapes, resolve array-like dtypes
2. type_inference   — Annotate params with types from actual arguments
3. check_dispatch_types — Validate array dtypes against backend capabilities
4. scalar localization — Give scalar params and outer locals the loop assigns per-iteration local storage
5. workgroup participation — Prove the supported collective control-flow domain (GPU only)
6. ir_optimize      — Conservative copy propagation
7. ir_pack_scalars  — Group scalar params into array buffers (GPU only)
8. ir_type_annotate — Annotate scalar expressions and assignment storage types
9. ir_bounds.guard_accesses — Skip accesses whose checked index is negative (debug mode only, at the end of 8)

resolve_variant() runs the common passes only for a new compiled variant, one neither in the backend's cache nor in the disk cache; a variant read from disk carries its post-pass IR and runs none of them. GPU packing works on a separate copy so launch-range resolution retains the original parameter names. CPU skips packing. tack.inspect() also performs the backend's texture decision, check_dispatch_types, scalar localization and verification; its source preparation annotates once before packing and again afterwards on GPU.

docs.title: Copying and Template Ownership (ir_traversal.py)
docs.text:
Cached templates remain pristine. Variant preparation, assigned-scalar localization, GPU packing and inspection use clone_ir() for their working copies. This specializes Python deep copying for registered plain IR nodes and list/dict containers. It copies every node attribute, including pass annotations and metadata, rather than only structural children. One memo preserves aliases and cycles across the entire graph, while mutable state is independent of the original. ScalarType objects retain their identity; other metadata uses Python's deepcopy protocol. Structural cycles remain invalid and are rejected by the verifier.

Cache hits do not clone IR. All pass-boundary checks below remain in place. Adding a registered node with slots or a custom copying protocol requires revisiting the cloning fast path; the registered nodes currently use plain attribute dictionaries. Clone regression tests cover every registered kind, metadata ownership and cached dispatch.

uv run --no-sync python benchmarks/ir_clone.py --output /tmp/ir-clone.json compares generic copying and specialized cloning on the pristine and typed CPU IR of dataset filters: it runs a contour and a clip of VTK's wavelet once, clears the variant cache, captures their kernels on a second run and alternates copy methods on each graph. It reports median and individual samples plus unique-node and occurrence counts. Setup, compilation and filtering are outside those timings; this measures copying cost, not total cold compilation or GPU performance.

docs.title: Verification (ir_verify.py)
docs.text:
The production pipeline calls verify_ir() at these boundaries:

Stage Checks added to structural and loop checks lowered Valid statement/expression roles, known node kinds/operators, numeric constants, unique parameters, existing bindings, exactly one normalized top-level parallel loop, no store, atomic, block reduction, barrier or print outside it, and consistent break/continue targets resolved No dimensions or attributes in generated expressions; allocation dtypes and texture extents resolved inferred Scalar parameter types and array/scalar categories present; array accesses name array parameters or allocated arrays, including inlined pointer copies localized Recheck the invariants after assigned scalar parameters and outer locals become per-iteration locals optimized Recheck the invariants after copy propagation packed Recheck the invariants and ensure no scalar parameters remain on GPU typed Every generated scalar expression and scalar assignment has a type; logical results have i32 dtype

The parallel loop end is evaluated by the host on each dispatch. Dimension queries in that expression remain legal and do not force specialization on a flat array's length. Array references are pointers and do not require a scalar expression dtype.

IRVerificationError reports the kernel, stage, node kind, and structural path. Failed variants never reach compilation or enter the compiled cache. Template verification runs before caching lowered IR; the remaining checks run on variant misses. Warm dispatch performs no verification walks, and neither does an entry read from the disk cache, which was verified when it was built. Direct low-level pass/codegen calls used to build IR fragments must invoke the verifier themselves when they need the full kernel contract.

These checks establish tree and annotation invariants. Binding checks test whether a name exists anywhere in the function, not whether every path initializes it before a read. They do not prove bounds safety, alias safety of future optimizations, absence of races, barrier uniformity, or numerical equivalence. Differential tests and backend hardware validation remain necessary.

docs.title: IR Resolve (ir_resolve.py)
docs.text:
Replaces IRDimSize(array_name, dim) with IRConstant(shape[dim]) using the actual array shapes passed at call time. Also sets IRTextureSample.shape from the Texture3D object. In debug mode it turns each IRArrayExtent into a load from the hidden __tack_extents__ array (three i64 extents per parameter, written by dispatch), so a debug kernel does not specialize on the lengths it checks.

This pass runs early because subsequent passes (optimization, codegen) need concrete sizes.

docs.title: Type Inference (type_inference.py, 81 lines)
docs.text:
Annotates each IRParam with: - type_annotation — a ScalarType (f32, i32, i64, etc.) - _is_array — True if the argument is an Array or Texture3D - _is_texture — True if the argument is a Texture3D

Type rules: - Array → dtype of the array - Texture3D → dtype of the underlying array (always f32; tack.texture3d() rejects others) - Python float or np.floating → f32 by default; auto-promotes to f64 if any array argument uses f64 - Python int or np.integer → i32 if it fits, else i64, else u64

docs.title: Dispatch-Time Type Checking (type_inference.py)
docs.text:
check_dispatch_types() validates that all array argument dtypes are supported by the target backend. This runs after type inference when building a new compiled variant.

Each backend defines its supported dtypes (e.g., Metal excludes f64). Unsupported dtypes produce a clear TypeError naming the kernel, parameter, dtype, and backend.

docs.title: Workgroup Participation (workgroup_participation.py)
docs.text:
GPU variant construction checks collective control flow after scalar localization, before optimization and scalar packing. A structured uniformity analysis follows assignments and branch joins, with monotone loop fixed points for carried values and lane-dependent exits. It rejects unproven participation before code generation and returns the full-256-lane launch requirement, cached on KernelVariant. Cached dispatch checks logical counts without repeating this pass. Public inspection follows the same boundary; direct GPU generation checks mutable IR afresh.

Ordinary memory/texture loads are varying. Scalar arguments and immutable scalar packs are uniform; pack_scalars marks generated parameters with _is_scalar_pack so packed codegen retains that fact. Shape metadata and collective results are uniform too. Conditional/short-circuit reductions and while-condition reductions are restricted where codegen cannot preserve evaluation. See the language contract and test_workgroup_participation.py. This does not replace structural verification or prove race freedom.

docs.title: IR Optimize (ir_optimize.py)
docs.text:
Copy propagation replaces subsequent uses of a single-assignment copy with its source when the source is never rebound in the containing block. Assignment counts include nested control flow, loop-variable bindings, and local/shared array bindings. Assignments remain in place, reads before the assignment are unchanged, and rewritten sequential loops retain their step.

This is useful after @tack.func inlining, which creates assignments such as __func_x_0__ = x. Array aliases can then use the original parameter: a = x followed by a[i] becomes x[i].

Tack's custom loop-invariant code motion and common subexpression elimination are disabled. An invariant address does not imply an invariant loaded value, and hoisting an assignment can change a zero-trip loop's behavior. Loads must also account for stores through overlapping arrays. These passes need memory and control-flow safety analyses before they can return. LLVM and vendor compilers continue to optimize generated code, without unconditional disjoint-storage promises on array parameters.

docs.title: IR Type Annotate (ir_type_annotate.py)
docs.text:
Walks the IR and annotates every expression node with a dtype attribute (a ScalarType). This also sets _resolved_type on each IRAssign.

After this pass, codegen backends read node.dtype directly instead of reimplementing type inference heuristics. This eliminated ~40 lines of duplicated _infer_c_type / _infer_expr_type logic per codegen backend.

Key rules:

  • IRConstant(42) → i32, IRConstant(2**31) → i64
  • IRConstant(3.14) → f32 unless it is part of a weak literal expression that meets an f64 operand, an f64 cast, or an f64 store, atomic or local; then every float literal in that expression is retyped to f64 (_meet, _adopt, _retype), following NumPy's NEP 50. Nodes carry _literal and _weak flags for this. Expressions without f64 operands annotate exactly as f32 literals would
  • IRArrayLoad → element type of the array
  • IRBinOp → promoted type, except integer / → f32, and shifts or integer ** → the left/base type independent of the count/exponent type
  • IRCast(value, ScalarType) → the target ScalarType
  • IRCall("sqrt", ...) → f32 (or f64 if any arg is f64)
  • IRCall("abs", [int_arg]) → preserves integer type
  • IRCall("min"/"max", ...) → promoted type of arguments
  • IRCall("pow", [int_base, int_exponent]) → the base type; otherwise the promoted floating precision
  • IRCompare, IRBoolOp → i32
  • IRName referencing an array param → None (array pointers aren't scalars)

Integer promotion preserves both full operand ranges; signed/u64 pairs require an explicit cast where promotion applies. True division and power use their distinct rules instead. Negative literal integer exponents are rejected here. See the language contract.

The pass joins all assignments to each local to one storage type, then annotates expressions using the settled environment (var_name → ScalarType). An IRBoundsCheck is i64.

docs.title: Bounds Guards (ir_bounds.py, debug mode)
docs.text: annotate_types ends with guard_accesses, which does nothing unless the function was lowered with bounds checks (bounds_sites). Each user array access whose index is an IRBoundsCheck is skipped when that index is negative: a load becomes index >= 0 ? load : 0 with a zero of the load's own type (hence after typing), and a store or atomic runs under if index >= 0. The index is evaluated twice, which is harmless because indices have no effects but the check's record of the first violation. Accesses to the hidden arrays and to GPU scalar packs are left alone. It runs once per function (_bounds_guarded), so annotating again before and after packing does not guard twice.

docs.title: Scalar Packing (ir_pack_scalars.py)
docs.text:
GPU backends only. Groups scalar parameters by type into packed array buffers to reduce buffer binding count (critical for Metal's 31-binding limit).

Algorithm: 1. Collect all params where _is_array == False, grouped by type 2. Create new IRParam for each group: __pack_f32__, __pack_i32__, etc. 3. Rewrite IRName("scalar_param") → IRArrayLoad(IRName("__pack_f32__"), IRConstant(idx)) 4. Remove original scalar params, append pack params

The pass runs on a clone_ir copy of the IR (to preserve the cached original) and stores pack_info metadata for the dispatch layer. Pack array buffers are allocated once and cached alongside the compiled kernel — subsequent calls just update the scalar values via from_numpy.

clone_ir preserves ScalarType identity, matching its __deepcopy__ protocol (type map lookups rely on object identity).

docs.title: Codegen
docs.text: Each backend has a code generator that walks the Tack IR and emits target-specific code. All codegens follow the same pattern: iterate over IR nodes, emit text or LLVM IR.

docs.title: Backend Summary
docs.text: Backend Codegen Output Key class CPU llvm_gen.py LLVM IR LLVMCodeGen (uses llvmlite builder) Metal msl_gen.py MSL source MSLCodeGen CUDA cuda_gen.py CUDA C source CUDACodeGen HIP hip_gen.py HIP C source HIPCodeGen(CUDACodeGen) Level Zero opencl_gen.py OpenCL C source OpenCLCodeGen(CUDACodeGen)

docs.title: Inheritance
docs.text:
HIP and OpenCL extend CUDA codegen because their device code syntax is nearly identical:

  • HIP: Same as CUDA (blockIdx, threadIdx, __global__), just adds #include <hip/hip_runtime.h>.
  • OpenCL: Different qualifiers (__kernel, get_group_id(0), __local, barrier()), overloaded math (no f suffix). Also maps long long → long for integer types.

Both override only the differences (kernel signature, type names, a few expressions) and inherit everything else.

docs.title: C-Like Codegens (CUDA, MSL, OpenCL)
docs.text: These share common patterns:

docs.title: Identifier Namespaces
docs.text:
codegen/identifiers.py makes a structural copy of the prepared IR for GPU emission. lang/ir_names.py enumerates binding and reference slots: parameters, assignments, loops, allocations, names, dimensions and texture references. Intrinsic call names, attributes and type/dispatch metadata are not renamed. Every binding uses tack_var_; every kernel entry uses tack_kernel_. ASCII names use the a_ branch, with Z and underscores escaped as Z1 and Z0; Unicode names use u_ plus UTF-8 hex. The encodings are injective, produce ASCII identifiers without double underscores, and keep user names separate from emitted helpers and temporaries. No vendor keyword list is needed.

Runtime compilation and inspection call kernel_entry_name on the original IR name; do not encode the IR function name in place or encode an already emitted spelling. LLVM uses the same entry encoding because llvmlite's JIT lookup requires ASCII. Canonical IR and its metadata keep their original names, and parameter positions/resource indices are preserved. Before this final emission step, lowering, template expansion, vector scalarization, scalar localization and packing use fresh_name to avoid merging generated bindings with source bindings.

docs.title: Variable Declaration and Type Inference
docs.text:
When emitting IRAssign, the codegen needs a C type for the variable declaration. It uses _resolved_type from the IR type annotation pass, mapped to a C type string via the backend's type map (_C_TYPE_MAP, _MSL_TYPE_MAP, _OCL_C_TYPE_MAP).

For expression nodes used in other contexts (index casts, printf format selection, floor division), the codegen reads node.dtype directly. The _infer_c_type(node) method checks node.dtype first and falls back to _local_vars only for array pointer references (which have dtype=None).

The _resolved_type_to_c() method maps ScalarType → C type string, and is overridden by OpenCL to use long instead of long long.

docs.title: If-Branch Variable Hoisting
docs.text:
C requires variable declarations before use at the scope level. When an IRAssign appears inside an if branch, the variable might not be visible in the else branch or after the if. The codegen "hoists" these declarations before the if:

float temp;          // hoisted
if (cond) {
    temp = 3.14;
} else {
    temp = 2.71;
}
// temp is visible here

The hoisting uses _find_assign_type to determine the type, which prefers _resolved_type from the annotation pass.

docs.title: Sequential For Loop Variables
docs.text:
Loop variables are always re-declared in the for header to handle reuse of the same variable name in sibling loops (C block scoping):

for (long k = 0; k < 8; k++) { ... }
for (long k = 0; k < 8; k++) { ... }  // re-declared, not "k = 0"

docs.title: Integer Types
docs.text:
GPU backends use 64-bit integers for loop variables and index arithmetic to support grids with more than 2^31 elements: - CUDA/HIP: long long, with blockIdx.x widened before the multiply - MSL: long, initialized from the uint thread position - OpenCL: long, from get_group_id(0) widened before the multiply; Intel's get_global_id(0) wraps at 2^32 despite its size_t type

The runtime refuses a launch longer than one grid can index (check_launch_size in runtime/kernel_utils.py), so the index never wraps.

docs.title: Floating Floor Division and Remainder
docs.text:
float_division.py shares typed GPU helpers for // and %; LLVM emits internal typed helpers with the same operations. Both operands convert to the annotated floating precision before a truncating remainder is computed. Sign correction makes nonzero remainders follow the divisor. Quotients are reconstructed and snapped to integral floating values, avoiding both rounded-division boundary errors and integer conversion overflow. The helpers explicitly preserve signed zeros and nonfinite result classes. Do not replace them with C % or an integer cast of floor(a / b).

All CUDA kernels omit --use_fast_math, explicitly selecting non-flushing, precise division/sqrt and permitted multiply/add contraction. Metal disables fastMathEnabled for all kernels. Runtime reduction sources use the same settings. No operator scan or mutable per-kernel math mode is needed. Inspection emits the same arithmetic helpers as dispatch. See the language contract for the nonzero-divisor and denormal domains.

docs.title: Floating-point policy
docs.text:
Floating math calls convert arguments to their annotated result precision before calling backend routines. CPU libm functions use their f32/f64 symbols and return that precision before enclosing arithmetic; integer math arguments default to f32 even when the destination array is f64. OpenCL/Metal calls need explicit casts to avoid overload ambiguity.

CPU emits no fast-math flags and HIP/OpenCL retain standard compiler settings without unsafe math options, except that HIP passes -ffp-contract=on (_HIPRTC_OPTIONS in hip_backend.py): hipRTC's default, fast, fused a product into one read of a variable while another read it rounded, so p - p was not zero. Expression grouping and nonfinite classes/signs must survive optimization. Adjacent multiply/add contraction is permitted inside one expression, so CPU/GPU results need not agree bitwise; a value bound to a name is rounded once and every read agrees. Scalar floating min/max prefer a number to NaN; the sign of equal zero ties is unspecified. Denormal support and global math accuracy are not inferred from safe compiler settings. test_float_semantics.py checks execution and explicit regression bounds; the language contract states the supported domains.

Compiler options live in module constants (_NVRTC_OPTIONS, _HIPRTC_OPTIONS, _OCLOC_OPTIONS and _MODULE_BUILD_FLAGS) that both the compiler call and the backend's cache_target() read, so changing one also stops the disk cache from reusing code compiled without it.

docs.title: Debug-Mode Bounds Checks
docs.text: Every generator emits IRBoundsCheck, and only when the kernel was lowered in debug mode, so normal kernels' code is unchanged. The C-family generators share codegen/bounds.py: one helper per kernel, __tack_in_bounds__, tests an index against its extent and, out of bounds, records the first violation in the errors array (an atomic add on its count elects the first); a check is && over its dimensions, then the flat index or -1. llvm_gen.py builds the same helper in LLVM IR (_bounds_helper). MSL counts a check as a store when deciding whether a sequential loop's body goes in the noinline __tack_body__ function (_stores_inside_sequential_loop), since it writes the errors array.

docs.title: LLVM Codegen (llvm_gen.py, 1,008 lines)
docs.text:
Uses llvmlite's IRBuilder to construct LLVM IR. Arrays become pointer arguments; scalars become value arguments. All allocas are placed in the entry block for SSA dominance.

Key differences from C-like codegens: - Types are LLVM types (FloatType(), IntType(64), etc.) - No variable declaration needed — LLVM uses SSA - Uses alloca for mutable local variables - IRLocalAlloc maps to a private stack alloca. Shared allocations, barriers, thread IDs and block reductions are rejected by workgroup_support.py before emission; CPU has no workgroup execution model.

docs.title: MSL Codegen (msl_gen.py, 689 lines)
docs.text:
Generates Metal Shading Language for Apple GPUs. Notable features:

  • Buffer bindings: device float* name [[buffer(N)]]
  • Textures use a separate binding namespace: texture3d<float> [[texture(N)]]
  • Threadgroup detection: scans IR for IRSharedAlloc/IRBarrier to decide between dispatch_threads (simple) and threadgroup-based dispatch
  • Hardware texture sampling: tex.sample(__samp__, float3(u, v, w)) with coordinate transform for Tack's texel-center convention
  • Float atomic min/max via CAS loop on atomic_uint

docs.title: CUDA Codegen (cuda_gen.py, 643 lines)
docs.text:
Generates extern "C" __global__ kernel functions. Thread index: 

long long __idx__ = (long long)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
if (__idx__ >= __n__) return;

The cast comes before the multiply: the built-ins are 32-bit unsigned, and their product would wrap at 2^32 threads.

_expr_constant emits a float literal annotated f64 as an unsuffixed repr (exact, since repr round-trips) and one annotated f32 with an f suffix. Float literals are weakly typed, so the annotation comes from the operand, cast or target the literal meets; see ir_type_annotate.py.

Float atomic min/max use CAS-based helper functions emitted on demand.

docs.title: OpenCL Codegen (opencl_gen.py, 338 lines)
docs.text:
Extends CUDA with OpenCL syntax differences. Also handles:

  • Hardware texture sampling: read_imagef(image, sampler, coords) when the device supports it (checked at runtime via maxSamplers)
  • Software trilinear fallback: generates an inline helper function with the texture dimensions baked in as constants, reading the texture's private f32 copy of its array

docs.title: The Backend Contract
docs.text:
Every backend subclasses Backend (runtime/backend.py), which declares what a backend must implement and what callers may ask it.

Required: allocate_array(), wrap_ptr(), execute().

Optional, with defaults that suit a backend lacking the feature:

Method Default Overridden by fill_array(array, value) False: Array.fill fills the buffer in place CPU, which runs a fill of 256 KiB or more as a kernel through its dispatch, so the threads first-touch the pages synchronize() Nothing to wait for Metal, CUDA, HIP and Level Zero, which queue launches (tack.sync() calls it on every backend, Device.synchronize() on one) memory_space(ptr) "cpu" Backends with device memory cache_target(), variant_artifact(), load_variant() None: compiled variants are not stored on disk Every backend; see The disk cache reduce_array(), texture_in_hardware(), create_texture_image() Host reductions, software sampling Backends with device reductions or texture units

Declared capabilities — read these instead of probing with hasattr:

Attribute Meaning name Device type, as a spec writes it (tack.device("metal")) ordinal Which of the type's devices; 0 for now (Device.index) display_name / label How to write the backend in a message supported_dtypes Scalar types accepted as array dtypes supports_f64 Derived from supported_dtypes — never declared separately supports_device_reductions Whether reduce_array() runs on device; otherwise Array.sum() and friends fall back to numpy supports_workgroups Native workgroup execution for shared memory, barriers, local thread IDs and block reductions; false on CPU device_memory_spaces Memory spaces a pointer must be in for array_from_ptr(); empty means no check device_options Keyword options tack.device() passes to the constructor; any other is refused memory_domain Derived: (name, ordinal), plus the context on Level Zero. Backends with one domain run kernels on each other's arrays

Anything derivable is derived. supports_f64 used to be declared independently, existed on Level Zero alone, and so getattr(backend, 'supports_f64', True) reported True for Metal — which has no f64 at all. Deriving it from supported_dtypes means there is nothing to keep in step.

Level Zero sets supported_dtypes in __init__ rather than on the class, because f64 depends on what the device reports. That shadows the class attribute, and supports_f64 follows automatically.

docs.title: Backend Lifecycle
docs.text:
Each backend follows the same lifecycle:

tack.device("metal")            (or set_default_device, or device="metal")
    → dispatch.py creates MetalBackend() on first use, kept in _devices
    → Backend discovers device, creates command queue / context
    → as_device(backend) wraps it as the tack.Device users see

kernel(x, y, out, alpha, n)
    → Kernel.__call__
    → dispatch.launch_backend(name, args): the default device if it can
      address the arrays, else the arrays' own device
    → backend.execute(kernel, args, kwargs)
    → Template expansion + IR pipeline + codegen + dispatch

A backend made without options lives for the process, in the registry dispatch._devices; one made with options lives while its Device or any of its arrays does (every Array holds its backend). Switching the default device builds nothing and invalidates nothing.

docs.title: Backend.execute() Flow
docs.text:
Every backend uses resolve_variant() in runtime/kernel_utils.py to find or build a specialization. A call first tries the dispatch fast path (below); otherwise:

  1. Expand template arguments and detect vector and texture arrays.
  2. Obtain the pristine IR template for this specialization (lowered, or read from the disk cache) and check required workgroup primitives against the backend's supports_workgroups. CPU memoizes feature discovery on the immutable template so warm dispatch does not walk the body again. GPU targets bypass this rejection check. In debug mode the template is the bounds-checked lowering, and the two hidden arguments (debug_bounds.hidden_args) are appended to the call's.
  3. Infer argument dtypes and categories on a private parameter probe, record texture extents, and derive resolved shape dependencies.
  4. Look up the variant in the backend's weakly keyed per-kernel cache, and then in the disk cache (_stored_variant).
  5. On a miss of both, clone the template (clone_ir in lang/ir_traversal.py, not copy.deepcopy), resolve dimensions, infer/check types, localize outer scalars the loop body assigns (_localize_outer_scalars), check atomics and workgroup participation, and run conservative copy propagation. The backend build callback then packs scalars where needed, annotates types, generates code, and compiles. The KernelVariant records the atomic targets and the array arguments the kernel may write. _store_variant then writes it to disk.
  6. On every call, check atomic alignment and refuse read-only arrays bound to written parameters (check_writable_arrays), and record the call's signature for the fast path.
  7. Resolve the launch range from the variant's IR for this dispatch; GPU backends refuse a range past their launch limit (check_launch_size). Replace each Texture3D with the storage it owns (bind_textures), bind arguments (updating any scalar pack buffers), and launch. GPU backends do the last two under a lock: the variant's dispatch_lock on CUDA and HIP, the backend's _batch_lock on Metal and _launch_lock on Level Zero. The CPU pool's run is a transaction under CPool._txn.

docs.title: The dispatch fast path
docs.text:
resolve_variant first reads the call's signature off its arguments (_call_signature): each array's dtype, shape and element layout, each scalar's kind and integer width, and for a template its class token, its class constants' current values and what the key and the expansion read of each attribute (nested templates by path). Equal signatures imply an equal variant key, so a signature seen before (_fast_resolve) expands the templates through a stored plan, decides disjointness over precomputed array slots, runs the per-call checks of step 6 (_check_call) and returns the variant the entry holds, without the template scope, IR lookup or key. drop_variants drops the entries with the variants. Debug mode and keyword arguments never use or record entries. A warm CPU dispatch with eight array arguments costs about 34 µs of host time on a 2 GHz Xeon. Anything that changes the variant key must change the signature too, or a call will run the wrong variant; test_dispatch_fast_path.py covers what the signature must separate (integer widths, the float context, class constants, template structure) and what a hit must still check.

The compiled key includes dtypes, array/scalar/texture categories, vector widths, texture extents, template structure/constants, and baked-in dimension sizes. Template structure includes actual class identity and runtime scalar attribute names. Changing scalar values alone does not recompile; changing an attribute layout or a vector width does.

Passes run only on a cache miss and never mutate the pristine template. Parameter probing is private to each dispatch so concurrent calls cannot observe another call's types. Arrays may overlap in storage; generated array parameters therefore carry no unconditional noalias or restrict promise.

The CPU backend adds one more key element: whether this call's arrays are disjoint. arrays_disjoint() compares the byte ranges of the array arguments on every dispatch and passes when no array the kernel writes overlaps another array. Qualifying calls use a variant compiled with noalias on its array pointers; the rest use the variant without it. Without the promise LLVM must reload after every store, which matters for kernels that accumulate through an array in an inner loop. Measured on 2026-10-03, single-threaded: on a 2012 Xeon E5-2650 the store-accumulator kernel at 2^20 elements ran in 2465 µs without the promise and 736 µs with it, and a stencil in 776 µs and 604 µs; the check added about 3–4 µs per 16-element dispatch there and about 1–1.6 µs on an Apple M1 Max, where the accumulator showed no comparable gain. See Specialization and Caching and Memory and Aliasing.

Template classes appear in keys as a token rather than the class object. When a @tack.device_class class is collected, a finalizer drops the IR and the compiled variants specialized on it from every backend's cache.

Public inspection checks the selected backend's workgroup capability before preparing a variant. Private _prepare_ir may omit a backend for cross-target codegen tools/tests. Direct LLVM generation always checks the supplied IR afresh because callers may mutate it.

GPU variant construction checks conservative workgroup participation after scalar localization, before optimization/packing. KernelVariant caches the full-group requirement; every collective dispatch checks its logical count, including cache hits. Direct GPU generators check mutable IR afresh, using _is_scalar_pack metadata for immutable runtime scalar inputs. Metal pipeline capacity and Level Zero X/total limits must admit 256 lanes. These checks do not establish atomic type/scope support or race freedom.

docs.title: The Disk Cache
docs.text:
runtime/disk_cache.py (public as tack.cache) keeps two levels across processes. Kernel._lower asks it for the lowered IR (.ir entries), keyed by content: the kernel's source and closure, the specialization, template content (MRO names, @tack.func sources, constants), Tack's fingerprint and the Python version. While lowering runs, every name resolved through CallBindings is recorded with a fingerprint of what it was bound to, and an entry is used only if each still resolves the same way, so an edited device function or constant misses. Anything lowering reads from Python must go through CallBindings or into the key.

_resolve_variant asks it for a compiled variant (.variant entries) on an in-memory miss, keyed by the .ir entry, the probed parameter types, vector widths, baked-in shapes, disjointness, the backend name and Backend.cache_target(). An entry holds the IR after the passes and whatever variant_artifact() returned; load_variant() rebuilds the payload from it, so a hit skips the passes, code generation and as much of compilation as the backend can (the CPU stores object code, Metal its MSL, CUDA PTX, HIP code objects, Level Zero a native binary with its SPIR-V). The target must name everything the artifact depends on besides the kernel and its argument types: the device, the compiler's and driver's versions, and the compile options, which the backends keep in module constants (_NVRTC_OPTIONS, _HIPRTC_OPTIONS, _OCLOC_OPTIONS) that compiler and target both read. A GPU payload's scalar pack buffers are device memory of the process, so load_variant makes them anew from the call's arguments. Debug mode is part of the lowered key, so its kernels are stored apart. The test suite runs with TACK_CACHE=off unless the environment says otherwise; test_disk_cache.py runs its cases in fresh processes. See The Kernel Cache for the settings and MPI bundles.

docs.title: Launch Completion
docs.text: Only the CPU backend finishes a launch before execute returns. Metal, CUDA, HIP and Level Zero queue launches in program order (an open Metal command buffer, one stream per CUDA context or HIP device, one asynchronous immediate command list with a barrier after each command on Level Zero) and return; CUDA, HIP and Level Zero queue fills and host-to-device copies in the same order. The host waits where it reads array memory (numpy(), read_range, reductions; on Metal every host access to a buffer) or calls tack.sync(), which is Backend.synchronize(). An array dropped while a queued launch still uses it is freed after that launch (stream-ordered allocation, Level Zero's deferred free, Metal's per-launch references). Memory handed outside Tack (wrap_ptr, DLPack export, share()) makes every launch that uses it complete before it returns, and so does a CUDA, HIP or Level Zero launch with a texture. A launch's error surfaces at the next wait. test_cuda_async.py, test_hip_async.py and test_level_zero_async.py check ordering, host writes and the waits.

docs.title: Loop Range Resolution
docs.text:
_get_loop_range() extracts the parallel for-loop bound from the IR and resolves it against actual arguments. It supports:

  • IRConstant(N) — literal bound
  • IRName("n") — scalar parameter
  • IRDimSize("x", 0) — x.shape[0] or len(x)
  • IRBinOp over any of the above — e.g. range(n - 1)

This must run before scalar packing since packing removes scalar params.

The grid bound is the one IRDimSize that resolve_ir deliberately leaves unresolved. Everywhere else it folds to a literal, because the value has to appear in the generated code; the grid bound does not — codegen reads the __loop_end__ parameter — so folding it would make the compiled kernel depend on the array's length and force a recompile for every new size. ir_shape_deps() excludes it from the variant key for the same reason.

docs.title: Array Allocation
docs.text:
Each backend implements allocate_array(dtype, shape) returning a backend-specific buffer:

Backend Buffer type Memory model CPU NumpyBuffer numpy array (host memory) Metal MetalBuffer Metal shared buffer (unified CPU+GPU) CUDA CUDABuffer Stream-ordered device pointer (cuMemAllocAsync) HIP HIPBuffer Stream-ordered device pointer (hipMallocAsync; hipMalloc without memory pools) Level Zero L0Buffer Device pointer (zeMemAllocDevice)

Array (tack.Array) wraps a buffer with dtype and shape metadata. tack.copyto() and numpy() handle host-device transfers through the buffer's from_numpy() / to_numpy() (on Metal this is a memcpy within unified memory; on CUDA/HIP/L0 it involves explicit copies).

A new array's contents are unspecified on every backend; nothing fills it. tack.zeros, ones and full call Array.fill, which first offers the fill to Backend.fill_array. The CPU backend takes a fill of 256 KiB or more and runs tack.algorithms.copy._fill_kernel through its dispatch, so the threads that will use the pages touch them first; GPU buffers fill on the device. Metal's new buffers are already zero (starts_zeroed), so tack.zeros skips the fill there -- but not for a buffer of 1 MiB or more reused from Metal's pool of freed ones, which holds what it held. Code that reads an array before writing it must make it with tack.zeros.

docs.title: CPU
docs.text:
The LLVM-JIT'd function is called via ctypes. The backend compares measured serial work against measured thread fan-out cost, splitting worthwhile ranges across a persistent pool of pthreads that is itself JIT'd from LLVM IR (cpu_pool.py): one ctypes call posts the launch to the workers it uses (each waits on its own mailbox; the rest sleep on), each worker calls the compiled function with a (start, end) sub-range through a per-kernel wrapper, and none of them touches Python. Workers and the caller claim chunks from a counter rather than taking one equal share each, so a slow worker takes fewer. Idle workers block on a futex (Linux) or os_sync_wait_on_address (macOS 14.4+) and poll elsewhere. Arguments reach the wrapper as array addresses packed into 8-byte slots with one struct.pack_into. TACK_CPU_POOL=python uses a ThreadPoolExecutor instead, which is also the fallback on Windows and wherever the pool cannot be built; tests that simulate workers through the Python path's seams set it.

Periodic serial rechecks sample different positions in the range. Long worker spans establish a floor under the serial estimate, preventing cheap image slices from making an expensive frame look cheap. That floor applies to the measured workload: runtime inputs can change without recompilation. When every worker of a complete dispatch later finishes below the trusted span duration, the backend retires the old floor and schedules a serial recheck on the next call. Partial head/tail dispatches and a short median with any long worker cannot retire it. Worker spans below the rate clock's resolution still establish that the complete dispatch was short.

docs.title: Metal
docs.text: Encodes a compute command: the array pointers go into one argument buffer (declared resident with useResource), and dispatchThreads covers the grid. Textures use a separate binding namespace (setTexture_atIndex_) and bind the MetalTextureImage the Texture3D owns. Each launch owns a fresh argument buffer and its packed scalars, encodes into the open command buffer, and returns; the command buffer is committed every 64 launches.

docs.title: CUDA / HIP
docs.text: Launches via cuLaunchKernel / hipModuleLaunchKernel with a pointer array of arguments, on the context's (CUDA) or device's (HIP) stream, and returns once queued. Grid size = ceil(loop_end / 256), block size = 256. A texture argument passes the texture object of the CUDATextureImage or HIPTextureImage its Texture3D owns.

docs.title: Level Zero
docs.text: Sets kernel arguments via zeKernelSetArgumentValue. Dispatches via zeCommandListAppendLaunchKernel on the backend's asynchronous immediate command list, followed by a barrier, and returns once appended; the arguments are captured at the append, so the next call may set its own. Textures use the L0TextureImage (zeImageCreate, bound as image3d_t) their Texture3D owns on devices with sampler hardware.

docs.title: Scalar Packing at Dispatch
docs.text: Pack array buffers are allocated once during compilation and cached. On subsequent calls, _update_pack_arrays() just writes the new scalar values into the existing device buffers via from_numpy(). This avoids per-dispatch allocation overhead. With queued launches this stays correct because the copy is queued too: on CUDA, HIP and Level Zero the next call's update is queued after the launch that reads the old values. Metal launches carry their own copy of the scalars (_Uniforms) instead.

docs.title: Device Pointer Interop
docs.text:
tack.array_from_ptr() wraps an existing device pointer as an Array without allocation or copy. Each backend implements wrap_ptr(ptr, dtype, shape):

Backend ptr type Implementation CPU numpy array or int address np.frombuffer view into existing memory Metal MTLBuffer object Creates numpy view via contents().as_buffer() CUDA device address (int, NumPy integer or CUdeviceptr) Stores pointer, skips cuMemAlloc HIP device address (anything int() accepts) Stores it as an int (hip-python reads a NumPy scalar as a buffer), skips hipMalloc Level Zero device address (anything int() accepts) Stores c_void_p, skips zeMemAllocDevice

On CUDA, HIP and Level Zero, array_from_ptr() first checks the pointer with as_address() (TypeError if it is not an address) and memory_space() (ValueError if it is not device memory).

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
Wrapped buffers set _owned = False. Buffer destructors (__del__) check this flag to skip freeing external memory:

def __del__(self):
    if hasattr(self, '_device_ptr') and getattr(self, '_owned', True):
        # in stream order, after the launches queued so far
        driver.cuMemFreeAsync(self._device_ptr, token.queue())  # skipped for wrapped ptrs

docs.title: Read-Only Protection
docs.text: Array._writable defaults to True for allocated arrays and False for array_from_ptr(); a read-only DLPack import is also not writable. The _check_writable() method guards tack.copyto() and fill(). For kernels, the variant records which array arguments the kernel may store to (KernelVariant.written_arrays, from written_array_params, all of them when a store can't be traced), and check_writable_arrays() raises ValueError on every dispatch that binds a read-only array to one of them.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Kernel.__call__ wraps backend errors: - TypeError → includes kernel name, once (a message that already starts with it is kept as is) - Compilation failure → extracts error lines, suppresses full source dump - RuntimeError → includes kernel name and backend class name

In debug mode, Kernel.__call__ (and the result epilogue) calls debug_bounds.check() after the launch, which waits for it and raises IndexError naming the first out-of-bounds access it recorded. On a backend that queues launches, any other launch's error surfaces at the next wait rather than at its call.

tack.device() wraps backend start-up errors with the device type, platform, and install instructions.

docs.title: Template System
docs.text: The template system enables zero-cost polymorphism: the same kernel source compiles to different GPU code depending on the concrete types passed.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Three pieces work together:

  1. @tack.device_class (device_class.py) — marks a class as passable to kernels. Collects @tack.func methods into cls._tack_func_methods.

  2. @tack.func (func.py) — captures a function's AST and original Python callable for inlining and static binding resolution. Class methods are stored on the class by @tack.device_class.

  3. Template rewrite (template_rewrite.py) — AST pre-pass that resolves template parameters before IR transformation.

docs.title: Template Rewrite Flow
docs.text:
When backend.execute() detects a @tack.device_class argument:

# In cpu.py / metal.py / etc.:
template_args = _detect_template_args(kernel, args)
# → {0: ("grid", grid_obj)}  (param index → (name, object))

effective_args = _expand_template_args(args, template_args)
# → removes template objects, inserts their array attributes and runtime scalars

ir_module = kernel.get_ir(..., template_args=template_args)
# → calls template_rewrite.rewrite_templates() before AST transform

docs.title: What rewrite_templates Does
docs.text:
Given a kernel:

@tack.kernel
def avg(cs, data, out, n):
    for c in range(n):
        total = 0.0
        for v in range(cs.points_per_cell):
            total = total + data[cs.get_point_id(c, v)]
        out[c] = total / float(cs.points_per_cell)

Called with CellSetStructured3D(nx=50, ny=50, nz=50):

  1. Remove template param from signature: cs is removed
  2. Add array params: cs.connectivity (if it exists) becomes a new parameter __tmpl_cs_connectivity__
  3. Add runtime scalar params: cs.width (instance scalar) becomes parameter __tmpl_cs_width__
  4. Replace class constant access: cs.points_per_cell → ast.Constant(8) (baked in)
  5. Replace instance scalar access: cs.width → ast.Name("__tmpl_cs_width__") (runtime parameter)
  6. Replace method calls: cs.get_point_id(c, v) → inline the method body with self references resolved

The rewrite returns the AST and a local map of resolved methods. Method names include the template parameter name, so repeated object arguments retain distinct synthetic array/scalar layouts. Generated calls carry an AST marker to distinguish them from user functions with the same spelling. The map belongs to this transformation; no registration or global cleanup is required. Resolved methods retain the original Python callable for globals/closure lookup and do not mutate the class's captured source.

docs.title: Attribute Classification
docs.text:
classify_template_attrs(obj) splits an object's attributes into three categories:

scalars = {"points_per_cell": 8}              # class variables → compile-time constants
arrays = {"connectivity": <Array>}             # instance Arrays → kernel parameters
runtime_scalars = {"width": 512, "height": 512}  # instance scalars → runtime parameters
  • Class-level scalars (defined on the class, e.g., points_per_cell = 8) become AST constants, baked into generated code, and are part of the cache key. Changing them triggers recompilation.
  • Instance scalars (set in __init__, e.g., self.width = width) become synthetic kernel scalar parameters. They are passed at dispatch time and do not appear in the cache key — changing them reuses the compiled kernel.
  • Instance arrays become synthetic kernel buffer parameters (as before).

This distinction avoids unnecessary JIT recompilation when only runtime values (like image dimensions) change between calls.

docs.title: Nested Templates
docs.text:
A template may hold templates as instance attributes. template_tree(obj) lists (path, object) for the object and everything nested in it, depth first, children by name, and refuses a cycle. classify_template_attrs flattens the tree: a nested object's constants, arrays and runtime scalars are named by their path joined with __ (base__step), so the runtime's argument expansion and vector-array detection, which read the flattened dicts, need nothing new, and the synthetic parameters follow one order. rewrite_templates builds a _Node per object (its own constants, the synthetic names of its own arrays and scalars, its resolved methods and function attributes, its children); every resolved method of the tree takes the whole tree's synthetic parameters, and self.a.b.method() and self.a.b.attr resolve by walking the children (_resolve_call, _resolve_attribute). A chain stops at the first attribute that is not a template, so self.data.shape[0] still reads an array's shape.

A dispatch reads a template several times -- its key, its expanded arguments, its vector arrays -- so resolve_variant opens a template_scope, in which each object's tree, classification, function attributes, structure and cache-key part are found once (memoized). The objects are the call's arguments, alive throughout, so their ids cannot be reused within the scope.

Only a call the dispatch fast path cannot answer enters the scope. A warm call reads each template into its signature instead (_template_signature in runtime/kernel_utils.py): the class token, the class constants' current values, and per attribute what the key and the expansion read, following an attribute layout learned once per class (_template_layouts, relearned when an instance's attribute names or types differ). It then expands the arguments through the plan stored with the signature.

docs.title: @tack.func Inlining
docs.text:
When the AST transformer encounters a @tack.func call, it runs _inline_func_call():

Calls are first resolved by call_bindings.py using the defining callable's globals and closure cells, or the marked template-method map. Function identity determines the body. Arguments are lowered under the caller's bindings; body traversal temporarily switches to the callee's bindings. Validation uses the same resolver, including intrinsic shadowing checks. Only static module attributes are followed; object properties and runtime callables are unsupported. The active function identities detect recursion.

  1. Generate unique suffix: __{func_name}_{param}_{counter}__
  2. Build rename map: callee param names → unique names
  3. Deep-copy callee AST and rename all variables
  4. Propagate metadata: vector variables, texture arrays
  5. Emit parameter assignments: __func_x_0__ = caller_arg (skipped for texture params — they reference the original kernel parameter)
  6. Visit renamed body to produce IR statements
  7. Return result variable as IRName

The inlined statements are collected in _pre_stmts and hoisted before the statement containing the call.

docs.title: Multi-Return Inlining
docs.text:
For functions returning tuples:

@tack.func
def minmax(a, b):
    if a < b:
        return a, b
    return b, a

The inliner detects n_returns > 1 and creates multiple result variables: __minmax_ret_0_0__, __minmax_ret_1_0__. Return statements become assignments to these variables.

docs.title: Texture Propagation
docs.text:
When a texture array is passed through @tack.func, the inliner must:

  1. Propagate _texture_arrays: renamed param → same shape metadata
  2. Track origin: _texture_origin[renamed] = original_param_name
  3. Skip assignment: texture params can't be assigned to pointer variables
  4. Use original name: IRTextureSample.array_name uses the original kernel param name (via _texture_origin), not the renamed inline name

docs.title: Local Array Propagation
docs.text:
When a tack.local_array is passed to a @tack.func, arrays can't be assigned in C (int arr2[8] = arr1; is invalid). The inliner handles this by aliasing the caller's array name directly:

  1. Before the renamer runs, check if the caller arg is in _shared_vars
  2. If so, override the rename map: rename_map[param_name] = caller_arg_name
  3. The renamer substitutes the callee's param name with the caller's array name throughout the inlined body
  4. Skip the parameter assignment (like textures)

This means the inlined body's pts[v] = ... compiles to caller_array[v] = ... with no intermediate variable. The same mechanism works for tack.shared() arrays.

docs.title: Cache Keys
docs.text:
Each unique combination of template types produces a different compiled kernel. The cache key includes:

  • Kernel object identity (held weakly by the backend cache)
  • Type signature and array/scalar/texture category of all params
  • Actual template class identity, typed compile-time constants, array metadata, and runtime scalar attribute names
  • The paths and classes of the templates it holds (template_structure), whose tokens also retire the variants when a nested class is collected
  • Vector array widths
  • Texture shapes
  • Dimension sizes baked into code by shape resolution

Runtime scalar values do not specialize, but changing the set of runtime attributes changes the parameter layout and requires another variant.

This means avg(structured_cs, ...) and avg(explicit_cs, ...) produce two separately cached compilations with different generated code.

The disk cache cannot use class identity across processes, so it keys a template by content instead: the names along its class's MRO, the sources of its @tack.func methods and function attributes, and its constants. Each name lowering resolves is also recorded with a fingerprint of what it was bound to, so an edited method or class constant misses.

docs.title: Adding a New Feature
docs.text: This chapter walks through the process of adding a new IR node to Tack, using tack.local_array() as the example. This was an actual feature added in a single session.

docs.title: 1. Define the IR Node
docs.text:
Add a new class to ir.py:

class IRLocalAlloc(IRNode):
    """Allocate a per-thread local array (private memory on GPU, stack on CPU)."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, dtype: str, size):
        self.name = name
        self.dtype = dtype   # "float", "int", etc.
        self.size = size     # IRNode expression for number of elements

Also add it to the dump() function for debugging:

if isinstance(node, IRLocalAlloc):
    return f"{prefix}LocalAlloc {node.name}: {node.dtype}[{dump(node.size)}]"

docs.title: 2. Add the Python-Side API
docs.text:
In __init__.py, add a placeholder that raises at runtime (the actual handling happens at AST level):

def local_array(dtype, size):
    """Allocate a per-thread local array. Only usable inside a @tack.kernel."""
    raise RuntimeError("local_array() can only be used inside a @tack.kernel")

docs.title: 3. Handle in AST Transform
docs.text:
In ast_transform.py and lang/lowering/local_arrays.py, add recognition in two places:

Assignment form (the normal usage):

# In visit_Assign, after shared memory check:
if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    local_result = self._try_parse_local_alloc(target.id, value)
    if local_result is not None:
        return local_result

Standalone call error (helpful message if used wrong):

if func_name == "local_array":
    raise NotImplementedError(
        "tack.local_array() must be used in an assignment: "
        "arr = tack.local_array(tack.f32, 8)")

Parser method (mirrors _try_parse_shared_alloc, in lang/lowering/local_arrays.py):

def _try_parse_local_alloc(self, target_name, value_node):
    # Parse tack.local_array(tack.f32, 8) → IRLocalAlloc
    name = self._resolve_call_name(value_node)
    if name != "local_array":
        return None
    # ... parse dtype, size ...
    self._shared_vars.add(target_name)  # treat as array for indexing
    return ir.IRLocalAlloc(name=target_name, dtype=c_type, size=size)

Note: adding to _shared_vars ensures that arr[i] is recognized as array indexing (array load/store) rather than a scalar subscript.

docs.title: 4. Update IR Passes
docs.text:
Register the node's structural children in ir_traversal.py. Resolution, packing, and copy substitution will then recurse into them automatically:

ir.IRLocalAlloc: (('size', 'expr'),),

Add the node to the appropriate statement/expression set in ir_verify.py, declare required metadata there, and enforce its stage postconditions. Unknown nodes fail verification and traversal until explicitly supported. Type annotation and control-flow-sensitive analyses still need semantic handling. For an allocation, annotate the size and record the element type:

if isinstance(node, ir.IRLocalAlloc):
    _annotate_expr(node.size, env, array_params)
    env[node.name] = node.dtype
    return

Test resolution, packing, copy substitution, and verification through the new child slots, including malformed IR and missing required annotations.

docs.title: C-Like Backends (CUDA, MSL, OpenCL)
docs.text:
Simple — emit a C array declaration:

# cuda_gen.py (also inherited by HIP):
elif isinstance(node, ir.IRLocalAlloc):
    self._emit(f"{node.dtype} {node.name}[{self._expr(node.size)}];")

# msl_gen.py:
elif isinstance(node, ir.IRLocalAlloc):
    self._emit(f"{node.dtype} {node.name}[{self._expr(node.size)}];")

# opencl_gen.py (overrides _emit_stmt):
