elif isinstance(node, ir.IRLocalAlloc):
    self._emit(f"{node.dtype} {node.name}[{self._expr(node.size)}];")

docs.title: LLVM Backend
docs.text:
Use private stack allocation for local arrays on CPU. Shared memory requires workgroup execution and is rejected by the CPU target:

elif isinstance(node, ir.IRLocalAlloc):
    self._emit_local_alloc(node)

docs.title: 6. Write Tests
docs.text:
Test on all available backends:

def _available_backends():
    backends = ["cpu"]
    for arch in ["metal", "cuda", "hip", "level_zero"]:
        try:
            tack.set_default_device(arch)
            backends.append(arch)
        except (ImportError, RuntimeError, OSError):
            pass
    tack.set_default_device("cpu")
    return backends

@pytest.fixture(params=_available_backends())
def backend(request):
    tack.set_default_device(request.param)
    return request.param

def test_local_array_store_load(backend):
    @tack.kernel
    def use_local(out, n):
        for i in range(n):
            arr = tack.local_array(tack.f32, 4)
            arr[0] = 1.0
            arr[1] = 2.0
            out[i] = arr[0] + arr[1]
    # ...

A new test module for a new area joins the quick tier (pytestmark = pytest.mark.quick at module level) if it runs in under ten seconds; see "Tests, in three tiers" in CLAUDE.md. The suite runs with the disk cache off (TACK_CACHE=off) unless the environment says otherwise, so a test that counts compilations is not hidden by a cache hit.

docs.title: 7. What Else a Feature Can Touch
docs.text:
The IR node is most of the work, but several runtime mechanisms assume they know everything that shapes the generated code:

  • Debug mode. A node that indexes an array must have its index checked in debug mode: lowering wraps it through _checked in lang/lowering/bounds.py (an IRBoundsCheck), ir_bounds.guard_accesses must skip the access when the check is negative, and every generator must emit the check. Run the new tests with TACK_DEBUG=1 too; a test of what plain mode generates (source text, a reduced toolchain) takes the no_debug fixture.
  • Variant key and fast-path signature. A new fact about the arguments that changes the generated code goes into the variant key, and the dispatch fast path's _call_signature must distinguish it as well, or a warm call reuses the wrong variant.
  • Disk cache. What lowering reads from Python must be resolved through CallBindings or added to the lowered key (disk_cache.lowered_key). What compiled code depends on besides the IR and argument types (a device property, a compiler version or option) must be named by the backend's cache_target(); keep compiler options in the module constant the target reads.
  • Metal objects. Every new... selector metal.py calls must be registered in _OWNED_RESULTS before it is first called, or PyObjC retains its result once too often and it is never freed.
  • Queued launches. On Metal, CUDA, HIP and Level Zero a launch returns before it runs. Host code that reads device memory without going through a DeviceBuffer method, or hands it to another library, must call tack.sync() (or Backend.synchronize()) first.

docs.title: 8. Incidental Fixes
docs.text: New features often expose pre-existing bugs. tack.local_array revealed that reusing a loop variable name in sibling for loops caused "undeclared identifier" errors on GPU backends due to C block scoping. The fix (always re-declare loop variables in the for-header) was unrelated to local arrays but was caught by the new tests.

docs.title: Summary Checklist
docs.text:
For any new IR node (all files under packages/tack-core/src/tack/):

  • [ ] lang/ir.py: Node class + dump entry
  • [ ] __init__.py: Python-side API placeholder
  • [ ] lang/ast_transform.py or the lang/lowering/ module for the job: AST recognition + parser (and _checked for an indexed access)
  • [ ] lang/ir_traversal.py: Structural children in CHILD_FIELDS
  • [ ] lang/ir_verify.py: Statement/expression role, required metadata
  • [ ] lang/ir_resolve.py: Recurse into child expressions
  • [ ] lang/ir_pack_scalars.py: Recurse into child expressions
  • [ ] lang/ir_type_annotate.py: Annotate dtype or skip
  • [ ] lang/ir_optimize.py: Handle if it affects optimization
  • [ ] codegen/llvm_gen.py: LLVM emission
  • [ ] codegen/cuda_gen.py: CUDA C emission (inherited by HIP)
  • [ ] codegen/msl_gen.py: MSL emission
  • [ ] codegen/opencl_gen.py: OpenCL C emission (if different from CUDA)
  • [ ] lang/ir_bounds.py: Guard the access in debug mode, if it indexes memory
  • [ ] Tests on all backends (in packages/tack-core/tests/), with and without TACK_DEBUG=1; a new module marked quick if it is fast

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Look up the functions you call from Python here. The signatures and detailed descriptions below are generated from the source. For a complete program, use the User's Guide; for a reminder of which operations belong on the host or in a kernel, use the quick reference.

Task Call Result or effect Choose the default device tack.set_default_device("cuda") Arrays are allocated there; with nothing set it is the CPU Name a device tack.device("cuda"), with tack.device("cuda"): The same Device every time; with makes it the default in the block Allocate on a device tack.empty((n,), device="cuda") Every constructor takes device= Move an array a.to_device("cpu"), a.device a itself if its memory is usable there, else a copy Check indices tack.set_debug(True) Every kernel launched afterwards checks its indices Allocate an output tack.empty((n,)) New f32 array with unspecified contents Work in double precision tack.set_default_float(tack.f64) Arrays without a dtype (and Python floats) are f64 Allocate with another dtype tack.empty((n,), tack.i32) Any Tack type or NumPy dtype (np.int32, "int32") Allocate zeros, ones or a value tack.zeros((n,)), tack.ones((n,)), tack.full((n,), 2.5) New array, filled on the device Match storage without copying tack.empty_like(prototype) Same shape and element dtype; no values read or initialized Match and fill tack.zeros_like(a), tack.ones_like(a), tack.full_like(a, v) Same shape and element dtype, filled Upload NumPy data tack.array(host) New array with an independent copy; a NumPy array keeps its dtype Use an array as is tack.asarray(obj) obj itself if it is already a Tack array (of dtype, if given), else tack.array(obj) Overwrite values from the host tack.copyto(a, host) Copies into a; host has a.numpy()'s shape or broadcasts to it Copy between arrays tack.copyto(dst, src) Device-side copy into an existing array of the same shape Download data a.numpy() or np.asarray(a) Independent NumPy array; waits for earlier writes Allocate vector elements tack.empty((n,), tack.vec3()) Array of n 3-vectors; NumPy download shape (n, 3) Inspect shape and size a.shape, a.ndim, a.size, a.nbytes Element counts (components excluded) and storage bytes Reshape without copying a.reshape(rows, -1) Shares storage; one dimension may be -1 Wait for device work tack.sync() Waits for queued launches on every device; returns None Inspect a kernel tack.inspect(kernel, *args, mode="source") Generated source as a string; does not execute the kernel

Without a dtype, an allocation is f32 (the default float type, tack.set_default_float); values from Python make it from floats and i32 from ints (i64 if a value needs it), and a NumPy array keeps its own dtype, so a float64 array becomes f64.

For ownership, errors and precise guarantees, see the Runtime API contract and the Kernel Language Contract. Compiler internals are in the Developer's Guide.

docs.title: Devices
docs.text: A kernel runs on its arrays' device: the default device when that can address them, otherwise theirs. See Backends: Devices.

docs.title: tack.device
docs.text:
device(spec='cpu', **options) -> Device

The device spec names: "cpu", "metal", "cuda", "cuda:0", "hip", "level_zero"; a Device is returned as it is.

Without options it is made on first use and the same device afterwards, so its compiled kernels and arrays are shared by everything that asks. Options go to the backend and must be ones it declares in Backend.device_options; they make a new device each call. The CPU takes num_threads; Level Zero takes external_context, the driver, device and context handles of a context owned by another library, so both can address the same memory.

"cuda:N" is device N as the runtime numbers it (CUDA's ordinal, HIP's device id, the index among the first Level Zero driver's devices); device_count says how many there are. A bare "cuda" or "hip" is the device the calling thread already uses: the one of a CUDA context another library made current, HIP's current device, else device 0. "level_zero" is device 0.

with tack.device("cuda"): makes it the default device in the block.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/runtime/dispatch.py 
def device(spec="cpu", **options) -> Device:
    """The device ``spec`` names: ``"cpu"``, ``"metal"``, ``"cuda"``, ``"cuda:0"``,
    ``"hip"``, ``"level_zero"``; a `Device` is returned as it is.

    Without options it is made on first use and the same device afterwards,
    so its compiled kernels and arrays are shared by everything that asks.
    Options go to the backend and must be ones it declares in
    `Backend.device_options`; they make a new device each call. The CPU
    takes ``num_threads``; Level Zero takes ``external_context``, the
    driver, device and context handles of a context owned by another
    library, so both can address the same memory.

    ``"cuda:N"`` is device N as the runtime numbers it (CUDA's ordinal,
    HIP's device id, the index among the first Level Zero driver's
    devices); `device_count` says how many there are. A bare ``"cuda"`` or
    ``"hip"`` is the device the calling thread already uses: the one of a
    CUDA context another library made current, HIP's current device, else
    device 0. ``"level_zero"`` is device 0.

    ``with tack.device("cuda"):`` makes it the default device in the block.
    """
    if isinstance(spec, Device):
        if options:
            raise TypeError("options make a new device: pass a device spec, not a Device")
        return spec
    kind, index = _parse(spec)
    if options:
        return as_device(_construct(kind, options, index))
    if index is None:
        index = _current_index(kind)
    with _lock:
        found = _devices.get((kind, index))
        if found is None:
            found = _devices[(kind, index)] = _construct(kind, {}, index)
        return as_device(found)

docs.title: tack.device_count
docs.text:
device_count(kind: str) -> int

How many devices of type kind this machine has: 0 where it cannot start.

Counting makes no device: tack.device(f"cuda:{n}") for n below the count does.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/runtime/dispatch.py 
def device_count(kind: str) -> int:
    """How many devices of type ``kind`` this machine has: 0 where it cannot start.

    Counting makes no device: ``tack.device(f"cuda:{n}")`` for ``n`` below
    the count does.
    """
    if kind not in _CONSTRUCTORS:
        available = ", ".join(sorted(_CONSTRUCTORS))
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown device type: '{kind}'. Available: {available}")
    try:
        return _backend_class(kind).device_count()
    except (ImportError, RuntimeError, OSError):
        return 0

docs.title: tack.set_default_device
docs.text:
set_default_device(spec='cpu', **options) -> Device

Make spec's device the default: where arrays are allocated, and where kernels without arrays run. Returns it.

The device is tack.device(spec, **options): without options the same one as before, so arrays and compiled kernels survive another call.

Set TACK_NO_REINIT=1 to leave the default alone once one is set (useful when embedded in an ANARI device that shares the process).

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/runtime/dispatch.py 
def set_default_device(spec="cpu", **options) -> Device:
    """Make ``spec``'s device the default: where arrays are allocated, and where
    kernels without arrays run. Returns it.

    The device is ``tack.device(spec, **options)``: without options the same
    one as before, so arrays and compiled kernels survive another call.

    Set ``TACK_NO_REINIT=1`` to leave the default alone once one is set
    (useful when embedded in an ANARI device that shares the process).
    """
    global _current_backend
    if _current_backend is not None and env_flag("TACK_NO_REINIT"):
        return as_device(_current_backend)
    _current_backend = device(spec, **options)._backend
    return as_device(_current_backend)

docs.title: tack.set_debug
docs.text:
set_debug(enabled: bool = True)

Check every array index in every kernel launched from now on.

A launch that went out of bounds raises IndexError naming the access; the access itself is skipped. Kernels compile separately in debug mode and run slower; each launch waits to finish. TACK_DEBUG=1 turns it on when Tack is imported.

def set_debug(enabled: bool = True):
    """Check every array index in every kernel launched from now on.

    A launch that went out of bounds raises ``IndexError`` naming the access;
    the access itself is skipped. Kernels compile separately in debug mode
    and run slower; each launch waits to finish. ``TACK_DEBUG=1`` turns it on
    when Tack is imported.
    """
    global _debug
    _debug = bool(enabled)

docs.title: tack.runtime.dispatch.get_backend
docs.text:
get_backend()

The default device's backend: the innermost with tack.device(...) block's, else the one set_default_device chose, starting the CPU if none was.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/runtime/dispatch.py 
def get_backend():
    """The default device's backend: the innermost ``with tack.device(...)``
    block's, else the one `set_default_device` chose, starting the CPU if
    none was."""
    global _current_backend
    if _open_scopes:     # a failed thread-local lookup costs ~0.2 us a launch
        stack = _scope.__dict__.get("stack")
        if stack:
            return stack[-1]
    if _current_backend is None:
        _current_backend = device("cpu")._backend
    return _current_backend

docs.title: tack.sync
docs.text:
sync()

Wait until every kernel launched so far, on every device, has finished.

Reading or writing an array from the host (numpy, tack.copyto, indexing, reductions, DLPack export) already waits for the kernels before it, so most code never needs this. It is for timing kernels, and for memory shared with another library that reads it without Tack.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/runtime/dispatch.py 
def sync():
    """Wait until every kernel launched so far, on every device, has finished.

    Reading or writing an array from the host (``numpy``, ``tack.copyto``,
    indexing, reductions, DLPack export) already waits for the kernels
    before it, so most code never needs this. It is for timing kernels, and
    for memory shared with another library that reads it without Tack.
    """
    for backend in live_backends():
        backend.synchronize()

docs.title: tack.sync_async async
docs.text:
sync_async()

sync for asyncio: await tack.sync_async() waits for every kernel launched so far, on every device, without blocking the event loop.

On CUDA, HIP, Metal and Level Zero the wait runs in a worker thread and the loop goes on; launches made after the call are not waited for. A launch's error is raised here. On the CPU, whose launches complete before returning, it returns at once. See tack.runtime.aio.

async def sync_async():
    """`sync` for ``asyncio``: ``await tack.sync_async()`` waits for every
    kernel launched so far, on every device, without blocking the event
    loop.

    On CUDA, HIP, Metal and Level Zero the wait runs in a worker thread and
    the loop goes on; launches made after the call are not waited for. A
    launch's error is raised here. On the CPU, whose launches complete
    before returning, it returns at once. See `tack.runtime.aio`.
    """
    from tack.runtime.aio import sync_async as _sync_async
    await _sync_async()

docs.title: Arrays
docs.text: tack.Array holds storage on one device (a.device), chosen at allocation. Its shape counts elements; its dtype describes one scalar, vector or matrix element. tack.dataset.Field instead couples coefficient values with a space on a topology. See Arrays and Types for examples.

docs.title: tack.Array
docs.text:
Array(
    dtype: ScalarType,
    shape: tuple[int, ...],
    buffer: DeviceBuffer,
    writable: bool = True,
    device=None,
)

An n-dimensional array of scalar, vector or matrix elements on a device.

shape counts elements and dtype describes one element, so an array of shape (n,) and dtype vec3(f32) holds 3 * n scalars and downloads as (n, 3).

layout says how a vector or matrix array stores its components: "aos" (the default) interleaves them in one buffer, "soa" keeps one scalar array per component (SoaArray). An array of scalars says "aos".

def __init__(self, dtype: ScalarType, shape: tuple[int, ...], buffer: DeviceBuffer,
             writable: bool = True, device=None):
    self._dtype = dtype
    self._shape = tuple(shape)
    self._buffer = buffer
    self._writable = writable
    # The backend that made the buffer. Every Tack constructor says; an
    # array built without one takes the default device when asked.
    self._device = device

def numpy(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """Copy the values into a new NumPy array.

    Vector and matrix components become trailing NumPy dimensions: an
    array of shape ``(n,)`` and dtype ``vec3(f32)`` gives ``(n, 3)``.
    """
    arr = self._buffer.to_numpy()
    # The buffer keeps the shape it was allocated with, so a reshaped
    # view has to impose its own -- the same data either way.
    if arr.shape != self._host_shape:
        arr = arr.reshape(self._host_shape)
    return arr

Set every element to value.

A vector or matrix array also takes one element's value, a sequence of its components: colors.fill([1.0, 1.0, 1.0]).

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def fill(self, value):
    """Set every element to ``value``.

    A vector or matrix array also takes one element's value, a sequence
    of its components: ``colors.fill([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])``.
    """
    self._check_writable()
    if np.ndim(value) == 0:
        if not self._backend.fill_array(self, value):
            self._buffer.fill(value)
        return
    vector_shape = self._vector_shape()
    element = np.asarray(value)
    if vector_shape is None:
        raise TypeError(
            f"fill() takes a scalar for an array of scalars, "
            f"got a value of shape {element.shape}")
    element_shape = vector_shape[len(self._logical_shape):]
    if element.shape != element_shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"fill() value has shape {element.shape}; "
            f"the elements of this array have shape {element_shape}")
    from tack.runtime.device_fill import element_pattern
    if not self._buffer.fill_bytes(element_pattern(element, self.scalar_dtype.numpy_dtype)):
        self._upload(np.broadcast_to(element.astype(self.scalar_dtype.numpy_dtype),
                                     vector_shape))

Export this array as a DLPack capsule for zero-copy interop.

Usage

torch_tensor = torch.from_dlpack(tack_array) cupy_array = cupy.from_dlpack(tack_array) np_array = np.from_dlpack(tack_array) # numpy 1.25+

A consumer passing max_version >= (1, 0) gets a versioned capsule, which is the only form that can carry the read-only flag. Without it the consumer must assume the memory is writable, so NumPy marks what it gets read-only and then cannot re-export it -- which breaks round trips through anything that hands the array back.

def __dlpack__(self, *, stream=None, max_version=None, dl_device=None, copy=None):
    """Export this array as a DLPack capsule for zero-copy interop.

    Usage:
        torch_tensor = torch.from_dlpack(tack_array)
        cupy_array = cupy.from_dlpack(tack_array)
        np_array = np.from_dlpack(tack_array)  # numpy 1.25+

    A consumer passing max_version >= (1, 0) gets a versioned capsule,
    which is the only form that can carry the read-only flag. Without
    it the consumer must assume the memory is writable, so NumPy marks
    what it gets read-only and then cannot re-export it -- which breaks
    round trips through anything that hands the array back.
    """
    from tack.lang.dlpack import array_to_dlpack
    if copy is True:
        raise BufferError("Tack DLPack export does not support copy=True")
    versioned = max_version is not None and max_version[0] >= 1
    return array_to_dlpack(self, versioned=versioned)

docs.text:
__getitem__(index)

Read one element from the host: a[i], a[i, j], or a[()] for a zero-dimensional array.

An array of scalars gives a Python number; a vector or matrix array gives a NumPy array of the element. Negative indices count from the end, as in Python. This is for inspection and for host-side decisions: on backends without host-visible memory each read is a transfer of that element, so many elements are read with numpy(). Arrays are not written this way; see tack.copyto and fill.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def __getitem__(self, index):
    """Read one element from the host: ``a[i]``, ``a[i, j]``, or ``a[()]`` for a
    zero-dimensional array.

    An array of scalars gives a Python number; a vector or matrix array
    gives a NumPy array of the element. Negative indices count from
    the end, as in Python. This is for inspection and for host-side
    decisions: on backends without host-visible memory each read is a
    transfer of that element, so many elements are read with
    ``numpy()``. Arrays are not written this way; see ``tack.copyto``
    and ``fill``.
    """
    shape = self.shape
    indices = index if isinstance(index, tuple) else (index,)
    if len(indices) != len(shape) or not all(
            isinstance(i, (int, np.integer)) and not isinstance(i, bool) for i in indices):
        if not shape:
            wanted = "a[()]"
        elif len(shape) == 1:
            wanted = "one integer index"
        else:
            wanted = f"{len(shape)} integer indices"
        raise TypeError(
            f"an array of shape {shape} takes {wanted} on the host, not {index!r}; "
            f"to read many elements use numpy()")
    flat = 0
    for i, extent in zip(indices, shape, strict=True):
        i = int(i)
        if not -extent <= i < extent:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index!r} is out of range for an array of shape {shape}")
        flat = flat * extent + (i + extent if i < 0 else i)
    vector_shape = self._vector_shape()
    if vector_shape is None:
        return self._buffer.read_range(flat, 1)[0].item()
    element_shape = vector_shape[len(shape):]
    count = int(math.prod(element_shape))
    return self._buffer.read_range(flat * count, count).reshape(element_shape)

    """Copy with a new component type or a matching vector/matrix dtype.

    A scalar dtype changes the component type while preserving the element
    dimensions. An element dtype must have those same dimensions.

    if isinstance(dtype, ElementType):
        if element_shape is None or dtype.shape != element_shape[len(self._logical_shape):]:
            raise TypeError("astype cannot change an element's component dimensions")

    from tack.algorithms.copy import copy as _copy
    _copy(self._scalar_view(), out._scalar_view(), self.scalar_size)
    return out

docs.text:
reshape(*shape) -> Array

Share storage under a new shape, preserving the element type.

Takes the shape as a tuple or as separate integers, as NumPy does; one dimension may be -1, inferred from the size.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def reshape(self, *shape) -> 'Array':
    """Share storage under a new shape, preserving the element type.

    Takes the shape as a tuple or as separate integers, as NumPy does;
    one dimension may be ``-1``, inferred from the size.
    """
    if len(shape) == 1 and not isinstance(shape[0], (int, np.integer)):
        shape = shape[0]
    new_shape = list(_array_shape(shape, allow_infer=True))
    if new_shape.count(-1) > 1:
        raise ValueError("reshape can infer at most one dimension")
    if -1 in new_shape:
        known = int(math.prod([n for n in new_shape if n != -1]))
        if known == 0 or self.size % known:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot reshape {self.shape} ({self.size} elements) "
                             f"to {tuple(shape)}")
        new_shape[new_shape.index(-1)] = self.size // known
    new_shape = tuple(new_shape)
    new_size = int(math.prod(new_shape))
    if new_size != self.size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot reshape {self.shape} ({self.size} elements) "
            f"to {new_shape} ({new_size} elements)")
    reshaped = _array_view(self.dtype, new_shape, self._buffer, self._writable,
                           self._device)
    hold = getattr(self, '_dlpack_hold', None)
    if hold is not None:
        reshaped._dlpack_hold = hold
    return reshaped

def empty(shape, dtype=None, *, device=None, exportable=False, layout="aos") -> Array:
    """A new array of uninitialized scalar, vector or matrix elements.

    ``shape`` counts elements; ``dtype`` describes one element, by default the
    default float type (f32 unless `set_default_float` changed it). A vector
    array of shape ``(n,)`` and dtype ``vec3(f32)`` downloads as ``(n, 3)``.
    Initialize its values with a kernel, ``fill`` or ``tack.copyto`` before
    reading. ``device`` is a `tack.Device` or a spec such as ``"cuda"``; by
    default the default device. ``layout="soa"`` stores a vector or matrix
    array's components in one array each (see `SoaArray`).
    """
    backend = _target(device)
    shape = _array_shape(shape)
    dtype = get_default_float() if dtype is None else as_dtype(dtype)
    if _check_layout(layout, dtype):
        return SoaArray(tuple(empty(shape, dtype.scalar_dtype, device=backend,
                                    exportable=exportable) for _ in range(dtype.size)),
                        dtype.shape)
    scalar = dtype.scalar_dtype if isinstance(dtype, ElementType) else dtype
    _check_dtype(backend, scalar)
    storage = (int(math.prod(shape)) * dtype.size,) if isinstance(dtype, ElementType) else shape
    buffer = _allocate(backend, scalar, storage, exportable=exportable)
    return _array_view(dtype, shape, buffer, device=backend)

set_default_float(dtype) -> ScalarType

Make dtype (tack.f32 or tack.f64, or a NumPy float type) the floating-point type arrays get when nothing chooses one, and return it.

It is what tack.empty, zeros and ones allocate without a dtype, what Python floats become in tack.array, full and arange, the component type of tack.vec3() and the other vector and matrix types without one, and the float type of implicit arrays and of tack.dataset's constructors and readers. A NumPy array keeps its own type, and kernels are unchanged: their precision follows the arrays they are given. Process-wide, as the default device is; arrays already made keep their type. Metal has no f64, so with f64 there, an array made without a dtype raises TypeError.

def set_default_float(dtype) -> ScalarType:
    """Make ``dtype`` (``tack.f32`` or ``tack.f64``, or a NumPy float type) the
    floating-point type arrays get when nothing chooses one, and return it.

    It is what ``tack.empty``, ``zeros`` and ``ones`` allocate without a
    ``dtype``, what Python floats become in ``tack.array``, ``full`` and
    ``arange``, the component type of ``tack.vec3()`` and the other vector and
    matrix types without one, and the float type of implicit arrays and of
    ``tack.dataset``'s constructors and readers. A NumPy array keeps its own
    type, and kernels are unchanged: their precision follows the arrays they
    are given. Process-wide, as the default device is; arrays already made keep
    their type. Metal has no f64, so with ``f64`` there, an array made without
    a ``dtype`` raises ``TypeError``.
    """
    global _default_float
    dtype = as_dtype(dtype)
    if dtype not in (f32, f64):
        raise TypeError(f"the default float type is tack.f32 or tack.f64, not {dtype}")
    _default_float = dtype
    return dtype

array(
    obj, dtype=None, *, device=None, layout=None
) -> Array

A new array holding a copy of obj: a NumPy array, a sequence or a Tack array.

Without dtype, all of obj's dimensions are array dimensions, a NumPy array keeps its dtype, and Python floats and ints become the default float type (f32 unless set_default_float changed it) and i32 (i64 if a value needs it). With an element dtype such as vec3(f32), the trailing dimensions are the elements' components. A Tack array is copied on its device unless device names another. layout is "aos" or "soa" for a vector or matrix array (see SoaArray); by default a Tack array keeps its own and other data is interleaved.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def array(obj, dtype=None, *, device=None, layout=None) -> Array:
    """A new array holding a copy of ``obj``: a NumPy array, a sequence or a Tack array.

    Without ``dtype``, all of ``obj``'s dimensions are array dimensions, a
    NumPy array keeps its dtype, and Python floats and ints become the default
    float type (f32 unless `set_default_float` changed it) and i32 (i64 if a
    value needs it). With an element dtype such as
    ``vec3(f32)``, the trailing dimensions are the elements' components.
    A Tack array is copied on its device unless ``device`` names another.
    ``layout`` is ``"aos"`` or ``"soa"`` for a vector or matrix array (see
    `SoaArray`); by default a Tack array keeps its own and other data is
    interleaved.
    """
    if isinstance(obj, Array):
        if layout is not None and layout != obj.layout:
            if device is not None:
                obj = obj.to_device(device)
            out = empty(obj.shape, obj.dtype if dtype is None else dtype,
                        device=obj._backend, layout=layout)
            copyto(out, obj)
            return out
        if device is not None and _target(device).memory_domain != obj._backend.memory_domain:
            moved = obj.to_device(device)
            return moved if dtype is None else moved.astype(dtype)
        return obj.copy() if dtype is None else obj.astype(dtype)
    host = np.asarray(obj)
    dtype = _host_dtype(host, obj) if dtype is None else as_dtype(dtype)
    shape = host.shape
    if isinstance(dtype, ElementType):
        rank = len(dtype.shape)
        if len(shape) < rank or shape[-rank:] != dtype.shape:
            raise ValueError(f"input shape {shape} must end with element shape {dtype.shape}")
        shape = shape[:-rank]
    out = empty(shape, dtype, device=device, layout=layout or "aos")
    out._upload(host.astype(out.scalar_dtype.numpy_dtype, copy=False))
    return out

def asarray(obj, dtype=None, *, device=None, layout=None) -> Array:
    """``obj`` itself if it is a Tack array of ``dtype`` (or any, without one)
    on ``device`` (or any, without one) in ``layout`` (or either, without one),
    else `array(obj, dtype, device=device, layout=layout)`."""
    if isinstance(obj, Array):
        if layout is not None and layout != obj.layout:
            return array(obj, dtype, device=device, layout=layout)
        if device is not None:
            obj = obj.to_device(device)
        if dtype is None or as_dtype(dtype) == obj.dtype:
            return obj
        return obj.astype(dtype)
    return array(obj, dtype, device=device, layout=layout)

def arange(start, stop=None, step=1, dtype=None, *, device=None) -> Array:
    """Evenly spaced values in ``[start, stop)``, as ``np.arange``.

    Without ``dtype``, integer arguments give i32 (i64 if a value needs it)
    and any float argument gives the default float type (`get_default_float`).
    """
    if stop is None:
        start, stop = 0, start
    values = np.arange(start, stop, step)
    if dtype is None:
        dtype = _host_dtype(values, [start, stop, step])
        if values.size == 0 and values.dtype.kind in 'iu':
            dtype = i32 if all(integer_type_for_value(int(v)) is i32 for v in (start, stop)) else i64
    return array(values, dtype, device=device)

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def concat(arrays) -> Array:
    """Join a sequence of arrays end to end into a new one-dimensional array.

    All arrays must have the same dtype and be on one device, where the copy
    runs.
    """
    arrays = list(arrays)
    if not arrays:
        raise ValueError("concat requires at least one array")
    dt = arrays[0].dtype
    for a in arrays[1:]:
        if a.dtype != dt:
            raise TypeError(
                f"concat: all arrays must have the same dtype, got {dt} and {a.dtype}")
    from tack.runtime.dispatch import same_device
    same_device("concat()", arrays)
    total = sum(a.size for a in arrays)
    result = empty((total,), dt, device=arrays[0]._backend)
    from tack.algorithms.copy import copy_with_offset
    offset = 0
    for a in arrays:
        copy_with_offset(a, result, offset, a.size)
        offset += a.size
    return result

A vector array whose components are the given arrays, without copying.

tack.soa(x, y, z) is an array of vec3 elements whose element i is (x[i], y[i], z[i]): the structure-of-arrays layout, for data that arrives that way, such as a simulation's coordinate arrays or another library's tensors (from_dlpack, array_from_ptr). Kernels read and write it as they do any vector array, and writes go to the component arrays. The components are arrays of scalars of one dtype and one shape, on one device. An element dtype of the same component type makes a matrix array instead, components row-major: tack.soa(a, b, c, d, dtype=tack.mat2()).

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def soa(*components, dtype=None) -> SoaArray:
    """A vector array whose components are the given arrays, without copying.

    ``tack.soa(x, y, z)`` is an array of ``vec3`` elements whose element
    ``i`` is ``(x[i], y[i], z[i])``: the structure-of-arrays layout, for
    data that arrives that way, such as a simulation's coordinate arrays
    or another library's tensors (``from_dlpack``, ``array_from_ptr``).
    Kernels read and write it as they do any vector array, and writes go
    to the component arrays. The components are arrays of scalars of one
    dtype and one shape, on one device. An element ``dtype`` of the same
    component type makes a matrix array instead, components row-major:
    ``tack.soa(a, b, c, d, dtype=tack.mat2())``.
    """
    if len(components) == 1 and isinstance(components[0], (list, tuple)):
        components = tuple(components[0])
    if not components:
        raise TypeError("soa() takes the component arrays, at least one")
    for c in components:
        if not isinstance(c, Array):
            raise TypeError(f"soa() takes Tack arrays, not {type(c).__name__}; make one "
                            f"with tack.array(), tack.from_dlpack() or tack.array_from_ptr()")
        if hasattr(c, '_vector_n'):
            raise TypeError(f"soa() takes arrays of scalars, one per component, "
                            f"not an array of {c.dtype}")
    first = components[0]
    for c in components[1:]:
        if c.scalar_dtype is not first.scalar_dtype or c.shape != first.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"soa() components must share a dtype and a shape; got {first.dtype} "
                f"{first.shape} and {c.dtype} {c.shape}")
    from tack.runtime.dispatch import same_device
    same_device("soa()", components)
    if dtype is None:
        element = vec(len(components), first.scalar_dtype)
    else:
        element = as_dtype(dtype)
        if not isinstance(element, ElementType) or element.size != len(components):
            raise TypeError(f"soa() was given {len(components)} components; dtype must be "
                            f"a vector or matrix of {len(components)}, not {element}")
        if element.scalar_dtype is not first.scalar_dtype:
            raise TypeError(f"soa() components are {first.scalar_dtype}; dtype {element} "
                            f"has {element.scalar_dtype} components")
    return SoaArray(components, element.shape)

A vector or matrix array stored as one scalar array per component.

Made by soa from arrays that exist already (from another library, through from_dlpack or array_from_ptr), or by a constructor given layout="soa". It is an Array like any other: a kernel reads a[i] as a vector, stores, updates and atomically updates it, and only the generated code differs, reading component c of element i from a.components[c][i] rather than from i * n + c of one buffer. A kernel compiled for one layout is not used for the other.

With no single buffer, an SOA array is not exported whole (DLPack, export_memory); its components are.

def numpy(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """Copy the values into a new NumPy array, components as the trailing
    dimensions, exactly as for an interleaved array."""

        self._host_shape)

Copy src into the existing array dst, as np.copyto does.

src is host data -- a NumPy array, a sequence or a scalar -- whose shape is dst.numpy()'s or broadcasts to it, converted to dst's dtype; or a Tack array of dst's shape on dst's device, copied there (src.to_device(dst.device) brings one from another device).

It only writes into Tack arrays. numpy reads one into a new NumPy array; np.copyto copies between NumPy arrays.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def copyto(dst: Array, src):
    """Copy ``src`` into the existing array ``dst``, as ``np.copyto`` does.

    ``src`` is host data -- a NumPy array, a sequence or a scalar -- whose
    shape is ``dst.numpy()``'s or broadcasts to it, converted to ``dst``'s
    dtype; or a Tack array of ``dst``'s shape on ``dst``'s device, copied
    there (``src.to_device(dst.device)`` brings one from another device).

    It only writes into Tack arrays. `numpy` reads one into a new NumPy
    array; ``np.copyto`` copies between NumPy arrays.
    """
    if not isinstance(dst, Array):
        raise TypeError(f"copyto() writes into a Tack array, not {type(dst).__name__}")
    if isinstance(src, Array):
        if src.shape != dst.shape or src.scalar_size != dst.scalar_size:
            raise ValueError(f"copyto() from an array of shape {src.shape} and dtype "
                             f"{src.dtype} into one of shape {dst.shape} and dtype {dst.dtype}")
        from tack.runtime.dispatch import same_device
        same_device("copyto()", (dst, src))
        dst._check_writable()
        from tack.algorithms.copy import copy as _copy
        if src.layout == dst.layout == "aos":
            _copy(src._scalar_view(), dst._scalar_view(), dst.scalar_size)
            return
        # An SOA array has no one buffer: copy element by element, which
        # reads and writes either layout.
        if getattr(src.dtype, 'shape', None) != getattr(dst.dtype, 'shape', None):
            raise ValueError(f"copyto() from an array of {src.dtype} elements into one "
                             f"of {dst.dtype} elements")
        _copy(src.reshape(src.size), dst.reshape(dst.size), dst.size)
        return
    host = np.asarray(src, dtype=dst.scalar_dtype.numpy_dtype)
    expected = dst._host_shape
    if host.shape != expected:
        try:
            host = np.broadcast_to(host, expected)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"copyto() into an array whose values have shape {expected}: "
                             f"cannot broadcast shape {host.shape}") from None
    dst._upload(host)

def __init__(self, x, y=(0.0,), z=(0.0,), dtype=None, device=None):
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    if device is None:      # host axes go where the device axes are
        device = next((a._device for a in (x, y, z) if isinstance(a, _DeviceArray)), None)
    self.xs, self.ys, self.zs = (self._axis(a, dtype, device) for a in (x, y, z))
    self.dims = (self.xs.shape[0], self.ys.shape[0], self.zs.shape[0])
    self.px, self.py = self.dims[0], self.dims[1]

def __init__(self, dims, origin=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), spacing=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), direction=None,
             dtype=None, device=None):
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    dims = tuple(int(d) for d in dims)
    if not 1 <= len(dims) <= 3:
        raise ValueError(f"an image has one to three sizes, not {dims!r}")
    dims += (1,) * (3 - len(dims))
    self.dims = dims
    self.px, self.py = dims[0], dims[1]
    origin, spacing = _three(origin, 0.0, "origin"), _three(spacing, 1.0, "spacing")
    self.ox, self.oy, self.oz = origin
    self.sx, self.sy, self.sz = spacing
    matrix = np.eye(3)
    if direction is not None:
        given = np.asarray(direction, float)
        if given.shape == (2, 2):
            matrix[:2, :2] = given
        elif given.size == 9:
            matrix = given.reshape(3, 3)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"direction is a 3 x 3 matrix, or 2 x 2 for a 2D image, not "
                             f"{given.shape}")
    if direction is not None and not np.allclose(matrix, np.eye(3)):
        self.ORIENTED = 1
    # Always present, so an f64 grid's scalars are f64 in the kernel; it
    # puts the grid on ``device`` (by default the default device).
    self.direction = _store(matrix.reshape(-1), dtype, device)
    self._origin, self._spacing, self._matrix = origin, spacing, matrix
    _metadata(self, math.prod(dims), 3, dtype)

def Concatenate(*arrays):
    """The arrays end to end, as VTK's composite array: of one width and type."""
    if not arrays:
        raise ValueError("Concatenate needs at least one array")
    parts = _operands(*arrays)
    for part in parts[1:]:
        if (width_of(part), dtype_of(part)) != (width_of(parts[0]), dtype_of(parts[0])):
            raise TypeError("concatenated arrays must have one width and one type")
    joined = parts[0]
    for part in parts[1:]:
        joined = _Concatenation(joined, part)
    return joined

def Components(*arrays):
    """Two to four scalar arrays as the components of a vector array, as Viskores'
    composite vector."""
    parts = _operands(*arrays)
    if not 2 <= len(parts) <= 4 or any(width_of(p) for p in parts):
        raise TypeError("Components takes two to four scalar arrays")
    if len({size_of(p) for p in parts}) != 1:
        raise ValueError("the component arrays differ in size")
    if len({dtype_of(p) for p in parts}) != 1:
        raise TypeError("the component arrays differ in type: Cast them to one")
    out = {2: _Components2, 3: _Components3, 4: _Components4}[len(parts)]()
    for c, part in enumerate(parts):
        setattr(out, f"c{c}", part)
    _metadata(out, size_of(parts[0]), len(parts), dtype_of(parts[0]))
    return out

def materialize(values):
    """``values`` as a device array: itself if it is one, else computed by a kernel."""

def texture3d(source_array, shape=None, interp='linear'):
    """Create a 3D texture from an array for hardware-accelerated sampling.

    The texture copies the array's data now. Later writes to the array --
    kernel stores, ``from_numpy``, external or DLPack writes -- are not
    visible to it until ``tex.update()`` copies the array again. That holds
    on every backend, including CPU.

    Args:
        source_array: A Tack array with f32 dtype holding W*H*D elements,
               x varying fastest.
        shape: (W, H, D) tuple for the 3D dimensions.  If the array's shape
               is already 3D, this can be omitted.
        interp: Interpolation mode. Only 'linear' (the default) is
               implemented.
    """
    if shape is None:
        shape = source_array.shape
    if len(shape) != 3:
        raise ValueError("texture3d requires a 3D shape")
    return Texture3D(source_array, shape_3d=shape, interp=interp)

docs.title: tack.lang.array.Texture3D
docs.text:
Texture3D(
    source_array: Array,
    shape_3d: tuple,
    interp: str = "linear",
)

A 3D texture over a snapshot of an array, sampled trilinearly.

Created via tack.texture3d(array, shape=(W, H, D)). In kernels, tex.sample(u, v, w) samples at normalized [0,1] coordinates using trilinear interpolation.

The texture copies the array's data when it is created, and again on update(); writes to the array in between do not reach it. That holds on every backend. Where the backend samples in hardware the copy is a texture image (a CUDA or HIP array, an MTLTexture, a Level Zero image); elsewhere it is a private array the generated code interpolates in software. Either way the texture owns it, so it is released with the texture and no other texture can be handed it.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/array.py 
def __init__(self, source_array: Array, shape_3d: tuple, interp: str = 'linear'):
    # Every hardware path builds a single-channel 32-bit float image,
    # so f64 data would be reinterpreted rather than converted.
    if source_array.dtype is not f32:
        raise ValueError(
            f"texture3d requires an f32 array, got {source_array.dtype}; "
            f"convert it first with array.astype(tack.f32)")
    # The generated code interpolates linearly on every backend; nothing
    # implements another mode.
    if interp != 'linear':
        raise ValueError(
            f"texture3d supports interp='linear' only, got {interp!r}")
    shape_3d = tuple(int(s) for s in shape_3d)
    W, H, D = shape_3d
    if W * H * D != source_array.size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"texture3d shape {shape_3d} holds {W * H * D} elements, but "
            f"the array has {source_array.size} elements")
    self.array = source_array
    self.shape_3d = shape_3d   # (W, H, D) logical 3D shape
    self.interp = interp

    # The texture lives where its array does, and kernels sampling it run
    # there (``dispatch.launch_backend`` reads ``_device``).
    backend = self._device = source_array._backend
    if backend.texture_in_hardware(shape_3d):
        self._storage = backend.create_texture_image(shape_3d)
    else:
        self._storage = Array(f32, (source_array.size,),
                              _allocate(backend, f32, (source_array.size,)),
                              device=backend)
    self.update()

def update(self):
    """Copy the array's current data into the texture.

    Sampling after this sees the array as it is now, on every backend.
    """
    if isinstance(self._storage, Array):
        from tack.algorithms.copy import copy as _copy
        _copy(self.array.reshape((self.array.size,)), self._storage,
              self.array.size)
    else:
        self._storage.upload(self.array)

def array_from_ptr(ptr, shape, dtype, *, device=None, writable: bool = False) -> Array:
    """Wrap existing device memory as a Tack array without copying.

    Use this for interop with external libraries (pycuda, cupy, Catalyst)
    or when receiving a device pointer from a simulation framework.

    The array does NOT own the memory — Tack will not free it.
    Read-only by default; pass writable=True to enable writes.

    Raises ValueError if the pointer's memory space does not match the
    active backend (e.g. a CPU pointer with the CUDA backend), and
    TypeError if a CUDA, HIP or Level Zero pointer is not an address.

    Args:
        ptr: device pointer (integer) or backend-specific buffer object.
             - CPU: integer address or numpy array
             - Metal: MTLBuffer object (from PyObjC), or a NumPy array of
               host memory: a buffer Tack handed out, or memory on whole
               pages, wrapped in place (TypeError otherwise)
             - CUDA/HIP: device pointer as integer
             - Level Zero: device pointer as integer
        shape: the array's dimensions, counting elements
        dtype: scalar or element type (tack.f32, tack.vec3(), np.int32, ...)
        device: the device whose memory this is; by default the default device
        writable: if False (default), copyto() and fill() raise errors

    Returns:
        An Array wrapping the external memory.
    """
    from tack.runtime.kernel_utils import as_address

    shape = _array_shape(shape)
    dtype = as_dtype(dtype)
    if isinstance(dtype, ElementType):
        scalar = dtype.scalar_dtype
        storage = (int(math.prod(shape)) * dtype.size,)
    else:
        scalar, storage = dtype, shape
    backend = _target(device)
    _check_dtype(backend, scalar)

    # Validate the pointer's memory space against what this backend expects,
    # on backends that distinguish device memory; Metal MTLBuffer objects
    # and CPU numpy arrays are not addresses and need no check. Any form a
    # device pointer arrives in -- int, numpy integer, CUdeviceptr -- is
    # checked, not only a Python int.
    if backend.device_memory_spaces:
        if as_address(ptr) is None:
            raise TypeError(
                f"array_from_ptr() on the {backend.label} backend takes a "
                f"device address (an integer, or an object int() accepts), "
                f"not {type(ptr).__name__}.")
        space = backend.memory_space(ptr)
        if space not in backend.device_memory_spaces:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Pointer is in '{space}' memory but the device is "
                f"'{backend.label}'. array_from_ptr() requires a device "
                f"pointer. Use tack.array() to copy host data to the device.")

    buf = backend.wrap_ptr(ptr, scalar, storage)
    return _array_view(dtype, shape, buf, writable=writable, device=backend)

A Tack array from a DLPack capsule or any object with __dlpack__.

Zero-copy: the array shares memory with the source, and the source is held alive for as long as the array lives. Works for device tensors as well as host ones. device must be able to wrap the tensor; by default the array goes on the default device when that can, else on the tensor's own device, as the array API's from_dlpack does.

Wrap, not address: the Metal backend reads host memory perfectly well but cannot turn a host pointer into the MTLBuffer an array needs, so with Metal as the default a host tensor becomes a CPU array, and device="metal" refuses it and says so. Pass copy=True for an independent array instead.

Usage

a = tack.from_dlpack(torch_tensor) a = tack.from_dlpack(cupy_array) a = tack.from_dlpack(numpy_array) a = tack.from_dlpack(vtk_capsule)

def from_dlpack(x, *, device=None, copy: bool = False) -> Array:
    """A Tack array from a DLPack capsule or any object with ``__dlpack__``.

    Zero-copy: the array shares memory with the source, and the source is
    held alive for as long as the array lives. Works for device tensors as
    well as host ones. ``device`` must be able to wrap the tensor; by
    default the array goes on the default device when that can, else on the
    tensor's own device, as the array API's ``from_dlpack`` does.

    Wrap, not address: the Metal backend reads host memory perfectly well
    but cannot turn a host pointer into the MTLBuffer an array needs, so
    with Metal as the default a host tensor becomes a CPU array, and
    ``device="metal"`` refuses it and says so. Pass ``copy=True`` for an
    independent array instead.

    Usage:
        a = tack.from_dlpack(torch_tensor)
        a = tack.from_dlpack(cupy_array)
        a = tack.from_dlpack(numpy_array)
        a = tack.from_dlpack(vtk_capsule)
    """
    if copy:
        host = x if isinstance(x, np.ndarray) else np.from_dlpack(x)
        return array(host, device=device)

    from tack.lang.dlpack import dlpack_to_array
    return dlpack_to_array(x, device=device)

With versioned, produces a v1.0 DLManagedTensorVersioned in a 'dltensor_versioned' capsule; otherwise the legacy DLManagedTensor in a 'dltensor' one. Only the versioned form can carry the read-only flag, so a non-writable array exported the legacy way arrives as writable -- the legacy protocol simply has no way to say otherwise.

def array_to_dlpack(array, versioned=False):
    """Create a DLPack capsule from a Tack array.

    With `versioned`, produces a v1.0 DLManagedTensorVersioned in a
    'dltensor_versioned' capsule; otherwise the legacy DLManagedTensor in
    a 'dltensor' one. Only the versioned form can carry the read-only
    flag, so a non-writable array exported the legacy way arrives as
    writable -- the legacy protocol simply has no way to say otherwise.
    """
    device_type, device_id, data_ptr = _get_device_info(array)

    dl_dtype = _DTYPE_TO_DLPACK.get(array.scalar_dtype)
    if dl_dtype is None:
        raise TypeError(f"DLPack does not support dtype: {array.dtype}")
    code, bits, lanes = dl_dtype

    shape = array._host_shape
    ndim = len(shape)
    shape_arr = (ctypes.c_int64 * ndim)(*shape)

    # Contiguous C-order strides (in elements, not bytes)
    strides_arr = (ctypes.c_int64 * ndim)()
    stride = 1
    for i in range(ndim - 1, -1, -1):
        strides_arr[i] = stride
        stride *= shape[i]

    if versioned:
        managed = DLManagedTensorVersioned()
        managed.version = DLPackVersion(major=1, minor=0)
        managed.flags = 0 if array._writable else DLPACK_FLAG_BITMASK_READ_ONLY
        capsule_name = b"dltensor_versioned"
        deleter = _dlpack_deleter_versioned
    else:
        managed = DLManagedTensor()
        capsule_name = b"dltensor"
        deleter = _dlpack_deleter

    managed.dl_tensor.data = ctypes.c_void_p(data_ptr)
    managed.dl_tensor.device = DLDevice(device_type=device_type, device_id=device_id)
    managed.dl_tensor.ndim = ndim
    managed.dl_tensor.dtype = DLDataType(code=code, bits=bits, lanes=lanes)
    managed.dl_tensor.shape = shape_arr
    managed.dl_tensor.strides = strides_arr
    managed.dl_tensor.byte_offset = 0

    # The key travels in manager_ctx, which is the only thing the deleter
    # gets back. Pin everything the capsule points at under that key.
    key = next(_ctx_keys)
    managed.manager_ctx = ctypes.c_void_p(key)
    managed.deleter = _natively(deleter)
    _prevent_gc[key] = (array, managed, shape_arr, strides_arr)

    # addressof, not byref: byref yields a temporary whose lifetime is not
    # tied to the capsule. `managed` itself is kept alive by _prevent_gc.
    return _PyCapsule_New(
        ctypes.addressof(managed), capsule_name,
        ctypes.cast(_natively(_capsule_destructor), ctypes.c_void_p),
    )

dlpack_to_array(source, writable=True, device=None)

Wrap a DLPack tensor as a Tack array, without copying.

source may be a capsule or anything implementing __dlpack__ -- a CuPy array, a PyTorch tensor, a VTK array via vtkmodules.util.dlpack_support.

The tensor is held for as long as the array lives, so the source may be dropped immediately. The array does not copy, so the two share memory and a write through either is visible to the other.

device is where the array goes. By default it is the default device when that can wrap the tensor, else the tensor's own device, as the array API's from_dlpack keeps an array on its device: CUDA memory imported with the CPU as default is a CUDA array, not a copy.

Raises RuntimeError if device is given and cannot wrap the tensor -- CUDA memory imported onto the CPU device. Metal refuses host tensors for a different reason, and says which: it can read that memory, it just cannot make an MTLBuffer out of it.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/dlpack.py 
def dlpack_to_array(source, writable=True, device=None):
    """Wrap a DLPack tensor as a Tack array, without copying.

    `source` may be a capsule or anything implementing ``__dlpack__`` -- a
    CuPy array, a PyTorch tensor, a VTK array via
    ``vtkmodules.util.dlpack_support``.

    The tensor is held for as long as the array lives, so the source may be
    dropped immediately. The array does not copy, so the two share memory
    and a write through either is visible to the other.

    ``device`` is where the array goes. By default it is the default
    device when that can wrap the tensor, else the tensor's own device, as
    the array API's ``from_dlpack`` keeps an array on its device: CUDA
    memory imported with the CPU as default is a CUDA array, not a copy.

    Raises RuntimeError if ``device`` is given and cannot wrap the tensor --
    CUDA memory imported onto the CPU device. Metal refuses host tensors for
    a different reason, and says which: it can read that memory, it just
    cannot make an MTLBuffer out of it.
    """
    from tack.lang.array import _target, array_from_ptr
    from tack.runtime.dispatch import get_backend

    capsule = _request_capsule(source)

    capsule_ptr = ctypes.cast(id(capsule), ctypes.c_void_p)
    if _PyCapsule_IsValid(capsule_ptr, b"dltensor_versioned"):
        name, used_name = b"dltensor_versioned", b"used_dltensor_versioned"
        struct = DLManagedTensorVersioned
    elif _PyCapsule_IsValid(capsule_ptr, b"dltensor"):
        name, used_name = b"dltensor", b"used_dltensor"
        struct = DLManagedTensor
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "expected an unconsumed DLPack capsule; this one has already "
            "been taken by another consumer")

    managed_ptr = _PyCapsule_GetPointer(capsule_ptr, name)
    managed = ctypes.cast(managed_ptr, ctypes.POINTER(struct)).contents
    tensor = managed.dl_tensor

    if struct is DLManagedTensorVersioned and \
            managed.flags & DLPACK_FLAG_BITMASK_READ_ONLY:
        # The producer says this memory must not be written. Honour it rather
        # than handing back an array whose writes go somewhere unexpected.
        writable = False

    if not tensor.data:
        raise ValueError("the tensor has a null data pointer")

    dtype = _DLPACK_TO_DTYPE.get((tensor.dtype.code, tensor.dtype.bits))
    if dtype is None:
        raise TypeError(
            f"no Tack dtype for DLPack (code={tensor.dtype.code}, "
            f"bits={tensor.dtype.bits})")
    if tensor.dtype.lanes != 1:
        raise TypeError(
            f"vectorized DLPack dtypes are not supported (lanes={tensor.dtype.lanes})")

    shape = tuple(tensor.shape[i] for i in range(tensor.ndim))

    # Only C-contiguous tensors can be wrapped. Anything else would be read
    # with the wrong stride, which produces plausible-looking wrong numbers.
    if tensor.strides:
        expected, stride = [0] * tensor.ndim, 1
        for i in range(tensor.ndim - 1, -1, -1):
            expected[i] = stride
            stride *= shape[i]
        actual = [tensor.strides[i] for i in range(tensor.ndim)]
        if actual != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"only C-contiguous tensors can be wrapped without copying; "
                f"strides {tuple(actual)} != {tuple(expected)}")

    allowed = _DEVICE_BACKENDS.get(tensor.device.device_type)
    if tensor.device.device_type == kDLMetal:
        raise ValueError(
            "Metal DLPack tensors (kDLMetal) cannot be imported: Tack has "
            "no way yet to wrap the MTLBuffer handle they carry. Move the "
            "tensor to host memory in the producing library, then import "
            "it with copy=True.")
    if allowed is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unsupported DLPack device type {tensor.device.device_type}")
    where = (tensor.device.device_type, tensor.device.device_id)
    if device is not None:
        backend = _target(device)
    else:
        backend = get_backend()
        if not backend.addresses_dlpack(*where):
            backend = _tensor_device(allowed[0], tensor.device.device_id)
    if backend.name not in allowed and not backend.addresses_dlpack(*where):
        message = (
            f"the tensor is on a device the '{backend.name}' device cannot "
            f"wrap without copying (DLPack device type "
            f"{tensor.device.device_type}). Import it on its own device with "
            f"tack.from_dlpack(x, device='{allowed[0]}'), or pass copy=True.")
        if backend.dlpack_refusal_note:
            message += f" {backend.dlpack_refusal_note}"
        raise RuntimeError(message)

    array = array_from_ptr(
        (tensor.data or 0) + tensor.byte_offset, shape, dtype, device=backend,
        writable=writable)

    # Adopt the capsule: rename it so nobody else releases it, and attach the
    # hold to the array so the producer is told when the array is gone.
    _PyCapsule_SetName(capsule, used_name)
    array._dlpack_hold = _CapsuleHold(capsule, managed_ptr, struct)
    return array

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/kernel.py 
def __init__(self, func, funcdef=None):
    self.func = func
    if funcdef is None:
        self._source = textwrap.dedent(read_source(func, "kernel"))
        self._ast = ast.parse(self._source)
        tag_origin(self._ast, func)
        self._funcdef = self._ast.body[0]  # The FunctionDef node
    else:
        # A kernel derived from another's AST: the result epilogue below.
        self._source = ast.unparse(funcdef)
        self._ast = ast.Module(body=[funcdef], type_ignores=[])
        self._funcdef = funcdef
    self.name = self._funcdef.name
    # Lazy IR: defer transform until first dispatch (vector arrays may be needed)
    self._ir = None
    self._ir_cache = {}  # vector_arrays key → IRModule
    # A kernel ending in `return expr` has the expression computed by a
    # one-thread epilogue kernel into a hidden array; see _split_result.
    self._result = None if funcdef is not None else _split_result(self, func)
    # Per thread: each call stores its result there and reads it back,
    # so two threads sharing one array read each other's result.
    self._result_arrays = threading.local()

def get_ir(self, vector_arrays=None, template_args=None, texture_arrays=None, debug=False):
    """Get IR, re-transforming if vector/texture array or template metadata is provided.

    ``debug`` lowers with bounds checks (see ``ir_bounds``), cached apart.
    """
    if template_args:
        key = self._make_cache_key(vector_arrays, template_args, texture_arrays, debug)
        cached = self._ir_cache.get(key)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        with _transform_lock:
            # Re-check: another thread may have built it while we waited.
            if key not in self._ir_cache:
                self._ir_cache[key] = self._lower(vector_arrays, texture_arrays,
                                                  template_args, debug)
                for token in _key_tokens(key):
                    token.kernels.add(self)
            return self._ir_cache[key]
    if not vector_arrays and not texture_arrays and not debug:
        if self._ir is None:
            with _transform_lock:
                if self._ir is None:
                    self._ir = self._lower(None, None, None)
        return self._ir
    key = self._make_cache_key(vector_arrays, None, texture_arrays, debug)
    cached = self._ir_cache.get(key)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    with _transform_lock:
        if key not in self._ir_cache:
            self._ir_cache[key] = self._lower(vector_arrays, texture_arrays, None, debug)
        return self._ir_cache[key]

def device_class(cls):
    """Mark a class as a device class: its objects can be kernel arguments.

    Methods decorated with @tack.func are collected and made available
    for inlining when instances are passed to kernels.
    """
    from tack.lang.template_rewrite import template_func_methods

    cls._device_class = True
    # A record of the methods at decoration, inherited ones included.
    # Lowering looks them up again per class, so subclasses defined later,
    # decorated or not, get their own.
    cls._tack_func_methods = template_func_methods(cls)

    return cls

constant(value, dtype=None)

Declare a named constant that kernels and device functions may read.

DT = tack.constant(0.01) at module (or enclosing function) scope lets a kernel write DT as if it were the literal 0.01. Without dtype the constant behaves exactly like that literal: an integer takes the narrowest of i32, i64 and u64 that holds it, and a float is weak, taking the precision of what it meets. With dtype it has that type, as tack.u32(747796405) or tack.f64(0.1) written in the kernel would: tack.constant(747796405, tack.u32) multiplies in wrapping u32 arithmetic, and tack.constant(0.1, tack.f64) is the exact double.

The value is fixed here. A kernel reads the constant its name is bound to when the kernel is first compiled; binding the name to another constant afterwards does not change a compiled kernel, the same rule as for device functions.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/lang/constant.py 
def constant(value, dtype=None):
    """Declare a named constant that kernels and device functions may read.

    ``DT = tack.constant(0.01)`` at module (or enclosing function) scope
    lets a kernel write ``DT`` as if it were the literal ``0.01``. Without
    ``dtype`` the constant behaves exactly like that literal: an integer
    takes the narrowest of i32, i64 and u64 that holds it, and a float is
    weak, taking the precision of what it meets. With ``dtype`` it has that
    type, as ``tack.u32(747796405)`` or ``tack.f64(0.1)`` written in the
    kernel would: ``tack.constant(747796405, tack.u32)`` multiplies in
    wrapping u32 arithmetic, and ``tack.constant(0.1, tack.f64)`` is the
    exact double.

    The value is fixed here. A kernel reads the constant its name is bound
    to when the kernel is first compiled; binding the name to another
    constant afterwards does not change a compiled kernel, the same rule
    as for device functions.
    """
    if dtype is not None and not isinstance(dtype, ScalarType):
        raise TypeError(f"tack.constant dtype must be a Tack scalar type, not {dtype!r}")
    if isinstance(value, (tuple, list, np.ndarray)):
        return _array_constant(value, dtype)
    if isinstance(value, (bool, numbers.Integral)):
        value = int(value)
        if dtype is None or dtype in INTEGER_TYPES:
            _check_representable(value, dtype)
            return IntConstant(value, dtype)
        return FloatConstant(float(value), dtype)
    if isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
        if dtype in INTEGER_TYPES:
            raise TypeError(
                f"tack.constant({value!r}, {dtype!r}): an integer type needs an integer "
                f"value; convert it explicitly with int() if truncation is intended")
        return FloatConstant(float(value), dtype)
    raise TypeError(
        f"tack.constant takes an int, a float, or a tuple of them (a vector) or of "
        f"tuples (a matrix), not {type(value).__name__}; arrays and other objects are "
        f"passed to kernels as arguments")

docs.title: tack.math
docs.text:
Shader-style helpers as device functions: fract, mix, clamp...

GLSL, MSL and Taichi's taichi.math share a small vocabulary that graphics and simulation code reaches for constantly, and that Python's math lacks. These are ordinary @tack.func device functions, so they inline into kernels, and because Tack's arithmetic and builtins apply to each component of a vector, each one works on scalars and on vectors (and matrices) alike, as the GLSL functions do::

from tack import math as tm

@tack.kernel
def shade(uv, out, n):
    for i in range(n):
        st = tm.fract(uv[i] * 8.0) - 0.5          # a 2-vector
        edge = tm.smoothstep(0.0, 0.05, st.x)     # a scalar
        out[i] = tm.mix(DARK, LIGHT, edge)        # 3-vectors

The definitions are GLSL's, so mix(x, y, a) is x * (1 - a) + y * a, smoothstep is the Hermite polynomial on the clamped ratio, and step and sign select per component through tack.select. They are only callable from kernels and device functions; a NumPy reference writes the same one-liners with np.floor, np.clip and friends.

@tack.func
def smoothstep(edge0, edge1, x):
    """Hermite interpolation: 0 below ``edge0``, 1 above ``edge1``, smooth between.

    ``edge0`` greater than ``edge1`` reverses the step, as in GLSL.
    """
    t = min(max((x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0), 0.0), 1.0)
    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)

docs.title: tack.random
docs.text:
Random numbers in kernels, from a counter-based generator with explicit state.

Nothing here is hidden: a kernel seeds a u32 state from the element it works on and a stream number, and every draw returns the value and the next state. The sequence is a pure function of those integers, so the same program draws the same numbers on every backend and for any thread order, and a NumPy reference that calls the np_ mirrors below draws exactly the same ones::

from tack import random

@tack.kernel
def scatter(pos, n, frame):
    for i in range(n):
        state = random.seed(i, frame)        # element i of this frame
        u, state = random.uniform(state)     # f32 in [0, 1)
        z, state = random.normal(state)      # standard normal
        d, state = random.direction3(state)  # a unit 3-vector
        pos[i] = [u, z, d.x]

The generator is PCG's output permutation (RXS-M-XS on 32 bits) over a linear congruential step, in wrapping u32 arithmetic. uniform is the state's top 24 bits scaled, so it is exact and identical everywhere; normal and the directions go through log, sqrt, cos and sin, so they agree across backends to those functions' rounding. Taichi's ti.random() keeps hidden per-thread state instead; its results depend on the thread schedule and cannot be reproduced by a reference.

@tack.func
def advance(state):
    """The state after ``state``; also the 32 random bits it stands for."""
    x = tack.u32(state) * MULTIPLIER + INCREMENT
    word = ((x >> ((x >> S28) + S4)) ^ x) * MIX
    return (word >> S22) ^ word

@tack.func
def normal(state):
    """A standard normal draw (Box-Muller) and the next state; uses two states."""
    u1 = 1.0 - tack.f32(state >> S8) * SCALE              # in (0, 1], so log is finite
    state = advance(state)
    u2 = tack.f32(state >> S8) * SCALE
    return sqrt(-2.0 * log(u1)) * cos(TWO_PI * u2), advance(state)

@tack.func
def direction3(state):
    """A unit 3-vector uniformly distributed on the sphere, and the next state; two states."""
    a = TWO_PI * tack.f32(state >> S8) * SCALE
    state = advance(state)
    z = tack.f32(state >> S8) * SCALE * 2.0 - 1.0
    r = sqrt(1.0 - z * z)
    return tack.vec3(r * cos(a), r * sin(a), z), advance(state)

def inspect(kernel, *args, mode="source"):
    """Return generated code for a kernel without executing it.

    Args:
        kernel: A @tack.kernel decorated function.
        *args: The arguments the kernel would be called with.
        mode: What to return:
            "ir"        — Tack intermediate representation
            "source"    — backend-specific source code (MSL, CUDA C, LLVM IR, etc.)
            "optimized" — LLVM IR after O3; CPU only, since the GPU backends'
                          vendor compilers optimize past anything Tack sees

    Returns:
        The generated code as a string, for the device the call would run
        on (``dispatch.launch_backend``, as ``Kernel.__call__`` chooses): the
        default device if it can address the arrays, otherwise theirs.
    """
    from tack.lang.kernel import Kernel
    bound_to = getattr(kernel, '__self__', None)
    if bound_to is not None and isinstance(getattr(kernel, '__func__', None), Kernel):
        # A kernel method reached through its instance: model.step
        kernel, args = kernel.__func__, (bound_to, *args)
    if not isinstance(kernel, Kernel):
        raise TypeError(f"Expected a @tack.kernel, got {type(kernel).__name__}")

    from tack.runtime.dispatch import launch_backend
    backend = launch_backend(kernel.name, args)
    if not backend.supports_inspect:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"tack.inspect does not show kernels on the {backend.label} backend; "
            f"inspect '{kernel.name}' with arrays on another device")

    if mode == "ir":
        ir_func, _ = _prepare_ir(kernel, args, backend=backend)
        return ir.dump(ir_func)

    if mode == "source":
        return _generate_source(kernel, args)

    if mode == "optimized":
        return _generate_source(kernel, args, optimize=True)

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unknown inspect mode: '{mode}'. Use 'ir', 'source', or 'optimized'."
    )

Population variance of an array: Σ(x - mean)² / n.

Two passes over the first n elements: the mean by Array.sum(), then the squared differences, formed in the data's precision (f64 for f64 data, otherwise f32) and summed by Array.sum(). Returns a Python float; an empty range gives NaN, as Array.mean() does.

Source code in packages/tack-core/src/tack/algorithms/stats.py 
@on_inputs_device
def var(data, n=None):
    """Population variance of an array: Σ(x - mean)² / n.

    Two passes over the first n elements: the mean by ``Array.sum()``, then
    the squared differences, formed in the data's precision (f64 for f64
    data, otherwise f32) and summed by ``Array.sum()``. Returns a Python
    float; an empty range gives NaN, as ``Array.mean()`` does.
    """
    n, data = _count(n, data)
    if n == 0:
        return float('nan')
    if data.dtype in (tack.f32, tack.f64):
        mean_val = _prefix(data, n).sum() / n
    else:
        # An integer sum wraps (2^62 four times is 0): the values convert
        # first, as every other term does.
        mean_val = _terms(_converted, n, data).sum() / n
    terms = tack.empty((n,), _precision(data))
    _squared_diffs(data, mean_val, 1.0, terms, n)
    return terms.sum() / n

@on_inputs_device
def norm(data, ord=2, n=None):
    """Vector norm of an array, in the data's precision (f64 for f64 data,
    otherwise f32), as a Python float.

    ord=1: L1 norm (sum of absolute values)
    ord=2: L2 norm (Euclidean)
    ord=inf: L-infinity (max absolute value)

    Any other ord raises ValueError. An empty range gives 0.0.
    """
    if ord not in (1, 2, float('inf')):
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported norm order: {ord}")
    n, data = _count(n, data)
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0
    if ord == 1:
        return _terms(_abs_values, n, data).sum()
    if ord == 2:
        from math import sqrt
        return sqrt(_terms(_squares, n, data).sum())
    return _terms(_abs_values, n, data).max()

def count_nonzero(data, n=None):
    """The number of nonzero elements of an array, as a Python int: its 0/1 flags
    scanned into i64 on the device, so the count is exact past 2^31 and only
    the total comes back to the host."""

    if n == 0:

Values below the range are counted in the first bin and values above it in the last, unlike numpy.histogram, which drops them.

required bins

None n

@on_inputs_device
def histogram(data, bins=10, range=None, n=None):
    """Compute a histogram of array values with atomic bin counts.

    Values below the range are counted in the first bin and values above it
    in the last, unlike numpy.histogram, which drops them.

    Args:
        data: input array of any dtype
        bins: number of bins (at least 1)
        range: (min, max) tuple. If None, uses the minimum and maximum of
            the first n elements, and n must then be at least 1.
        n: number of elements (default: data.size)

    Returns:
        (counts, bin_edges) where counts is a Tack array of i32,
        bin_edges is a numpy array of (bins + 1) float64 edges.
    """
    import numpy as np
    n, data = _count(n, data)
    if int(bins) < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"histogram needs at least 1 bin, not {bins}")
    if range is None:
        if n == 0:
            raise ValueError("histogram of no elements needs an explicit range")
        head = _prefix(data, n)
        lo = float(head.min())
        hi = float(head.max())
        if not (np.isfinite(lo) and np.isfinite(hi)):
            # As numpy.histogram: bins cannot divide a range that is not finite.
            raise ValueError(f"autodetected range of [{lo}, {hi}] is not finite; "
                             "pass a finite range")
    else:
        lo, hi = float(range[0]), float(range[1])
        if not (np.isfinite(lo) and np.isfinite(hi)):
            raise ValueError(f"histogram range [{lo}, {hi}] is not finite")
        if lo > hi:
            raise ValueError(f"histogram range [{lo}, {hi}] has its minimum above its maximum")

    # Avoid division by zero for constant arrays
    if hi == lo:
        hi = lo + 1.0

    bin_width = (hi - lo) / bins
    inv_bw = 1.0 / bin_width

    counts = tack.empty((bins,), tack.i32)
    counts.fill(0)
    _histogram_kernel(data, counts, lo, inv_bw, bins, n)

    edges = np.linspace(lo, hi, bins + 1)
    return counts, edges

@on_inputs_device
def exclusive_scan(input_array, output_array, n, total=True, close=False):
    """Compute exclusive prefix sum on the inputs' device.

    output[i] = sum(input[0..i-1]), output[0] = 0.

    The scan runs in the output array's dtype; input values convert to it
    on the copy, so any dtype the backend allocates works.

    Args:
        input_array: array with input values.
        output_array: array for the output offsets.
        n: number of elements, at most either array's size. Zero writes
            nothing and returns 0.
        total: whether to return the total. Reading it waits for the
            device (on Metal, for every launch queued so far); a caller
            that needs only the offsets passes ``total=False`` and gets
            ``None``, and the scan stays queued.
        close: also write the total at ``output[n]``, so ``output`` is the
            ``n + 1`` offsets of CSR rows (``output[0]`` is 0 when ``n`` is
            0). In the scan's own launch where it is one, as for any array
            of at most a tile or 4096 elements; ``output`` needs ``n + 1``
            elements.

    Returns:
        The total of all input elements in the output's dtype, as a Python
        int or float; ``None`` with ``total=False``.
    """
    n = _count(n, input_array, output_array)
    if close and output_array.size < n + 1:
        raise ValueError(f"exclusive_scan with close writes output[{n}]: the output has "
                         f"{output_array.size} elements")
    if n == 0:
        # Nothing to scan; the empty sum is 0, as for Array.sum().
        if close:
            _close_empty(output_array)
        return 0 if total else None
    # Scan in the output's dtype, as the inclusive scan does: an i32 work
    # buffer truncated float inputs and wrapped wider integers.
    return _scan(input_array, output_array, n, inclusive=False, want_total=total, close=close)

Each segment's reduction: out[k] is the sum (op="min", "max", "mean": the least, the greatest, the sum over the count) of values[offsets[k]:offsets[k + 1]], for the size(offsets) - 1 segments, in values' element type (a vector's componentwise). An empty segment gets empty: by default 0 for a sum, NaN for a floating mean, and the type's greatest or least -- an infinity for floats -- for min and max; empty="keep" leaves its out as it is (a point with no cells keeps what the caller put there).

Floating sums group by chunks of 256 elements, the same on every backend and run; ordered=True sums each segment in element order, one thread a segment, as reduce_by_key does (a long segment is then one thread's loop). Integer sums wrap at the values' width; min and max are exact either way. Returns out (made if not given).
