@on_inputs_device
def jump(data, field):
    """A field's difference across each face at the face's center, side 1 minus side
    0 (zero on the boundary): a field on faces. Each side is the field as its own
    cell's basis has it at the face's center (the mean of the face's corners in
    the cell's reference element, the same point from both sides), so a DG
    field's jumps are its own, of any order, not its cells' averages; a
    continuous field's are zero. Up to order 1 the face's corner values
    (``traces``) give the center exactly; above it, the corners' linear mean was
    wrong, and each side's basis is evaluated there. Cell data (``Constant``, values on
    cells) is read from each side's cell directly, on any topology, polyhedral
    included."""
    field = _field(data, field)
    faces = data.topology.faces()
    out = _like(field.values, faces.num_faces)
    if _on_cells(data, field):
        for_each(_cell_jump, data, "faces", materialize(field.values), out)
    elif getattr(field.space, "order", 1) <= 1 or getattr(field.space, "varies", False):
        # Up to order 1 a side is linear over the face, so its corner values
        # (traces) give the center exactly -- on a pyramid's triangles too, whose
        # map from the reference is not affine.
        for_each(_trace_jump, data, "faces", traces(data, field), out)
    else:
        reference_cells(data.topology, "jump")
        sides = _like(field.values, 2 * faces.num_faces)
        if faces.num_faces:
            sides.fill(0)
        for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [field]):
            if group.count:
                _side_centers(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group), sides)
        for_each(_jump, data, "faces", sides, out)
    return Field(Values(data, "faces"), out, units.delta(field.unit))

upwind_flux(data, field, velocity)

The flux of field carried by a constant velocity through each face, out of side 0: (v . n) * area * u, u taken from the upwind side at the face's center -- the side the flow leaves -- as a DG advection scheme does. A boundary face takes its one side's value whichever way the flow goes. divergence of the result is each cell's net outflow.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/upwind_flux.py 
@on_inputs_device
def upwind_flux(data, field, velocity):
    """The flux of ``field`` carried by a constant ``velocity`` through each face, out
    of side 0: ``(v . n) * area * u``, ``u`` taken from the upwind side at the face's
    center -- the side the flow leaves -- as a DG advection scheme does. A boundary
    face takes its one side's value whichever way the flow goes. ``divergence`` of
    the result is each cell's net outflow."""
    field = _field(data, field)
    normals, areas = face_geometry(data)
    out = _like(field.values, data.topology.faces().num_faces)
    velocity, speed = units.number_and_unit(velocity)
    vx, vy, vz = (float(v) for v in velocity)
    if _on_cells(data, field):
        for_each(_cell_upwind, data, "faces", materialize(field.values), normals.values,
                 areas.values, vx, vy, vz, out)
    else:
        for_each(_upwind, data, "faces", traces(data, field), normals.values, areas.values,
                 vx, vy, vz, out)
    # (v . n) area u: a velocity given as a bare number leaves it unknown.
    area = units.derived((data.unit, data.topology.dimension - 1))
    return Field(Values(data, "faces", oriented=True), out,
                 units.named(units.derived(field.unit, speed, area)))

docs.text:
net_flux(data, flux)

Each cell's outward sum of flux, values on faces measured out of side 0 (Values(data, "faces", oriented=True), or plain face values taken so): a face's value counts plus for its side-0 cell and minus for its side-1 cell.

Given each face's integrated flux (upwind_flux, or a normal component times the area), it is the net outflow of each cell, V times the divergence; divergence divides by the cells' measure. Nothing is weighted: the values are summed as they are, so face area vectors sum to zero on a closed cell. Cells of a lower dimension than the mesh's have no faces: zero.

@on_inputs_device
def net_flux(data, flux):
    """Each cell's outward sum of ``flux``, values on faces measured out of side 0
    (``Values(data, "faces", oriented=True)``, or plain face values taken so): a
    face's value counts plus for its side-0 cell and minus for its side-1 cell.

    Given each face's integrated flux (``upwind_flux``, or a normal component times
    the area), it is the net outflow of each cell, ``V`` times the divergence;
    ``divergence`` divides by the cells' measure. Nothing is weighted: the
    values are summed as they are, so face area vectors sum to zero on a closed
    cell. Cells of a lower dimension than the mesh's have no faces: zero."""
    flux = _field(data, flux)
    if not _on_faces(data, flux):
        raise TypeError("net_flux sums a field on faces")
    data.topology.faces()                          # the incidence the cell views need
    out = _like(flux.values, data.num_cells)
    out.fill(0)
    # Cells of a lower dimension (a surface's triangles among tetrahedra) have
    # no faces of the mesh's, so no flux: zero. Nor has a mesh of vertices any.
    values = materialize(flux.values)
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == data.topology.dimension > 0:
            _outward_sums(data.domain_view("cells", group), values, out)
    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, flux.unit)

divergence(data, flux)

Each cell's finite-volume divergence of flux, the integrated flux through each face out of its side 0 (upwind_flux, or a normal component times the area): net_flux over the cell's measure (cell_geometry), so for a linear field it is the field's divergence. A cell of no measure gives no finite value, as perot and gradients give. flow_quantities gives the finite-element divergence instead, the trace of a field's gradient.

@on_inputs_device
def divergence(data, flux):
    """Each cell's finite-volume divergence of ``flux``, the integrated flux through
    each face out of its side 0 (``upwind_flux``, or a normal component times the
    area): ``net_flux`` over the cell's measure (``cell_geometry``), so for a
    linear field it is the field's divergence. A cell of no measure gives no
    finite value, as ``perot`` and ``gradients`` give. ``flow_quantities`` gives
    the finite-element divergence instead, the trace of a field's gradient."""
    net = net_flux(data, flux)
    measure = cell_geometry(data).measure
    out = _like(net.values, data.num_cells)
    if data.num_cells:
        _per_measure(net.values, measure.values, out)
    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, units.derived(net.unit, (measure.unit, -1)))

perot(data, flux)

A vector per cell from each face's normal component -- Perot's reconstruction, u_c = (1/V) sum_f A_f u_f (r_f - r_c), as C-grid models (MPAS, ICON) need to show their face-normal velocity at cells.

flux is a scalar field on faces, the component along each face's normal out of its side 0; the side each cell is on gives the sign. Face centers, areas and cell centroids and volumes are this module's, so a uniform field's normal components give it back exactly on cells with planar faces. First order, as Perot's method is. A cell of no volume gives NaN, and one of a lower dimension than the mesh's (no faces of it) zero.

@on_inputs_device
def perot(data, flux):
    """A vector per cell from each face's normal component -- Perot's reconstruction,
    ``u_c = (1/V) sum_f A_f u_f (r_f - r_c)``, as C-grid models (MPAS, ICON) need to
    show their face-normal velocity at cells.

    ``flux`` is a scalar field on faces, the component along each face's normal out
    of its side 0; the side each cell is on gives the sign. Face centers, areas
    and cell centroids and volumes are this module's, so a uniform field's normal
    components give it back exactly on cells with planar faces. First order, as
    Perot's method is. A cell of no volume gives NaN, and one of a lower dimension
    than the mesh's (no faces of it) zero."""
    flux = _field(data, flux)
    if not _on_faces(data, flux):
        raise TypeError("perot reconstructs from a field on faces")
    _, areas = face_geometry(data)
    centers = face_centers(data)
    volumes, centroids = cell_geometry(data)
    out = _vectors(data.num_cells, data.dtype)
    out.fill(0)                       # cells of a lower dimension, and vertices: no faces
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == data.topology.dimension > 0:
            _perot(data.domain_view("cells", group), materialize(flux.values), areas.values,
                   centers.values, centroids.values, volumes.values, out)
    # Areas times offsets over volumes cancel: the components' unit.
    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, flux.unit)

docs.text:
statistics(data, field, weights=None, level=None)

Descriptive statistics of a scalar field's values, as Viskores' Statistics filter gives them: a Statistics of n, min, max, sum, mean, the central moment sums m2, m3, m4, sample_variance (m2 / (n - 1)), population_variance (m2 / n), their standard deviations, skewness (sqrt(n) m3 / m2^1.5) and kurtosis (n m4 / m2^2, not the excess), the last two 0 for a constant field. Moments are taken about the mean, in a second pass. Ghosts are left out: cells and points data.ghosts marks a duplicate (another piece owns them) or hidden.

Over a PartitionedDataSet, field names a field every piece has: each piece's moments, over what it owns, are taken on its own device and combined pairwise, in the order of the pieces over every rank of data.world -- the same result however the pieces are shared out. Where every shared cell and point has one owner, the result is the whole's up to rounding. Over an AMRDataSet, the same over every box of every level: refined cells and points are left out, so each region of space counts once, at its finest level. Over an OctreeDataSet, its leaves (or the nodes of one level), every rank's.

weights weighs each value: "volume", each cell's measure (a cell field's), or a scalar field on the same entities, by name (a density, for mass-weighted moments). Then mean is sum(w x) / W, sum is sum(w x), the moments are sum(w (x - mean)^k), weight is W, the sum of the weights, the population variance m2 / W, the sample variance m2 / (W - sum(w^2) / W) (reliability weights, NumPy's aweights), and skewness and kurtosis take W for n. Cells of different sizes -- an AMR hierarchy's levels, an octree's leaves -- then count by their size.

@on_inputs_device
def statistics(data, field, weights=None, level=None):
    """Descriptive statistics of a scalar field's values, as Viskores' Statistics
    filter gives them: a ``Statistics`` of ``n``, ``min``, ``max``, ``sum``, ``mean``, the
    central moment sums ``m2``, ``m3``, ``m4``, ``sample_variance``
    (``m2 / (n - 1)``), ``population_variance`` (``m2 / n``), their standard
    deviations, ``skewness`` (``sqrt(n) m3 / m2^1.5``) and ``kurtosis``
    (``n m4 / m2^2``, not the excess), the last two 0 for a constant field.
    Moments are taken about the mean, in a second pass. Ghosts are left out:
    cells and points ``data.ghosts`` marks a duplicate (another piece owns
    them) or hidden.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, ``field`` names a field every piece has: each
    piece's moments, over what it owns, are taken on its own device and
    combined pairwise, in the order of the pieces over every rank of
    ``data.world`` -- the same result however the pieces are shared out. Where
    every shared cell and point has one owner, the result is the whole's up to
    rounding. Over an ``AMRDataSet``, the same over every box of every level:
    refined cells and points are left out, so each region of space counts
    once, at its finest level. Over an ``OctreeDataSet``, its leaves (or the
    nodes of one ``level``), every rank's.

    ``weights`` weighs each value: ``"volume"``, each cell's measure (a cell
    field's), or a scalar field on the same entities, by name (a density, for
    mass-weighted moments). Then ``mean`` is ``sum(w x) / W``, ``sum`` is ``sum(w
    x)``, the moments are ``sum(w (x - mean)^k)``, ``weight`` is ``W``, the sum of
    the weights, the population variance ``m2 / W``, the sample variance
    ``m2 / (W - sum(w^2) / W)`` (reliability weights, NumPy's ``aweights``), and
    skewness and kurtosis take ``W`` for ``n``. Cells of different sizes -- an
    AMR hierarchy's levels, an octree's leaves -- then count by their size."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet
    from tack.dataset.octree import OctreeDataSet

    if isinstance(data, OctreeDataSet):
        return data._statistics(field, weights, level)
    if level is not None:
        raise TypeError("level= picks an octree's level; this is not an OctreeDataSet")
    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        data = data._as_pieces()
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        fields_of(data, field, "statistics")
        from tack.dataset import units

        # Every rank's pieces' units, so a rank holding none agrees with the rest.
        every = [pair for part in data.world._allgather(
            [_units(piece, field, weights) for piece in data]) for pair in part]
        unit = units.common("statistics' pieces' field", [u for u, _ in every])
        weight_unit = units.common("statistics' pieces' weights", [w for _, w in every])
        moments = None
        for part in _over_pieces(data, lambda piece: _moments(piece, field, weights)):
            if part is not None:
                moments = part if moments is None else _merged(moments, part)
    else:
        unit, weight_unit = _units(data, field, weights)
        moments = _moments(data, field, weights)
    if moments is None:
        raise ValueError("statistics of no values")
    return _summary(*moments)._replace(unit=unit, weight_unit=weight_unit)

integrate(data, fields=None)

The measure of data -- its cells' total volume, area or length -- and the integral over it of each of fields (names; by default every field with a basis or on the cells), as VTK's vtkIntegrateAttributes gives them: Integrals(measure, measure_unit, values, units), values[name] a float or a tuple for a vector field.

Each cell is integrated by Gauss quadrature in its reference element through its own map (quadrature: collapsed onto simplices and wedges), with enough points for the field's order and the geometry's, so a curved geometry and a field of any order (H1, L2, point and cell data) integrate exactly, to rounding. Polyhedra, polygons and polylines take their measure from cell_geometry and integrate cell data and point data, which is linear on their pieces (sub-tetrahedra, triangles, segments), exactly. Only the cells of the mesh's dimension count, as in VTK: a volume's integrals leave out its surfaces, lines and vertices. Only owned cells count (ghost marks), and a PartitionedDataSet sums its pieces over every rank, in the pieces' order.

@on_inputs_device
def integrate(data, fields=None):
    """The measure of ``data`` -- its cells' total volume, area or length -- and the
    integral over it of each of ``fields`` (names; by default every field with a
    basis or on the cells), as VTK's ``vtkIntegrateAttributes`` gives them:
    ``Integrals(measure, measure_unit, values, units)``, ``values[name]`` a float or
    a tuple for a vector field.

    Each cell is integrated by Gauss quadrature in its reference element through
    its own map (``quadrature``: collapsed onto simplices and wedges), with enough
    points for the field's order and the geometry's, so a curved geometry and a
    field of any order (``H1``, ``L2``, point and cell data) integrate exactly, to
    rounding. Polyhedra, polygons and polylines take their measure from
    ``cell_geometry`` and integrate cell data and point data, which is linear on
    their pieces (sub-tetrahedra, triangles, segments), exactly. Only the cells of the mesh's dimension count, as in VTK: a volume's
    integrals leave out its surfaces, lines and vertices. Only owned cells count
    (ghost marks), and a ``PartitionedDataSet`` sums its pieces over every rank, in
    the pieces' order."""
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._common import _measure_unit
    from tack.dataset.partitioned import PartitionedDataSet

    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.statistics import _over_pieces

        pieces = list(data)
        names = _names(pieces[0], fields) if pieces else []
        parts = _over_pieces(data, lambda piece: _piece(piece, names))
        measure = math.fsum(m for m, _ in parts)
        values = {name: np.sum([v[name] for _, v in parts], axis=0) for name in names}
        first = pieces[0] if pieces else None
    else:
        names = _names(data, fields)
        measure, values = _piece(data, names)
        first = data
    out_units = {name: units.derived((first.fields[name].unit, 1),
                                     (_measure_unit(first), 1)) if first is not None else None
                 for name in names}
    return Integrals(measure=measure, measure_unit=_measure_unit(first) if first else None,
                     values={name: (float(v) if np.ndim(v) == 0 else tuple(map(float, v)))
                             for name, v in values.items()},
                     units=out_units)

The unit of the statistic name ("mean", "sum", ...), or None if unknown: min, max and mean are in the values' unit, sum in it times the weights', the moment sums m2 ... m4 in its powers times the weights', the variances in its square and the standard deviations in it (a difference of degrees Celsius is in kelvin), skewness, kurtosis and n pure numbers, weight in the weights' unit.

def unit_of(self, name):
    """The unit of the statistic ``name`` (``"mean"``, ``"sum"``, ...), or
    ``None`` if unknown: ``min``, ``max`` and ``mean`` are in the values'
    unit, ``sum`` in it times the weights', the moment sums ``m2`` ... ``m4``
    in its powers times the weights', the variances in its square and the
    standard deviations in it (a difference of degrees Celsius is in
    kelvin), ``skewness``, ``kurtosis`` and ``n`` pure numbers, ``weight``
    in the weights' unit."""
    from tack.dataset import units

    u, w = self.unit, self.weight_unit
    if name not in self._fields or name in ("unit", "weight_unit"):
        raise KeyError(f"no statistic {name!r}")
    if name in ("min", "max", "mean"):
        return u
    if name == "sum":
        return u if w == "dimensionless" else units.derived(u, w)
    if name in ("m2", "m3", "m4"):
        return units.derived((units.delta(u), int(name[1])), w)
    if name.endswith("variance"):
        return units.derived((units.delta(u), 2))
    if name.endswith("stddev"):
        return units.delta(u)
    if name == "weight":
        return w
    return "dimensionless"                   # n, skewness, kurtosis

    points left out; over an ``OctreeDataSet``, its leaves (or one ``level``'s
    nodes). With ``weights`` (``"volume"`` or a field, as ``statistics`` takes
    them) each bin's share is the weights' sum in it over theirs."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet
    from tack.dataset.octree import OctreeDataSet

    if isinstance(data, OctreeDataSet):
        return data._entropy(field, bins, weights, level)
    if level is not None:
        raise TypeError("level= picks an octree's level; this is not an OctreeDataSet")
    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        data = data._as_pieces()
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        fields_of(data, field, "entropy")
        extrema = [e for e in _over_pieces(data, lambda piece: _extrema(piece, field))
                   if e is not None]
        if not extrema:
            raise ValueError("entropy of no values")
        value_range = (float(np.min([e[0] for e in extrema])),
                       float(np.max([e[1] for e in extrema])))

        def counts(piece):
            if _extrema(piece, field) is None:
                return np.zeros(bins)
            return _counts(piece, field, bins, value_range, weights)
        p = sum(_over_pieces(data, counts))
    else:
        if _extrema(data, field) is None:
            raise ValueError("entropy of no values")
        # The histogram's own range, as before: it refuses one that is not finite.
        p = _counts(data, field, bins, None, weights)
    return _bits(p)

probe(data, where, fields=None, locator=None)

data's fields at the points of where -- a dataset, or an (n, 3) array of points, which becomes vertex cells -- as Viskores' Probe and VTK's vtkProbeFilter: the result is where with each field as point data, a field with a basis (H1, L2, Constant, values on points) evaluated through it in the cell holding the point, values on cells taken from that cell, and valid (1, or 0 where no cell holds the point and the values are 0). locator reuses a CellLocator of data. An integer field evaluated through a basis is rounded to the nearest integer, halves away from zero, as VTK's probe rounds; values on cells are copied.

data may be an AMRDataSet: each point goes to the finest level whose cell holds it (refined cells hold nothing), so a probe onto an image resamples the hierarchy, as VTK's vtkAMRResampleFilter does.

data may be an OctreeDataSet: each point takes the values of the leaf holding it (cell data, constant over the leaf), found by one binary search of the keys, as VTK's vtkHyperTreeGridProbeFilter does; a hidden leaf holds nothing. Over ranks, each point goes to the rank whose trees hold it and the values come back, as for a PartitionedDataSet.

data may be a PartitionedDataSet: each point goes to the piece one of whose own cells (not a ghost) holds it, the lowest such piece, which evaluates it there, and the values come back. where is then this rank's points -- a dataset, an array, or a PartitionedDataSet, which gives one back, each piece probed -- and every rank's points are probed over every rank's pieces of data.world. A point on a face two pieces share takes the lower piece's values, as one dataset takes its lower cell's.

Points given as an array are world positions; a dataset's are its own, relative to its origin. Either way they are taken relative to data's origin in double precision before they are located (the pieces of a PartitionedDataSet share one).

@on_inputs_device
def probe(data, where, fields=None, locator=None):
    """``data``'s fields at the points of ``where`` -- a dataset, or an ``(n, 3)``
    array of points, which becomes vertex cells -- as Viskores' Probe and VTK's
    vtkProbeFilter: the result is ``where`` with each field as point data, a
    field with a basis (``H1``, ``L2``, ``Constant``, values on points)
    evaluated through it in the cell holding the point, values on cells taken
    from that cell, and ``valid`` (1, or 0 where no cell holds the point and the
    values are 0). ``locator`` reuses a ``CellLocator`` of ``data``. An integer
    field evaluated through a basis is rounded to the nearest integer, halves away
    from zero, as VTK's probe rounds; values on cells are copied.

    ``data`` may be an ``AMRDataSet``: each point goes to the finest level whose
    cell holds it (refined cells hold nothing), so a probe onto an image
    resamples the hierarchy, as VTK's ``vtkAMRResampleFilter`` does.

    ``data`` may be an ``OctreeDataSet``: each point takes the values of the leaf
    holding it (cell data, constant over the leaf), found by one binary search
    of the keys, as VTK's ``vtkHyperTreeGridProbeFilter`` does; a hidden leaf
    holds nothing. Over ranks, each point goes to the rank whose trees hold it
    and the values come back, as for a ``PartitionedDataSet``.

    ``data`` may be a ``PartitionedDataSet``: each point goes to the piece one
    of whose own cells (not a ghost) holds it, the lowest such piece, which
    evaluates it there, and the values come back. ``where`` is then this
    rank's points -- a dataset, an array, or a ``PartitionedDataSet``, which
    gives one back, each piece probed -- and every rank's points are probed
    over every rank's pieces of ``data.world``. A point on a face two pieces
    share takes the lower piece's values, as one dataset takes its lower
    cell's.

    Points given as an array are world positions; a dataset's are its own,
    relative to its origin. Either way they are taken relative to ``data``'s
    origin in double precision before they are located (the pieces of a
    ``PartitionedDataSet`` share one)."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet
    from tack.dataset.octree import OctreeDataSet
    from tack.dataset.partitioned import PartitionedDataSet

    if isinstance(data, OctreeDataSet):
        if locator is not None:
            raise ValueError("probe of an OctreeDataSet searches its keys: it takes no "
                             "locator")
        return data._probe(where, fields)
    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        if locator is not None:
            raise ValueError("probe of an AMRDataSet uses each box's own locator")
        return _probe_pieces(data._as_pieces(), where, fields,
                             levels=[level for level, _ in data])
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        if locator is not None:
            raise ValueError("probe of a PartitionedDataSet uses each piece's own locator")
        return _probe_pieces(data, where, fields)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if locator is None:
        data = visible(data)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "probe with a locator")
    from tack.dataset.carry import _point_values, selected

    if not isinstance(where, DataSet):
        where = _vertices(relative_positions(where, data.origin, data.unit), data)
    if not isinstance(where.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("probe needs the probed points: an H1 geometry")
    units.check("probe's points and the dataset's spatial unit", where.unit, data.unit)
    locator = locator or cached_locator(data)
    if not locator.serves(data):
        raise ValueError("the locator was built for another topology or geometry, or "
                         "Tack has written the positions since: make a new one")
    points = arrays.materialize(_point_values(where.geometry.values, where.num_points))
    if where.origin != data.origin:
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._moving import _shifted_values

        points = _shifted_values(points, where.dtype,
                                 np.asarray(where.origin) - np.asarray(data.origin))
    found, pcs, tets = locator.find(points)
    m = found.shape[0]
    # Fields read by cell id where find searched from the points; built only
    # then, since it needs the cell bins.
    search = locator.__dict__.get("_mesh_search")
    grouped = []

    def by_cell():
        # The points grouped by the cell found, for the fields evaluated from
        # the cells (through each group's view), made once if any is.
        if not grouped:
            keys = tack.empty((m,), found.dtype)
            if m:
                _found_keys(found, data.num_cells, keys)
            # The extra cell: not found, never evaluated, so not filled.
            grouped.append(bucket_groups(keys, data.num_cells + 1,
                                         ids.at_least(data.id_dtype, m), skip=data.num_cells))
        return grouped[0]

    out = {}
    for name in selected(data, fields):
        f = _field(data, name)
        space = f.space
        if isinstance(space, Values) and space.on in ("points", "cells"):
            f = Field((H1 if space.on == "points" else Constant)(data), f.values, f.unit)
            space = f.space
        if not getattr(space, "interpolated", False) or space.on not in ("points", "cells"):
            continue
        width = arrays.width_of(f.values)
        dtype = arrays.dtype_of(f.values)
        # An interpolated integer field is evaluated in the geometry's float
        # type and rounded, as VTK's probe does; cell values are copied.
        rounds = not isinstance(space, Constant) and np.issubdtype(dtype.numpy_dtype,
                                                                   np.integer)
        evaluated = data.dtype if rounds else dtype
        values = (tack.empty((m,), tack.vec(width, evaluated)) if width
                  else tack.empty((m,), evaluated))
        by_id = field_by_id(data, f) if search is not None else None
        if m and by_id is not None:
            values.fill(0)
            # tets is read only in polyhedra; found stands in for it elsewhere.
            _values_from_points(search, by_id, found, pcs,
                                tets if tets is not None else found, values)
        elif m:
            values.fill(0)
            order, links = by_cell()
            for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [f]):
                if (group.count and locator.moved_cell_points is not None
                        and isinstance(space, H1)):
                    _evaluate_in_moved_tets(data.domain_view("cells", group), f.view(group),
                                            *locator.moved_cell_points, links, order, tets,
                                            pcs, values)
                elif group.count and locator.polyhedral:
                    _evaluate_in_tets(data.domain_view("cells", group), f.view(group), links,
                                      order, tets, pcs, values)
                elif group.count:
                    _evaluate(data.domain_view("cells", group), f.view(group), links, order,
                              pcs, values)
        if rounds:
            values = _to_integers(values, width, dtype, data.dtype)
        out[name] = Field(H1(where), values, f.unit)
    valid = tack.empty((m,), tack.i32)
    if m:
        _valid(found, valid)
    out["valid"] = Field(Values(where, "points"), valid)
    kept = dict(where.fields)
    kept.update(out)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(where, DataSet(where.topology, where.geometry, fields=kept,
                                     sets=dict(where.sets)))

voxelize(data, grid, fields=None, samples=4)

data on the voxels (cells) of grid, an image (uniform_grid): the image with fraction, the share of each voxel's volume the data covers, and each of fields' mean over that share (point and cell fields with a basis, all by default), as cell data -- what a simulation's fields are on a uniform grid for analysis or learning. A voxel the data does not reach is hidden (HIDDENCELL), its means 0.

Each voxel is sampled at samples points along each axis it spans (samples ** 3 in 3D, ** 2 on a 2D image), evenly, at the centres of its sub-voxels; a sample is inside where probe finds a cell holding it, and takes probe's value there. So fraction is right to about one sample's share, and a mean is the samples' mean, not an integral; more samples cost more probes. data is anything probe takes: a dataset, pieces over MPI ranks, an AMR hierarchy (its finest level at each sample) or an octree. The image keeps its fields; the result is on its device, at its origin and time. data's and grid's spatial units must agree.

def voxelize(data, grid, fields=None, samples=4):
    """``data`` on the voxels (cells) of ``grid``, an image (``uniform_grid``): the
    image with ``fraction``, the share of each voxel's volume the data covers, and
    each of ``fields``' mean over that share (point and cell fields with a basis,
    all by default), as cell data -- what a simulation's fields are on a uniform
    grid for analysis or learning. A voxel the data does not reach is hidden
    (``HIDDENCELL``), its means 0.

    Each voxel is sampled at ``samples`` points along each axis it spans
    (``samples ** 3`` in 3D, ``** 2`` on a 2D image), evenly, at the centres of
    its sub-voxels; a sample is inside where ``probe`` finds a cell holding it,
    and takes ``probe``'s value there. So ``fraction`` is right to about one
    sample's share, and a mean is the samples' mean, not an integral; more
    samples cost more probes. ``data`` is anything ``probe`` takes: a dataset,
    pieces over MPI ranks, an AMR hierarchy (its finest level at each sample)
    or an octree. The image keeps its fields; the result is on its device, at
    its origin and time. ``data``'s and ``grid``'s spatial units must agree."""
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._extract import _vertices
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.probe import probe
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import Ghosts, keep_marks
    from tack.dataset.topology import StructuredTopology

    coords = grid.geometry.values
    if not isinstance(coords, UniformCoordinates) or \
            not isinstance(grid.topology, StructuredTopology):
        raise TypeError("voxelize goes onto an image's voxels (uniform_grid)")
    k = int(samples)
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"samples is at least 1 a side, not {samples!r}")
    like = _like(data)
    units.check("voxelize's data and image spatial units", like.unit, grid.unit)
    cells = [max(d - 1, 1) for d in coords.dims]
    spans = [d > 1 for d in coords.dims]
    ks = [k if s else 1 for s in spans]
    halves = [0.5 if s else 0.0 for s in spans]
    per = int(np.prod(ks))
    n = grid.num_cells
    shift = np.asarray(grid.origin, np.float64) - np.asarray(like.origin, np.float64)
    device = grid.device
    with device:
        fraction = tack.empty((n,), like.dtype)
        hidden = tack.empty((n,), tack.u8)
        means = {}
        batch = max(1, _BATCH // per)
        for v0 in range(0, n, batch):
            nb = min(batch, n - v0)
            points = tack.empty((nb * per,), tack.vec3(like.dtype))
            _samples(coords, v0, cells[0], cells[1], ks[0], ks[1], ks[2], *halves, *shift,
                     per, points)
            probed = probe(data, _vertices(points, like), fields=fields)
            valid = probed.fields["valid"].values
            _fractions(valid, v0, per, fraction, hidden, nb)
            for name, field in probed.fields.items():
                if name == "valid" or name in grid.fields:
                    continue
                values = field.values
                if name not in means:
                    width = arrays.width_of(values)
                    dtype = arrays.dtype_of(values)
                    dtype = dtype if dtype.numpy_dtype.kind == "f" else like.dtype
                    means[name] = (tack.zeros((n,), tack.vec(width, dtype) if width else dtype),
                                   field.unit)
                _means(values, valid, v0, per, means[name][0], nb)
    out = dict(grid.fields)
    space = Values(grid, "cells")
    out["fraction"] = Field(space, fraction, "dimensionless")
    for name, (values, unit) in means.items():
        out[name] = Field(space, values, unit)
    result = keep_marks(grid, DataSet(grid.topology, grid.geometry, fields=out,
                                      sets=dict(grid.sets)))
    # Empty voxels hidden, beside whatever marks the image had; on its device.
    marks = hidden.numpy() * np.uint8(Ghosts.HIDDENCELL)
    if grid.ghosts is not None and grid.ghosts.cells is not None:
        marks |= grid.ghosts.cells.numpy()
    result.ghosts = Ghosts(cells=tack.array(marks.astype(np.uint8), device=device),
                           points=None if grid.ghosts is None else grid.ghosts.points)
    return result

Seeds moved through the velocity field (a 3-vector field or its name: point data, cell data, or a field of any order or L2, on a straight or curved geometry) by up to steps fixed steps of step_size, as Viskores' ParticleAdvection: a dataset of the particles where they stopped, one vertex cell each, with steps (taken), time and status (the bits SUCCESS, TERMINATE, SPATIAL_BOUNDS, TOOK_ANY_STEPS, ZERO_VELOCITY, SLOW_SPEED). seeds is an (n, 3) array or a field of 3-vectors; integrator "rk4", "euler" or "rk45" (adaptive steps, with tolerance, min_step and max_step: see streamlines); step_unit what step_size measures, "time" or "length" (an arc length along the path: see streamlines); max_length stops a particle whose path has gone that far, and terminal_speed (in the velocity's unit; vtkStreamTracer's) one where the velocity's speed is at or below it, before another step, the seed included (SLOW_SPEED); locator reuses a CellLocator of data. neighbors=True tries the face neighbours of the cell a particle was last found in before searching the locator's bins: the same particles, bit for bit, in about half the time on large meshes, for a table of six ids a cell kept with the locator (CellLocator.cell_neighbors).

seeds may also be what advect returned: the particles go on from where they stopped, with their times and the steps they took (steps counts those too), and a particle that stopped -- its steps done, at zero velocity, or outside -- stays as it is. A seed point field on it comes along.

Over a PartitionedDataSet (field by name), particles cross from piece to piece, in rounds: each goes to the lowest piece one of whose own cells (not a ghost) holds it, steps until it leaves that piece, and is handed on, until none is in flight on any rank.

Each particle is one thread that takes all its steps, so on a GPU a few seeds use a few threads of a device built for thousands, each slower than a CPU core: below a few thousand seeds a CPU copy of the mesh is faster (the Visualization Guide's "Integrate a steady velocity field").

@on_inputs_device
def advect(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator="rk4", locator=None,
           step_unit="time", tolerance=None, min_step=None, max_step=None, max_length=None,
           neighbors=False, terminal_speed=None):
    """Seeds moved through the velocity ``field`` (a 3-vector field or its name: point
    data, cell data, or a field of any order or ``L2``, on a straight or curved
    geometry) by up to ``steps`` fixed steps of ``step_size``, as
    Viskores' ParticleAdvection: a dataset of the particles where they stopped,
    one vertex cell each, with ``steps`` (taken), ``time`` and ``status`` (the
    bits ``SUCCESS``, ``TERMINATE``, ``SPATIAL_BOUNDS``, ``TOOK_ANY_STEPS``,
    ``ZERO_VELOCITY``, ``SLOW_SPEED``). ``seeds`` is an ``(n, 3)`` array or a field of
    3-vectors; ``integrator`` ``"rk4"``, ``"euler"`` or ``"rk45"`` (adaptive steps,
    with ``tolerance``, ``min_step`` and ``max_step``: see ``streamlines``);
    ``step_unit`` what ``step_size`` measures, ``"time"`` or ``"length"`` (an arc
    length along the path: see ``streamlines``);
    ``max_length`` stops a particle whose path has gone that far, and
    ``terminal_speed`` (in the velocity's unit; vtkStreamTracer's) one where the
    velocity's speed is at or below it, before another step, the seed included
    (``SLOW_SPEED``); ``locator`` reuses a ``CellLocator`` of ``data``.
    ``neighbors=True`` tries the face neighbours of the cell a particle was last
    found in before searching the locator's bins: the same particles, bit for
    bit, in about half the time on large meshes, for a table of six ids a cell
    kept with the locator (``CellLocator.cell_neighbors``).

    ``seeds`` may also be what ``advect`` returned: the particles go on from
    where they stopped, with their times and the steps they took (``steps``
    counts those too), and a particle that stopped -- its steps done, at zero
    velocity, or outside -- stays as it is. A ``seed`` point field on it comes
    along.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` (``field`` by name), particles cross from
    piece to piece, in rounds: each goes to the lowest piece one of whose own
    cells (not a ghost) holds it, steps until it leaves that piece, and is
    handed on, until none is in flight on any rank.

    Each particle is one thread that takes all its steps, so on a GPU a few
    seeds use a few threads of a device built for thousands, each slower than
    a CPU core: below a few thousand seeds a CPU copy of the mesh is faster
    (the Visualization Guide's "Integrate a steady velocity field")."""
    # A step as a time ("0.5 s") is in the spatial unit over the velocity's; as a
    # length ("1 mm"), in the spatial unit.
    if step_unit not in ("time", "length"):
        raise ValueError(f"step_unit is 'time' or 'length', not {step_unit!r}")
    step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step, max_length, terminal_speed = _parameters(
        data, field, step_unit, "advect", step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step, max_length,
        terminal_speed)
    adaptive = {"tolerance": tolerance, "min_step": min_step, "max_step": max_step,
                "max_length": max_length, "terminal_speed": terminal_speed}
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._particles import advect_pieces
        return advect_pieces(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator, step_unit,
                             neighbors, **adaptive)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if locator is None:
        data, field = visible(data, field)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "advect with a locator")
    seeds, resume, seed_ids = _resumed(seeds, data)
    xs, times, taken, status, _, _, _, _ = _run(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps,
                                                integrator, locator, record=False,
                                                resume=resume, unit=step_unit,
                                                neighbors=neighbors, **adaptive)
    out = _vertices(xs, data)                  # the particles stay on the device
    points = Values(out, "points")
    for name, values, unit in (("steps", taken, None), ("time", times, _time_unit(data, field)),
                               ("status", status, None)):
        out.fields[name] = Field(points, values, unit)
    if seed_ids is not None:
        out.fields["seed"] = Field(points, seed_ids.to_device(out.device))
    return out

The paths of advect's particles, as Viskores' Streamline: each seed's positions after every step, the seed first, as one polyline per seed (a PolylineTopology), with seed (which seed's path) on the cells and time on the points. A seed that takes no step has a point and no line. The arguments are advect's.

step_unit is what step_size measures (advect's too): "time" (the default, as Viskores steps), or "length", an arc length along the path: the particle follows the velocity's direction, as VTK's vtkStreamTracer does by default, so slow flow takes as long steps as fast, and steps * step_size is the longest path. time is the time the particle takes either way.

integrator="rk45" adapts the step, as VTK's vtkStreamTracer with its RK45 (Cash-Karp, vtkRungeKutta45): step_size is the first step, a step whose error estimate exceeds tolerance (a distance, in the spatial unit; 1e-6 by default) is tried again smaller, and each accepted step proposes the next, between min_step and max_step (by default a fiftieth of step_size and twice it, VTK's ratios), in step_unit. A step at min_step is taken whatever its error. max_length (any integrator) stops a path that has gone that far, its last step landing on it in the length unit; terminal_speed (in the velocity's unit, as vtkStreamTracer's) ends a path at its first point where the speed is at or below it, so a path stops where the flow does instead of wandering through near-still fluid.

Over a PartitionedDataSet (field by name), paths cross from piece to piece, each piece holding the stretches it traced.

@on_inputs_device
def streamlines(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator="rk4", locator=None,
                step_unit="time", tolerance=None, min_step=None, max_step=None,
                max_length=None, neighbors=False, terminal_speed=None):
    """The paths of ``advect``'s particles, as Viskores' Streamline: each seed's
    positions after every step, the seed first, as one polyline per seed
    (a ``PolylineTopology``), with ``seed`` (which seed's path) on the cells and
    ``time`` on the points. A seed that takes no step has a point and no line.
    The arguments are ``advect``'s.

    ``step_unit`` is what ``step_size`` measures (``advect``'s too): ``"time"``
    (the default, as Viskores steps), or ``"length"``, an arc length along the
    path: the particle follows the velocity's direction, as VTK's
    ``vtkStreamTracer`` does by default, so slow flow takes as long steps as
    fast, and ``steps * step_size`` is the longest path. ``time`` is the time
    the particle takes either way.

    ``integrator="rk45"`` adapts the step, as VTK's ``vtkStreamTracer`` with its
    RK45 (Cash-Karp, ``vtkRungeKutta45``): ``step_size`` is the first step, a
    step whose error estimate exceeds ``tolerance`` (a distance, in the spatial
    unit; 1e-6 by default) is tried again smaller, and each accepted step
    proposes the next, between ``min_step`` and ``max_step`` (by default a
    fiftieth of ``step_size`` and twice it, VTK's ratios), in ``step_unit``. A
    step at ``min_step`` is taken whatever its error. ``max_length`` (any
    integrator) stops a path that has gone that far, its last step landing on
    it in the length unit; ``terminal_speed`` (in the velocity's unit, as
    ``vtkStreamTracer``'s) ends a path at its first point where the speed is at
    or below it, so a path stops where the flow does instead of wandering
    through near-still fluid.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` (``field`` by name), paths cross from piece to
    piece, each piece holding the stretches it traced."""
    # A step as a time ("0.5 s") is in the spatial unit over the velocity's; as
    # a length ("1 mm"), in the spatial unit.
    if step_unit not in ("time", "length"):
        raise ValueError(f"step_unit is 'time' or 'length', not {step_unit!r}")
    step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step, max_length, terminal_speed = _parameters(
        data, field, step_unit, "streamlines", step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step,
        max_length, terminal_speed)
    adaptive = {"tolerance": tolerance, "min_step": min_step, "max_step": max_step,
                "max_length": max_length, "terminal_speed": terminal_speed}
    from tack.dataset.partitioned import PartitionedDataSet

    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._particles import streamlines_pieces
        return streamlines_pieces(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator, step_unit,
                                  neighbors, **adaptive)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if locator is None:
        data, field = visible(data, field)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "streamlines with a locator")
    from tack.dataset.polyhedra import PolylineTopology

    _, _, _, _, (trace, trace_times), lengths, capacity, _ = _run(
        data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator, locator, record=True, unit=step_unit,
        neighbors=neighbors, **adaptive)
    # Everything is chosen and numbered on the device; only counts come back.
    m = int(lengths.shape[0])
    idt = ids.for_output(data, m * capacity)
    starts = tack.empty((m,), idt)
    total = exclusive_scan(lengths, starts, m) if m else 0
    points = tack.empty((total,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
    point_times = tack.empty((total,), data.dtype)
    if m:
        _paths(trace, trace_times, lengths, starts, capacity, points, point_times)
    # The paths that moved, their points numbered as they are, make the chains.
    flags = tack.empty((m,), tack.i32)
    slots = tack.empty((m,), idt)
    if m:
        _moved(lengths, flags)
    lines = exclusive_scan(flags, slots, m) if m else 0
    kept = tack.empty((lines,), idt)
    seed_of = tack.empty((lines,), tack.i32)
    line_lengths = tack.empty((lines,), idt)
    if lines:
        _moved_paths(flags, slots, lengths, kept, seed_of, line_lengths)
    line_offsets = tack.empty((lines + 1,), idt)
    length = exclusive_scan(line_lengths, line_offsets, lines, close=True)
    line_points = tack.empty((length,), idt)
    if lines:
        _chains(kept, starts, lengths, line_offsets, line_points)
    topology = PolylineTopology(line_offsets, line_points, num_points=total, id_dtype=idt)
    out = DataSet(topology, points, **data._frame())
    out.fields["seed"] = Field(Values(out, "cells"), seed_of)
    out.fields["time"] = Field(Values(out, "points"), point_times, _time_unit(data, field))
    return out

@on_inputs_device
def extract_points(data, function, inside=True, fields=None):
    """The points inside ``function``'s region (at or below zero), or outside it
    (above), as vertex cells. Needs an ``H1`` geometry: one position per point.

    The point twin of ``extract_geometry``: the points as vertex cells, with point fields
    carried and cell fields left behind (a vertex cell has no cell of the input)."""

    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("extract_points needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    values = _point_values(implicit_values(data, function).values, data.num_points)
    # Outside is what is not inside: "above zero" as a range would need a bound
    # between zero and the smallest positive value, which f32 kernels (and GPUs
    # that flush denormals) do not keep.
    flags = _point_flags(data, values, -np.inf, 0.0)
    if not inside:
        _complement(flags)
    return _keep_points(data, flags, fields)

@on_inputs_device
def threshold_points(data, field, lower, upper, fields=None):
    """The points whose ``field`` (point data: ``H1``, values on points) lies in
    ``[lower, upper]``, as vertex cells.

    The point twin of ``threshold``: the points as vertex cells, with point fields
    carried and cell fields left behind (a vertex cell has no cell of the input)."""

A point with fewer than three neighbours, or whose neighbours lie on a line, gets a zero normal: so does one whose neighbourhood's two least spreads (variances) differ by less than 4 sqrt(eps) of the greatest, which the closed-form eigenvalues cannot tell from a line (in f32, a strip about 4% as wide as it is long).

@on_inputs_device
def point_normals(data, k=None, radius=None, viewpoint=None, direction=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
                  periodic=None, locator=None):
    """``data`` with ``normals``, each point's unit normal: the direction in which
    its neighbourhood -- its ``k`` nearest points, itself among
    them, or the points within ``radius`` -- spreads least, from the
    eigenvectors of their covariance, as VTK's vtkPCANormalEstimation and
    PDAL's ``filters.normal``. A point with fewer than three neighbours, or
    whose neighbours lie on a line, gets a zero normal: so does one whose
    neighbourhood's two least spreads (variances) differ by less than
    4 sqrt(eps) of the greatest, which the closed-form eigenvalues cannot tell
    from a line (in f32, a strip about 4% as wide as it is long).

    A normal's sign is chosen to point toward ``viewpoint`` (a world position)
    when one is given, else along ``direction`` (up, by default: the outside
    of terrain). ``periodic`` (a box) takes neighbours across its faces.
    ``locator`` reuses a ``PointLocator`` of ``data``."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "point_normals's radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "point_normals's periodic box")
    if (k is None) == (radius is None):
        raise ValueError("point_normals takes k or radius")
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("point_normals needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    locator = _locator(data, locator, periodic)
    n = data.num_points
    positions = locator.positions
    if k is not None:
        k = check_k(k)
        nearest, _ = locator.nearest(int(k), positions)      # itself included
        # Rows of k already: CSR offsets 0, k, 2k, ..., stored nowhere.
        offsets = CountingArray(n + 1, start=0, step=int(k), dtype=data.id_dtype)
        ids = nearest.reshape((n * k,))
    else:
        if not radius >= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"radius must be at least zero, not {radius!r}")
        offsets, ids = locator.neighbors(float(radius), positions)
    if viewpoint is not None:
        toward = np.asarray(viewpoint, np.float64) - np.asarray(data.origin)
        toward_point = 1
    else:
        toward = np.asarray(direction, np.float64)
        toward_point = 0
    normals = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
    if n:
        # Lines' gaps reach 1.22 sqrt(eps); see _smallest_axis.
        tolerance = 4.0 * float(np.sqrt(np.finfo(data.dtype.numpy_dtype).eps))
        _normals(locator.grid(), offsets, ids, *map(float, toward), toward_point, tolerance,
                 normals)
    out = DataSet(data.topology, data.geometry, fields=dict(data.fields),
                  sets=dict(data.sets), dtype=data.dtype, **data._frame())
    out.fields["normals"] = Field(H1(out), normals, "dimensionless")
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(data, out)

  • radius (radius and min_neighbors): fewer than min_neighbors other points within radius, as vtkRadiusOutlierRemoval; neighbors gives each point's count.
  • statistical (k and deviations): a mean distance to its k nearest other points more than deviations standard deviations above the mean of those means, as PCL; mean_distance gives each point's. vtkStatisticalOutlierRemoval also removes the points that many deviations below it (in dense spots, duplicates); the two agree on the mean distances. The mean and deviation are taken in double precision on the host.

The points are marked, not removed, as PDAL marks them (class 7): threshold_points(out, "outlier", 0, 0) keeps the rest. periodic (a box) measures across its faces. locator reuses a PointLocator of data.

Over a PartitionedDataSet of point clouds, each piece is searched with the copies of the other pieces' points it needs (ghost_points: within radius, or its points' k nearest), and the statistical test's mean and deviation are over every piece's points: each point gets the whole's answer. The pieces come back without the copies.

@on_inputs_device
def outliers(data, radius=None, min_neighbors=None, k=None, deviations=1.0, periodic=None,
             locator=None):
    """``data`` with each point marked an outlier or not: ``outlier``, a u8 point
    field, 1 for an outlier. Two tests, as VTK's two filters:

    - **radius** (``radius`` and ``min_neighbors``): fewer than ``min_neighbors``
      other points within ``radius``, as vtkRadiusOutlierRemoval; ``neighbors``
      gives each point's count.
    - **statistical** (``k`` and ``deviations``): a mean distance
      to its ``k`` nearest other points more than ``deviations`` standard
      deviations above the mean of those means, as PCL; ``mean_distance`` gives
      each point's. vtkStatisticalOutlierRemoval also removes the points that
      many deviations below it (in dense spots, duplicates); the two agree on
      the mean distances. The mean and deviation are taken in double precision
      on the host.

    The points are marked, not removed, as PDAL marks them (class 7):
    ``threshold_points(out, "outlier", 0, 0)`` keeps the rest. ``periodic`` (a
    box) measures across its faces. ``locator`` reuses a ``PointLocator`` of
    ``data``.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` of point clouds, each piece is searched with
    the copies of the other pieces' points it needs (``ghost_points``: within
    ``radius``, or its points' ``k`` nearest), and the statistical test's mean
    and deviation are over every piece's points: each point gets the whole's
    answer. The pieces come back without the copies."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "outliers's radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "outliers's periodic box")
    radial = radius is not None or min_neighbors is not None
    if radial == (k is not None):
        raise ValueError("outliers takes radius and min_neighbors, or k (and deviations)")
    if radial and (radius is None or min_neighbors is None or not radius >= 0):
        raise ValueError("the radius test takes a radius of at least zero and "
                         "min_neighbors")
    if not radial:
        k = check_k(k)
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        if locator is not None:
            raise ValueError("a PointLocator finds one piece's points; pieces take none")
        return _outliers_pieces(data, radius, min_neighbors, k, deviations, periodic)
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("outliers needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    locator = _locator(data, locator, periodic)
    n = data.num_points
    marks = tack.zeros((n,), tack.u8)
    out = DataSet(data.topology, data.geometry, fields=dict(data.fields),
                  sets=dict(data.sets), dtype=data.dtype, **data._frame())
    points = Values(out, "points")
    if radial:
        locator.check_radius(radius)
        counts = tack.empty((n,), data.id_dtype)
        if n:
            _count_within(locator.grid(), locator.positions, float(radius), 1, counts)
            _below(counts, int(min_neighbors), marks)
        out.fields["neighbors"] = Field(points, counts)
    else:
        means = _means(locator, n, int(k), data.dtype)
        if n:
            host = arrays.to_host(means).astype(np.float64)
            limit = host.mean() + float(deviations) * host.std()
            _above(means, float(limit), marks)
        out.fields["mean_distance"] = Field(points, means, data.unit)
    out.fields["outlier"] = Field(points, marks)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(data, out)

docs.text:
voxel_downsample(data, size, keep='centroid', fields=None)

One point per occupied voxel of a grid of size (a voxel's side, or three sides, in the geometry's units) anchored at the points' lower corner, as VTK's vtkVoxelGrid and PDAL's filters.voxeldownsize: vertex cells, with the input's origin.

keep chooses the point: "centroid", the mean of the voxel's points (new points: floating-point point fields averaged, integer ones -- a classification, intensities -- the voxel's first point's); "first", the voxel's lowest-numbered point; "nearest", its point nearest the centroid (the lowest-numbered on a tie). The last two keep input points, in input order, with their fields and ghost marks. Point fields come along (fields choosing, as filters do); cell fields do not. Each voxel is reduced in index order, so the result has the same bits from run to run, and the voxels and kept points are the same on every backend: the nearest point's distances are rounded alike everywhere (squared_length), so a tie falls the same way.

Over a PartitionedDataSet, the grid is anchored at the lower corner of every piece's points, and each voxel's owned points are brought to one block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then index, and reduced there. A voxel belongs to the piece of its first point, which keeps its centroid; "first" and "nearest" keep input points on their own pieces. Each piece of the result holds its share of the whole's points.

@on_inputs_device
def voxel_downsample(data, size, keep="centroid", fields=None):
    """One point per occupied voxel of a grid of ``size`` (a voxel's side, or three
    sides, in the geometry's units) anchored at the points' lower corner, as
    VTK's vtkVoxelGrid and PDAL's ``filters.voxeldownsize``: vertex cells, with
    the input's origin.

    ``keep`` chooses the point: ``"centroid"``, the mean of the voxel's points
    (new points: floating-point point fields averaged, integer ones -- a
    classification, intensities -- the voxel's first point's); ``"first"``,
    the voxel's lowest-numbered point; ``"nearest"``, its point nearest the
    centroid (the lowest-numbered on a tie). The last two keep input points,
    in input order, with their fields and ghost marks. Point fields come along
    (``fields`` choosing, as filters do); cell fields do not. Each voxel is
    reduced in index order, so the result has the same bits from run to run,
    and the voxels and kept points are the same on every backend: the
    nearest point's distances are rounded alike everywhere
    (``squared_length``), so a tie falls the same way.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, the grid is anchored at the lower corner of
    every piece's points, and each voxel's owned points are brought to one
    block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then index, and
    reduced there. A voxel belongs to the piece of its first point, which keeps
    its centroid; ``"first"`` and ``"nearest"`` keep input points on their own
    pieces. Each piece of the result holds its share of the whole's points."""
    size = _length(data, size, "voxel_downsample's size")
    if keep not in _KEEP:
        raise ValueError(f"keep is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _KEEP))}, not {keep!r}")
    sizes = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(size, np.float64), (3,)).astype(float)
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(sizes)) and np.all(sizes > 0)):
        raise ValueError(f"size is a positive voxel side, or three, not {size!r}")
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        return _downsample_pieces(data, size, sizes, keep, fields)
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("voxel_downsample needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    n = data.num_points
    positions = arrays.materialize(_point_values(data.geometry.values, n))
    if n:
        x = arrays.to_host(positions).reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.float64)
        low, high = x.min(axis=0), x.max(axis=0)
    else:
        low = high = np.zeros(3)
    counts = np.floor((high - low) / sizes).astype(np.int64) + 1
    if float(np.prod(counts.astype(float))) >= 2.0 ** 62:
        raise ValueError(f"{size!r} makes too many voxels over the points' box")
    keys = tack.empty((n,), tack.i64)
    if n:
        _voxel_keys(positions, *map(float, low), *map(float, sizes), int(counts[0]),
                    int(counts[1]), keys)
    order = argsort(keys)
    offsets, nruns = _run_offsets(gather(keys, order), n)
    if keep == "centroid":
        centroids = tack.empty((nruns,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
        if nruns:
            _run_means(positions, order, offsets, centroids)
        return _centroids(data, centroids, order, offsets, nruns, fields)
    flags = tack.zeros((n,), tack.i32)
    if nruns and keep == "first":
        _run_firsts(order, offsets, flags)
    elif nruns:
        centroids = tack.empty((nruns,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
        _run_means(positions, order, offsets, centroids)
        _run_nearest(positions, centroids, order, offsets, flags)
    return _keep_points(data, flags, fields)

deposit(
    data,
    grid,
    field=None,
    reduce=None,
    method="nearest",
    per_volume=False,
)

data's points deposited on grid, an image (uniform_grid, axis- aligned): a field on the image.

method="nearest" puts each point in the cell holding it (nearest grid point, Viskores' ParticleDensityNearestGridPoint): the field is on the cells. method="cic" spreads it over that cell's corners by trilinear weights (cloud in cell, Viskores' ParticleDensityCloudInCell, yt): the field is on the points. Points outside the image are left out.

Without field, each cell's (or corner's) count of points, or sum of weights. With one -- a point field of data or its name -- reduce takes "sum" (the default), "mean", "count", or, for "nearest", "min" and "max": a LiDAR surface model is the "max" of the heights on a 2D image, a terrain model the "min" of the ground's. A cell nothing reaches holds 0 for counts and sums, NaN for the rest. per_volume divides by a cell's volume (area, length on images of fewer axes): a number or mass density. Each target sums its entries in point order, so the result has the same bits from run to run. Counts, minima and maxima are the same on every backend; sums and means agree to rounding (a GPU may fuse a weight's multiply-add).

data and grid may have different origins: the points are moved to the image's by the difference, taken in double precision.

Over a PartitionedDataSet, each piece deposits its owned points (not the copies ghost_points adds) and the pieces' grids combine over every rank, in order of piece: sums and counts add, means divide the sums by the counts, minima and maxima take the least and the greatest. Every rank gets the whole grid's field, on grid's device; field is a name.

@on_inputs_device
def deposit(data, grid, field=None, reduce=None, method="nearest", per_volume=False):
    """``data``'s points deposited on ``grid``, an image (``uniform_grid``, axis-
    aligned): a field on the image.

    ``method="nearest"`` puts each point in the cell holding it (nearest grid
    point, Viskores' ParticleDensityNearestGridPoint): the field is on the
    cells. ``method="cic"`` spreads it over that cell's corners by trilinear
    weights (cloud in cell, Viskores' ParticleDensityCloudInCell, yt): the
    field is on the points. Points outside the image are left out.

    Without ``field``, each cell's (or corner's) count of points, or sum of
    weights. With one -- a point field of ``data`` or its name -- ``reduce``
    takes ``"sum"`` (the default), ``"mean"``, ``"count"``, or, for
    ``"nearest"``, ``"min"`` and ``"max"``: a LiDAR surface model is the
    ``"max"`` of the heights on a 2D image, a terrain model the ``"min"`` of the
    ground's. A cell nothing reaches holds 0 for counts and sums, NaN for the
    rest. ``per_volume`` divides by a cell's volume (area, length on images of
    fewer axes): a number or mass density. Each target sums its entries in
    point order, so the result has the same bits from run to run. Counts,
    minima and maxima are the same on every backend; sums and means agree to
    rounding (a GPU may fuse a weight's multiply-add).

    ``data`` and ``grid`` may have different origins: the points are moved to
    the image's by the difference, taken in double precision.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, each piece deposits its owned points (not
    the copies ``ghost_points`` adds) and the pieces' grids combine over every
    rank, in order of piece: sums and counts add, means divide the sums by the
    counts, minima and maxima take the least and the greatest. Every rank gets
    the whole grid's field, on ``grid``'s device; ``field`` is a name."""
    if method not in _METHOD:
        raise ValueError(f"method is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _METHOD))}, not {method!r}")
    reduce = reduce or ("sum" if field is not None else "count")
    if reduce not in _REDUCE:
        raise ValueError(f"reduce is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _REDUCE))}, not {reduce!r}")
    if field is None and reduce != "count":
        raise ValueError(f"reduce={reduce!r} needs a field to reduce")
    if method == "cic" and reduce in ("min", "max"):
        raise ValueError("cloud in cell weighs each point: it sums, counts or averages")
    coordinates = grid.geometry.values
    if not isinstance(coordinates, UniformCoordinates) or coordinates.ORIENTED == 1:
        raise TypeError("deposit goes onto an axis-aligned image (uniform_grid)")
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        return _deposit_pieces(data, grid, field, reduce, method, per_volume)
    unit = _unit(data, grid, field, reduce, per_volume)
    out, on = _deposited(data, grid, field, reduce, method, per_volume)
    return Field(Values(grid, on), out, unit)

@on_inputs_device
def sph_density(particles, kernel="cubic", smoothing_length="h", mass="mass", dimension=3,
                periodic=None, locator=None):
    """``particles`` with ``density``, each particle's SPH density ``rho_i = sum_j m_j
    W(|x_i - x_j|, h_i)`` -- itself included, from its own smoothing length (the
    gather form, as SPLASH computes it) -- for particles that come without one.
    The arguments are ``sph_interpolate``'s."""
    smoothing_length = _smoothing(particles, smoothing_length)
    mass, mass_unit = _given(particles, mass, "mass")
    periodic = _length(particles, periodic, "the periodic box")
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    w, support = _checked(kernel, dimension)
    if not isinstance(particles.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("sph_density needs the particles' positions: an H1 geometry")
    n = particles.num_points
    density = tack.zeros((n,), particles.dtype)
    if n:
        found = _locator(particles, locator, periodic)
        smoothing = _per_particle(particles, smoothing_length, "smoothing_length")
        found.check_radius(support * float(arrays.to_host(smoothing).max()))
        _densities(found.grid(), w, support, smoothing,
                   _per_particle(particles, mass, "mass"), density)
    out = DataSet(particles.topology, particles.geometry, fields=dict(particles.fields),
                  sets=dict(particles.sets), dtype=particles.dtype, **particles._frame())
    out.fields["density"] = Field(H1(out), density, units.derived(
        mass_unit, (particles.unit, -dimension)))
    return keep_marks(particles, out)

@on_inputs_device
def sph_interpolate(particles, target, fields=None, kernel="cubic", smoothing_length="h",
                    mass="mass", density="density", normalize=False, dimension=3,
                    periodic=None, locator=None):
    """``particles``' point fields at ``target``'s points by SPH kernel sums: ``A(x) =
    sum_j (m_j / rho_j) A_j W(|x - x_j|, h_j)``, each particle reaching to its
    kernel's support (2, 2.5 or 3 smoothing lengths), as VTK's
    vtkSPHInterpolator and SPLASH.

    ``target`` is a dataset -- an image to resample onto, a slice, a point cloud
    -- or an ``(n, 3)`` array of world positions, which becomes vertex cells;
    the result is ``target`` with each field (``fields`` chooses; all point
    fields but the smoothing length, mass and density by default) on its points,
    and ``shepard``, the sum of the particles' ``(m / rho) W`` there: where it
    is near 1 the particles cover the point, near 0 they do not. ``normalize``
    divides by it (VTK's ShepardProcessing), which makes a constant exact near
    the particles' edge.

    ``smoothing_length``, ``mass`` and ``density`` are the particles' point
    fields (names or ``Field``s) or numbers for all of them. ``kernel`` is
    ``"cubic"``, ``"quartic"``, ``"quintic"`` or ``"wendland"``, normalized in
    ``dimension`` dimensions. ``periodic`` (a box) reaches across its faces.
    ``locator`` reuses a ``PointLocator`` of the particles. The target's points are moved to the particles' origin by the
    difference of the two, in double precision."""
    smoothing_length = _smoothing(particles, smoothing_length)
    mass, mass_unit = _given(particles, mass, "mass")
    density, density_unit = _given(particles, density, "density")
    periodic = _length(particles, periodic, "the periodic box")
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._extract import _vertices
    from tack.dataset.dataset import relative_positions
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    w, support = _checked(kernel, dimension)
    if not isinstance(particles.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("sph_interpolate needs the particles' positions: an H1 geometry")
    if not isinstance(target, DataSet):
        target = _vertices(relative_positions(target, particles.origin, particles.unit), particles)
    if not isinstance(target.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("sph_interpolate needs the target's points: an H1 geometry")
    smoothing = _per_particle(particles, smoothing_length, "smoothing_length")
    reserved = {v for v in (smoothing_length, mass, density) if is_field_key(v)}
    names = [name for name in (fields if fields is not None else particles.fields)
             if name not in reserved or fields is not None]
    n = particles.num_points
    volumes = tack.empty((n,), particles.dtype)
    if n:
        _volumes(_per_particle(particles, mass, "mass"),
                 _per_particle(particles, density, "density"), volumes)
    units.check("sph_interpolate's target and particles' spatial unit", target.unit,
                particles.unit)
    # Each term is f times m/rho, a volume, times W, per volume: m / (rho L^d) is
    # a pure number for consistent units, unknown where the mass or density is a
    # number.
    weight_unit = units.derived(mass_unit, (density_unit, -1), (particles.unit, -dimension))
    locator = _locator(particles, locator, periodic)
    m = target.num_points
    queries = arrays.materialize(_point_values(target.geometry.values, m))
    if target.origin != particles.origin:
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._moving import _shifted_values

        queries = _shifted_values(queries, target.dtype,
                                  np.asarray(target.origin) - np.asarray(particles.origin))
    if queries.dtype != particles.geometry.values.dtype:
        queries = queries.astype(tack.vec(3, particles.dtype))
    reach = support * (float(arrays.to_host(smoothing).max()) if n else 0.0)
    locator.check_radius(reach)
    out = DataSet(target.topology, target.geometry, fields=dict(target.fields),
                  sets=dict(target.sets), dtype=target.dtype, **target._frame())
    shepard = tack.zeros((m,), particles.dtype)
    grid = locator.grid()
    for name in names:
        field = particles.fields[name]
        on_points = (isinstance(field.space, H1) and field.space.order == 1) or (
            isinstance(field.space, Values) and field.space.on == "points")
        if not on_points:
            continue
        values = arrays.materialize(_point_values(field.values, n))
        scalar = getattr(values.dtype, "scalar_dtype", values.dtype)
        if scalar.numpy_dtype.kind != "f":
            continue                            # an integer field has no kernel average
        result = tack.zeros((m,), values.dtype)
        if n and m:
            _interpolated(grid, w, support, reach, queries, smoothing, volumes, values,
                          result, shepard)
            if normalize:
                _normalized(result, shepard)
        same = normalize or weight_unit == "dimensionless"
        out.fields[name] = Field(H1(out), result, field.unit if same else
                                 units.derived(field.unit, weight_unit))
    if not names and n and m:                      # no fields: the Shepard sum alone
        _interpolated(grid, w, support, reach, queries, smoothing, volumes, volumes,
                      tack.zeros((m,), particles.dtype), shepard)
    out.fields["shepard"] = Field(H1(out), shepard, weight_unit)
    return keep_marks(target, out)

    region="point_region",
    mass=1.0,
    velocity=None,
    center="mbp",
    softening=0.0,
    G=1.0,
    periodic=None,

The halos of particles -- the groups of region, a point field of halo labels (connected_components' point_region: friends-of- friends with radius the linking length; -1 for no halo) -- as a point cloud of one point per halo, ported from Viskores' cosmotools and ParaView's LANL halo finder. Each halo's fields:

  • halo, its label; count; mass, the sum of its particles' (mass a point field or one number for all, as Viskores takes it);
  • com, its centre of mass;
  • mbp, its most bound particle (the index of the particle of least potential -G sum m_j / sqrt(r^2 + softening^2) over the halo), and potential, that least potential;
  • with velocity (a 3-vector point field): velocity, the mass- weighted mean, and dispersion, the one-dimensional velocity dispersion sqrt(sum m |v - mean|^2 / 3M);
  • radius, the farthest particle from the halo's point.

The point is the MBP's position (center="mbp") or the centre of mass ("com"). In a periodic box (a side, three, or corners, as PointLocator takes it) each halo is unwrapped about its first particle before anything is summed, so a halo across a face is whole, and its points are put back in the box. Positions are relative to the particles' origin, which the catalogue shares. Every sum runs in particle order, so the result has the same bits from run to run; counts and masses are the same on every backend, the other sums agree to rounding (a GPU may fuse a multiply-add), and so the most bound particle can differ between backends only where two potentials tie to rounding.

Over a PartitionedDataSet (labels numbered across the pieces, as connected_components numbers them), each halo's owned particles are brought to one block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then index, and catalogued there: a PartitionedDataSet of catalogues, the halos in order of label across them, each mbp an index in the piece mbp_piece (a global piece id).
